This week, he won reelection with approximately 83.7%, according to unofficial returns. He represents Ohio's 21st House District: Beachwood, Euclid, Lyndhurst, South Euclid, University Heights, and part of Cleveland, including Collinwood. He is also a Jewish American and a member of the Ohio Jewish Caucus. Before we even get into the election conversation, he wanted to give Collinwood some appreciation. People hear Beachwood and make assumptions about his district, but the communities he represents cover a wide range of incomes and experiences. Then we got into the question facing Democrats across Ohio: You 've won. What are you going to do with it? What Were Voters Telling Us? Matt: Do you think this was a mandate for Democratic policies, or a rejection of Trump and the Republican Party? What did voters tell you? Eric: We have to go by data and outcomes. Trump won in 2024. Independents and Republicans felt he should get a second term, and he won. We're not a party of election deniers. I personally believe his second term has been the worst presidency in modern times, if not the history of our country. His second presidency was different from his first from day one, in the way he tried to fundamentally change our country. Look at DOGE, the major changes to the federal government, tariffs, and the big budget bill. There are consequences that have already come down and consequences that will continue next year, particularly around healthcare and SNAP. I think voters realized how bad Trump is and how few members of his party stood up to him. This result was a year in the making. Matt: You saw this coming before this election? Eric: I knew this was going to be a good year for Democrats on election night in 2025. We saw Democrats winning school board, city council, township trustee, and village council races in suburban areas that had historically been Republican. We were all surprised by what happened this week, but the basis for it was already there. We still don't know everything about where the electorate is politically. Are they more Republican or more Democratic? We know they don't like Trump and this current Republican Party. What Changes When Republicans Can't Override the Governor? Matt: Republicans still control the legislature, but they can no longer override a Democratic governor's veto on their own. What does that mean? Eric: Before, they could override it. That hasn't happened constantly. In the almost two years I've been there, it happened once, on the property-tax legislation. But the threat was always there. The more important part, in my opinion, is that in a two-party system, if you're being objective, fair, and reasonable, you should want that pendulum to keep swinging back and forth. Think about the Ohio Supreme Court. We should want a court that's closely divided, where sometimes Republicans have the majority and sometimes Democrats do. When it's overwhelmingly one-sided, people going before the court feel like they already know which way their case is going to go. That's not fair. The same principle applies to the legislature. One party being in power for decades isn't healthy. Even if Democrats were the ones in power for 20 years, I would say the same thing. So yes, we're in a much healthier place as a democracy now than we were last week. But we still have to see what comes out of it. I hope we'll see that healthier balance reflected in the legislation that gets passed. What Can You Deliver in the First 100 Days? Matt: People on my Facebook page are asking about funding schools, the voucher program, healthcare, and SNAP. What can you realistically deliver in the first 100 days? Eric: We need more time. Give us 200 days. Matt: Okay, we'll give you 200 days. First negotiation done. haha Eric: I say that because the state operating budget is our most important document. It prioritizes everything for the following two-year cycle, and it has to pass by June 30. That's when we'll really know how the funding priorities have changed. Have we gone back to the Fair School Funding Plan? Do we have a fairer tax system? Our income-tax system is skewed to favor wealthier Ohioans. We should return to a progressive income-tax structure. Matt: The argument for tax cuts is that people keep more money and spend it. Does the state recover some of that through sales taxes? Eric: Without the numbers in front of me, I can't say. But the state is in a solid financial position. We get monthly and annual reports, and typically the state brings in more than its projections. We also have the rainy-day fund. The point is, we can afford the Fair School Funding Plan. Returning to a more progressive income-tax structure is one part of that. What Happens to Families Using Vouchers? Matt: A lot of families have been using vouchers for several years. They've made decisions about where their children go to school. Would you advocate eliminating the program? What happens to those families? Eric: I don't believe in radical change, one way or the other. First, we're still dealing with a Republican-controlled legislature. But even if we could do it, even if Democrats won all 99 House seats, I would say: Let's make changes or phase it out over years. Don't just totally cut it. There are reforms that I believe even advocates for the voucher program would concede on. Matt: But now you have Amy Acton, and she has line-item veto power. Republicans will have to negotiate. Doesn't that create the possibility for substantial changes? Eric: My concern is more on the Fair School Funding side, on the public-school side, than totally cutting vouchers. I wouldn't anticipate ending the voucher program overnight. We need to increase the state's support for public schools. There are different ways to start changing vouchers, too. We have a bill pending that would prevent families making more than $500,000 a year from receiving them. Currently, even at that income, families can still receive money. And remember, public districts still have responsibilities for students attending private schools, including transportation. We're subsidizing these schools while public schools continue carrying those obligations. Do We Still Want Fair Maps After Winning? Matt: Democrats just gained seats under these maps. Why mess with a good thing? Would you still support changing them? Eric: Yes. I support a constitutional amendment and an independent commission so this is actually done fairly. I personally heard Amy Acton say several times on the campaign trail that supporting another redistricting effort would be a priority. I want it on the ballot in 2027. Matt: Could that produce new districts for 2028? Eric: I don't believe it would get done in time for new districts in 2028. Whether it could happen before the next census cycle depends on how the amendment is written. I don't know what that language will look like yet. Matt: Republicans will point to Democratic states and say gerrymandering goes both ways. Eric: And it does. But just because another state does it the wrong way doesn't mean we should do it to balance things out. An independent commission should draw the lines. You're also never going to have 99 competitive House districts. Some communities are overwhelmingly Democratic, and others are overwhelmingly Republican. But even after a very good election for Democrats, there is still work to be done. What Should Ohio's Democrats Do in Washington? Matt: Ohio is sending more Democrats to Congress. What do you want them to do to help Ohio and help you do your job? Eric: Look at the Problem Solvers Caucus, which includes Republicans and Democrats. There are commonsense policy ideas and solutions that should be implemented but haven't been because Washington is so partisan. Let's find things we can actually get done. Look at how many of those proposals became law in previous Congresses, and let's improve on that. There's also appropriations. We support applications from cities, nonprofit groups, and other organizations seeking federal money. That's one way we work together. But the biggest issue is affordability. Matt: What does addressing affordability look like to you? Eric: I tend to look more at incomes than just expenses. Prices have gone up, especially over the last several years. Gas, groceries, construction materials. But if you're making a million dollars a year, you can absorb that. The fundamental issue is income inequality and the gap between the average worker and the people at the top. For lower-income and middle-class families, life has become too hard. This is not sustainable. Is the answer the minimum wage? More relief for people at the lower end? Something has to give. The biggest thing I want from Congress is to reverse the changes in the big budget bill: healthcare, SNAP, the coverage changes, and the additional paperwork people will have to deal with. That would be my most important message to Ohio's congressional Democrats. Where Is the Line Between Criticism and Antisemitism? | | ---|---|--- Matt: You recently strongly criticized a "friend's" post saying "Fuck Israel." Tell about how that crossed the line. Eric: This was a high school and college friend. I saw it and thought: This is beyond the pale. This is not acceptable. People don't always realize how that language comes across to Jewish people. Our religion, identity, history, and trauma are connected to Israel. To me, that statement goes beyond criticizing the government. Matt: Then how should people criticize what is happening in Israel and Gaza? How do you have that conversation without making our Jewish neighbors feel attacked? Eric: Name the individuals. Criticize the current Israeli government. It's like having a conversation about Trump and American politics without being anti-American. There's a way to do it. I'm not defending everything Israel has done in its history or modern history. I think continued settlement expansion in the West Bank is unconscionable. Some of the things Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir, and Smotrich have done are abhorrent. I don't believe those actions represent what Israel or Jewish values should be. Matt: On the other side, do you also see a rise in Islamophobia? Eric: One hundred percent. It's undeniable, and it's wrong. Period. I also want to see Muslim public figures condemn extremists acting in their religion's name. I have no problem criticizing people on my side, and I want to see that willingness from others. Those are separate issues. Islamophobia should be condemned, and public figures should also be willing to condemn bad actors within their own communities. How Do Voters Hold You Accountable? Matt: Democrats have the opportunity now. We've talked about school funding, the budget, and redistricting. How should people hold you accountable if those promises aren't fulfilled? Eric: We're back before voters in two years, and statewide officials are back in four. That's the accountability. We spend all this time talking about where the electorate is and what's popular. Every two and four years, we actually find out. If the Fair School Funding Plan doesn't get reimplemented, that's not good. We won't have the same support from teachers that we had this time. Matt: So voters get to judge whether you did the job, and you have to answer for it at the next election. Eric: Yes. Democrats have more power, a budget negotiation ahead, and promises people will remember. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by supporting Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: Not now, not ever.
body:
A governor just told pro-life states their laws don't count

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)
Dear Pro-Life Friend,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:
_“I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.**Not now, not ever.** ”_
The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count.

**That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do.** They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.”

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life:

_“I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?”_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**“It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.”**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm) _Roe v. Wade_ had been called “settled law” for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

[So please make your most generous tax-deductible contribution right now](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**:**
**> >> $25** puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop.
**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits.
**> >> $100** launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials.
**> >> $250** helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out.
**> >> $500** helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event.
Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind.
Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do.

Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her.

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, _Students for Life_

P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. We’re preparing a legal brief to stand with them, and I need your help to finish this fight. [Please give $500, $250, $100, $50, or $25 right away](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**.**
[GIVE NOW >>](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)

## Democratic Socialist Wins L.A. Mayor Race
Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman [unseated Mayor Karen Bass](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQheGnwR0Rg228Lii2cZdtt7TGMAR2wUQwSpS3v_J9hVv_0ied8_e-3zHldD7-YCHLoe4nvXsmZmp7wHylgu0_cT9qOTg2Qu67VtpIAKnMjo7Ti3YYvA1EmsaBLCzruJppUfMQLS0EiIsxi5q9AXCzCXQY7ZT26nDzkOzFASgDMMI03g4_rwE8_dLeTCo4MSnyiWu7_avp5Eghf-qL2s3VMmQbmZ9djL-F3oTeOFJMOV9N6C3WQtciobfOyCTfyC4KvRmY1hkWeSaOH5QNC54y1y7xfFCmLgt-ahN6G5r1z3fKOXWziEk9CqZvfeCf_fWy-isAAP__6aiAHA) after one term, and Bass conceded Thursday morning with Raman holding a lead of about 3 points. Raman, 45, is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, making her the city's first socialist mayor. Her win means democratic socialists will now run New York City, Washington, D.C., and Los Angeles. Bass never recovered from criticism of her performance during the January 2025 Palisades fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes while she was in Ghana for a presidential inauguration. Raman hammered Bass on homelessness and housing costs, and the mayor countered that her challenger was "[not ready for primetime](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuu2zAQRVdDdTT4kaingkUadS9tSmFEjqzJ48cgBxa8-8DeQuoDXJx7_nxv30CJyv03ZPR81K3g1RMyY9sOSG-Uof0g973mnc-GwH0zyjiptVRug8D0xE0P0R-IBu2AXs-LXdw4q2k4PUQ7RQMBlTMhzHZe9mkCu0eYnAvz10D-Pae1clpbPdrbHqfl0BG_THSjOoIYFUbi2m5_KxU-8Uiv-sR2CzUPyZ_Mjy7sL2FWYdbrum5lD-8bby7M-qiJmEIXZv14Y8LAVIswayE-XyAbZCgy1S6h3DFhlxletcmLioyYa2jAFGSvgSBRZ_kDDYvcoXfZQgGnrJ2Xofn4uCgl6m4Wo7pnoPRx5P8r-_TmXwAAAP__NBeQdQ)." Raman, a former urban planner born in India, had endorsed Bass before launching a late bid in February. She takes over a city preparing to host the 2028 Summer Olympics.

subject: Urgent Senate Update: A New Day
body:
| | | [Click here to open this e-mail in its own browser window](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet//view_newsletter_setup.aspx?link=SenVanHollen%2501317810%2501November%2b2026%2bPost-Election%2bNewsletter%250115441.63853593.8383214.7517223%2501dpwillis67%2540gmail.com%2501Friend%2501dpwillis67%2540gmail.com%2501Silver%2bSpring%252c%2bMD%2b20906%2501Friend%2501) | [Click here to open a plain text version of this email](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet//view_newsletter_setup.aspx?plain_text=Y&link=SenVanHollen%2501317810%2501November%2b2026%2bPost-Election%2bNewsletter%250115441.63853593.8383214.7517223%2501dpwillis67%2540gmail.com%2501Friend%2501dpwillis67%2540gmail.com%2501Silver%2bSpring%252c%2bMD%2b20906%2501Friend%2501)

| | | **November 6, 2026** |
---|---|---|---
| | |
### Urgent Senate Update: A New Day
This week, Marylanders and Americans across the country made their voices heard loud and clear. They've rejected the politics of cruelty and of corruption, and everything that has brought us: an economy that is crushing American families and a government that's lost its moral compass and forgotten who it answers to.

The billionaires who tried to buy this election failed, because no amount of money can hide from the American people the damage that has been done. They felt it for themselves in the checkout line, at the gas pump, and in their healthcare bills. They saw it on the streets of Minneapolis and in communities across the country where children were snatched on their way home from school. They saw it in the atrocities carried out around the world in their name.

The American people said enough is enough. They are now demanding a new kind of politics: a politics for the people. So now it's our turn. Voters are giving Democrats a chance, and it's on us to earn their trust.

We must earn it by taking on the powerful and corrupt interests, by ending finger-in-the-wind politics, and by delivering real results for the American people. That means a kitchen-table agenda that puts more money in the pockets of American workers and lowers the costs that are crushing American families. It means rooting out the rampant corruption and lawlessness of this Administration. It means ending the war in Iran. And it means replacing cruelty with decency and a moral compass at home and around the world.

As we begin this work, we cannot afford to get pulled into the superficial debates that too often consume Washington. This was not an election about right versus left. It was an election about right versus wrong. It was not an election about moderates or progressives. It was an election about whether our government works just for those at the very top, or answers to We the People.

We must also refuse to accept a false choice about whether this election was about the economy or our democracy. We do not have to pick one or the other. Voters have made clear that they understand this is one fight. We cannot fix what's broken in our economy without confronting what's broken in our democracy, and we cannot expect our democracy to endure without fixing what's broken in our economy.

I'm proud to continue the fight for the promise of an economy and a democracy that answer to us all.

This victory belongs not to any part of the party, but to all of you and to the American people everywhere who kept their faith in our country through the darkest days of the last two years. You refused to be silenced. You stood up for our Constitution, for our democracy, for our better angels, and for each other, even when Washington did not. This victory is yours.

Thank you for reminding us of who we are as a country and what is possible when Americans set their minds to it. Thank you for leading us to this point. Now it's up to all of us to deliver.

As always, I'll keep working to deliver for communities across Maryland and make sure your voices continue to be heard in Washington.
Onwards, Chris Van Hollen

To see more on my daily efforts in Congress, follow me on: [YouTube](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2f%40senatorvanhollen&redir_log=49030338036296), [Bluesky](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov&redir_log=939838092693319), [Instagram](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fchrisvanhollen%3futm_source%3dig_web_button_share_sheet%26igsh%3dZDNlZDc0MzIxNw%253D%253D&redir_log=547268099313732), [Threads](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.threads.com%2f%40chrisvanhollen&redir_log=958032566321279), [Facebook](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2fchrisvanhollen%2f&redir_log=328155479639284), and [X](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15441.63853593.8383214.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen&redir_log=218313979356198).

name: Wes Moore
subject: This week’s results
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2276%2E1086043%2EdiZZgW)
Peter,
This week’s elections prove that we’re ready for a different kind of politics in this country.
We need to address the issues that are facing the American people right now, work to make their life easier, and give people pathways to work, wages, and wealth.
And let’s be clear why we’re here: We have had a Congress who were cheerleaders instead of leaders.
The reason this week’s election results were a resounding rejection of the federal administration and their allies in Congress was both because of their reckless policies _and_ because we have had a Congress that cheered Donald Trump on while he made life harder for the American people.
The American people have spoken and they want accountability _and_ change. **It’s now up to all of us to deliver.** Let’s get to work.
Elevate,
Wes

Dear Patriot, This letter couldn't wait. That's why Kirk Cameron personally asked me to write you on the post-production budget shortfall for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk." He wanted to make sure you heard about this urgent situation as soon as possible. **And after you hear what's going on, I hope you'll support BRAVE FOR GOOD.** **[We are facing a serious budget shortfall of $48,523.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA_m3hSSZOIP6qWbckwXleYwVqwH7o6u9s0KbU-KQ5idRPazW46weDjGJbK8XxuA7kE8siVnaApBArPF-4htD484VzRsRBh7RcoVYMh144w)** But before I go into more detail, let me tell you a little about our mission to help parents instill wholesome and Godly values in America's children. Kirk just wrapped up this year's "See You at the Library Day," where we countered the Left and brought conservative values straight to America's children. Kirk is busy spearheading the "Bible Revival" movement that gets Biblical values -- that America was founded upon -- back into schools. And Kirk just finished filming Season 3 of our television show "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" that teaches children how to respond to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith. **I'm writing you with such urgency because Season 3 of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is in jeopardy.** **[And if I can't raise $48,523 in the next four weeks, "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" will be delayed -- or even postponed indefinitely.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA_m3hSSaw4P84HhIuxBIOrCrTG4naQBr2HbXzmc3Henv4KN6_EIeqODSFwMNMeFivML90DwqpYEpfH5CExrFoLXPqf_ZISpKOqOWUqZLDQ)** The radical Leftists who attack us because we're reaching America's children with God's Truth would love nothing more than to see "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" shut down. They hate that "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" has skyrocketed to the top of Angel Studios' streaming service. They hate that we've created a path around the addictive mind rot they put on TV. It's like Kirk always says... It's not enough to complain about culture raising our children. We must create something better for them. The first 2 seasons of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" have reached millions of children and counting, but Season 3 is in jeopardy. If "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" isn't funded, there will be no voice on TV countering the Left's dangerous lies. Lies like Drag Queens leading a Pride Parade SingAlong on Blue's Clues... Same-sex weddings on Arthur...And Sesame Street using YOUR tax dollars to normalize same-sex parents and men in dresses. And that's just what's on TV. Not to mention the thousands of 'Queer Kid' videos on platforms like YouTube Kids. The days of The Andy Griffith Show and Father Knows Best are gone. The Left has purposely used TV to create a generation of zombie children who are glued to their screens. "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is the antidote to that Leftist TV brainwashing. It uses low-stimulation production and teaches children how to respond to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith. Like when Mr. Kirk teaches Iggy:
---
* to love how God created him as an iguana, even when the villainous Culture the Vulture says Iggy must become a human to fit in.
* to rely on the wisdom of parents -- one mom and one dad -- to solve life's problems.
* to be BRAVE by speaking truth in the face of the Left's lies.

---
| | | **[BRAVE FOR GOOD needs to raise $48,523 in the next 4 weeks just for "Iggy and Mr. Kirk."](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNTIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAAA_m3hSSbbxvBjF__J2pZWhmvwLrmsAS6XNp2YJF4QgNXOXwq0WGP5d1Mts4NvWnDfSv3dpZXrqm0nWovEK2F9lFLR7Ix6cbQBFc5Ijkjeg)** That doesn't even begin to account for our "Bible Revival" efforts and the conservative Story Hours for the rest of the year. Fellow Patriot, please help. Because this is so urgent, I wanted to reach out to Americans who share our concern for the next generation. On behalf of myself, Kirk, and our entire team, thank you for considering supporting BRAVE FOR GOOD. Together, we will rebuild a culture that honors God and His will for our lives.
---
Sincerely, Dr. Trent TalbotFounder, BRAVE for Good

I never thought I would be locked in what is shaping up to be one of the closest Senate races in modern history. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ)
---
Hey, Derek, it's Scott. I was born and raised in Mississippi. Growing up here, I never thought I would be locked in what is shaping up to be one of the closest Senate races in modern history. [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.wz-auy&refcode=em_20261106_10250_fr&amount=20&t=6&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ) Getting here wasn’t easy. But over the last fourteen months my campaign has traveled all across the state, speaking with every last voter we could find. [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.wz-auy&refcode=em_20261106_10250_fr&amount=20&t=7&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ) We even spent some time talking to voters outside Trump’s Mississippi rally last month – _because that’s how you win in a state like this._ [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.wz-auy&refcode=em_20261106_10250_fr&amount=20&t=8&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ) Along the way we’ve been funded by grassroots donations of $5, $10, even $50 at a time. And it means the world to me to know that so many people have my back. But this race isn’t over yet. We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line. Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. This is going to be one of the most closely divided U.S. Senate races in modern American history. [**So please. If you can afford to make a split donation of $20 to the DNC and my campaign’s legal fund to help us stand up for voting rights in Mississippi and beyond, I hope you’ll donate today.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.wz-auy&refcode=em_20261106_10250_fr&amount=20&t=9&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ) _If you've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your split contribution between Scott Colom and the Democratic National Committee instantly:_ | | | **[Donate $20](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.3l7g7N&amount=20&refcode=em_20261106_10250_fr&t=28&akid=10250%2E22930333%2E9holgQ)**

I remember the last time we saw a major market crash - it was 2008. The subprime housing lending bubble burst. Bear Stearns and Lehman Brothers went bust. The federal government had to step in with a $700 billion bailout. The S&P 500 went down 37.5% that year - if you took it from its peak in 2007 to its trough in 2009 the S&P 500, which represents the biggest blue-chip companies in the world, went down 57%. The Great Recession kicked off and lasted 18 months as unemployment shot up to double-digits.
At the time, I was 33 years old (wow!). I was like, "Okay, how does this market collapse affect me and my little education company?" Major banks were closing and layoffs were widespread. I called my company's bank - Signature Bank, which would fail 15 years later - and was reassured that our account was fine. I didn't have enough personally in savings or investment at that point to be meaningfully impacted by the crash; my little nest egg went down but it wasn't that big a deal. It was one of the bright sides of being cash poor; most of my net worth was tied up in my little company. Meanwhile, unemployed 23-year-olds were washing ashore at our company's classrooms, which specialized in preparing people to head to business school. We had to rent extra classrooms and schedule more classes because so many young workers were losing their jobs on Wall Street and were seeking shelter.
"Huh," I thought. "It's weird that while the world is falling apart, my little company is doing better than ever." We had banner years in 2008 and 2009 - it turned out that our services were somewhat more in demand in tough times than in good times. Our revenue shot up to the point where we got acquired in 2009.
The 2008 crash was the result of excessive financial chicanery - banks sliced and diced subprime loans to the point where people thought they were high-quality because the ratings agencies were asleep at the switch. Also playing a huge role - low lending standards for housing buyers who should not have been given a zero-cash down mortgage. The acronym at the time was NINJA - No Income, No Job, No Assets mortgages. Yes, that was a thing. They gave mortgages to anyone with a pulse, many of whom couldn't afford them when they reset.
That crash shook me up. You mean we had this stock market bubble because our financial institutions were morons? The growth and prosperity were illusory? And then the Feds had to bail out the banks and the bankers with taxpayer - our - money? The anger formed the Tea Party faction of the Republican Party in 2009 and then Occupy Wall Street in 2011. In my view, the anger never really ran its course, and fueled both Bernie Sanders' should-have-been-successful insurgent campaign of 2016 and Trump's "drain the swamp" rise that year.
There have been market setbacks since then with COVID and interest rates, but in my mind there hasn't been a real market crash since 2008. I feel fortunate that I lived through that one. I also lived through the crash of 2000, when the Nasdaq went from 5000 to 2000 as the Internet bubble burst. My tiny dot-com company at that time was winked out of existence, and I turned to tutoring and throwing parties to make some money in the aftermath as a 26-year old with six figures in school debt.
Now, I'm 51 years old with a family. The market started flashing crazy red signals last week; Intel lost 29% of its stock market value in a day and numerous tech stocks were in the red as they reported being cash flow negative to fund AI infrastructure. Then, just yesterday, tech stocks declined sharply. Investors are trying to figure out who is going to pay $3 trillion for the AI buildout and how. I, personally, have long been [dubious](https://substack.com/redirect/48b2078e-a234-4185-9b5e-e14cb3de7e41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I've believed that two things could be true at the same time: AI is a game-changing technology AND the market has gotten way ahead of itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/97ac7d78-778c-402d-95f4-d967dd29caad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Think about the Internet circa 2000 - it did indeed change the way we live, shop and work. Amazon did eventually become a trillion-dollar company. But there was a bubble, it popped, and Pets.com, Global Crossing and dozens of other public companies were washed away as the Nasdaq shed 60% of its value. I literally attended liquidation events for dot-com companies that I'd attended launch parties for just months earlier as a hanger-on looking for free food.
AI is in the process of changing the way we think, work and love - for better or worse - and will shred [millions](https://substack.com/redirect/b39290b3-edcb-40e3-b031-025580b43ea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of jobs. Also, these valuations and investments don't make any sense. You can't conjure up another $80 billion in revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI when companies and individuals can accomplish most tasks with cheaper open-weight models that are fine for 85% of use cases at a tiny fraction of the costs. How much are you personally spending on AI? How much is your company spending or willing to spend? Indeed, it's crystal clear that Anthropic and OpenAI's compounded growth rates are already slowing. A lot of the money that is being spent right now will never be paid back. Billions of dollars are being squandered.
One clue as to what was happening was in January 2025, when DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company, announced it could achieve comparable results to ChatGPT at a small fraction of the cost. Nvidia lost 17% immediately and the tech sector shed $590 billion in value over fears that the infrastructure buildout costs were excessive. DeepSeek was banned in many U.S. agencies due to privacy concerns. But the fear that open-weight models could do a lot of lower-order work for pennies on the dollar never actually got addressed.
I've got a newsflash for everyone but . . . most work is lower-order work.
When I was raising money for Noble Mobile, multiple investors said to me, "Andrew, if you start something with AI in the name, I'll cut you a seven-figure check right now. But I can't invest in a feel-good consumer play." Perhaps because I'm somewhat contrarian, this made me feel better about what we were doing . . . and also that numerous AI companies were going to be funded that were never going to make it. By the way, [Noble Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/66702206-2e32-4d2f-9c2b-c83de8fdee6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is up to eight figures in annual revenue and growing and isn't going anywhere unless people decide they can do without a cellphone. I wanted to start something that would save the average consumer money and improve their outlook and mental health; I have the feeling that we'll only do better in tough times. History is repeating itself.
Much of the growth is once again illusory. Get ready for cascading loss of value at a scale that has not been seen in eighteen years. Dozens of billion-dollar companies are about to go up in smoke. The folly of some of our most exalted figures will be on full display, but hey - most of them made money on the way up.
TL;DR - When a bubble bursts, it's merciless and you don't want to be anywhere near it. Act accordingly.

I didn't have enough personally in savings or investment at that point to be meaningfully impacted by the crash; my little nest egg went down but it wasn't that big a deal. It was one of the bright sides of being cash poor; most of my net worth was tied up in my little company. Meanwhile, unemployed 23-year-olds were washing ashore at our company's classrooms, which specialized in preparing people to head to business school. We had to rent extra classrooms and schedule more classes because so many young workers were losing their jobs on Wall Street and were seeking shelter. "Huh," I thought. "It's weird that while the world is falling apart, my little company is doing better than ever." We had banner years in 2008 and 2009 - it turned out that our services were somewhat more in demand in tough times than in good times. Our revenue shot up to the point where we got acquired in 2009. The 2008 crash was the result of excessive financial chicanery - banks sliced and diced subprime loans to the point where people thought they were high-quality because the ratings agencies were asleep at the switch. Also playing a huge role - low lending standards for housing buyers who should not have been given a zero-cash down mortgage. The acronym at the time was NINJA - No Income, No Job, No Assets mortgages. Yes, that was a thing. They gave mortgages to anyone with a pulse, many of whom couldn't afford them when they reset. That crash shook me up. You mean we had this stock market bubble because our financial institutions were morons? The growth and prosperity were illusory? And then the Feds had to bail out the banks and the bankers with taxpayer - our - money? The anger formed the Tea Party faction of the Republican Party in 2009 and then Occupy Wall Street in 2011. In my view, the anger never really ran its course, and fueled both Bernie Sanders' should-have-been-successful insurgent campaign of 2016 and Trump's "drain the swamp" rise that year. There have been market setbacks since then with COVID and interest rates, but in my mind there hasn't been a real market crash since 2008. I feel fortunate that I lived through that one. I also lived through the crash of 2000, when the Nasdaq went from 5000 to 2000 as the Internet bubble burst. My tiny dot-com company at that time was winked out of existence, and I turned to tutoring and throwing parties to make some money in the aftermath as a 26-year old with six figures in school debt. Now, I'm 51 years old with a family. The market started flashing crazy red signals last week; Intel lost 29% of its stock market value in a day and numerous tech stocks were in the red as they reported being cash flow negative to fund AI infrastructure. Then, just yesterday, tech stocks declined sharply. Investors are trying to figure out who is going to pay $3 trillion for the AI buildout and how. I, personally, have long been . I've believed that two things could be true at the same time: AI is a game-changing technology AND the market has gotten way ahead of itself. | | ---|---|--- Think about the Internet circa 2000 - it did indeed change the way we live, shop and work. Amazon did eventually become a trillion-dollar company. But there was a bubble, it popped, and Pets.com, Global Crossing and dozens of other public companies were washed away as the Nasdaq shed 60% of its value. I literally attended liquidation events for dot-com companies that I'd attended launch parties for just months earlier as a hanger-on looking for free food. AI is in the process of changing the way we think, work and love - for better or worse - and will shred of jobs. Also, these valuations and investments don't make any sense. You can't conjure up another $80 billion in revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI when companies and individuals can accomplish most tasks with cheaper open-weight models that are fine for 85% of use cases at a tiny fraction of the costs. How much are you personally spending on AI? How much is your company spending or willing to spend? Indeed, it's crystal clear that Anthropic and OpenAI's compounded growth rates are already slowing. A lot of the money that is being spent right now will never be paid back. Billions of dollars are being squandered. One clue as to what was happening was in January 2025, when DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company, announced it could achieve comparable results to ChatGPT at a small fraction of the cost. Nvidia lost 17% immediately and the tech sector shed $590 billion in value over fears that the infrastructure buildout costs were excessive. DeepSeek was banned in many U.S. agencies due to privacy concerns. But the fear that open-weight models could do a lot of lower-order work for pennies on the dollar never actually got addressed. I've got a newsflash for everyone but . . . most work is lower-order work. When I was raising money for Noble Mobile, multiple investors said to me, "Andrew, if you start something with AI in the name, I'll cut you a seven-figure check right now. But I can't invest in a feel-good consumer play." Perhaps because I'm somewhat contrarian, this made me feel better about what we were doing . . . and also that numerous AI companies were going to be funded that were never going to make it. By the way, is up to eight figures in annual revenue and growing and isn't going anywhere unless people decide they can do without a cellphone. I wanted to start something that would save the average consumer money and improve their outlook and mental health; I have the feeling that we'll only do better in tough times. History is repeating itself. Much of the growth is once again illusory. Get ready for cascading loss of value at a scale that has not been seen in eighteen years. Dozens of billion-dollar companies are about to go up in smoke. The folly of some of our most exalted figures will be on full display, but hey - most of them made money on the way up. TL;DR - When a bubble bursts, it's merciless and you don't want to be anywhere near it. Act accordingly. For 6 months off your mobile bill with Noble Mobile, click or email and use my name to switch or explore. It will save you money and time - hundreds of dollars for the average American. Look up. | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Andrew Yang 111 Sutter Street, 7th Floor, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

_Formerly All On The Line_

**Peter, I hope you woke up feeling proud this morning — with a new sense of hope for the future of American democracy.**
Leading up to Tuesday’s elections, our movement had to stare down a national, concerted effort to prevent the American people from making their voices heard at the ballot box.
Power-hungry politicians tried to cling to power at any cost — attempting to cheat their way into unearned victories through blatant gerrymandering and voter suppression.
But with people like you fueling the fight, we held strong.
We organized against gerrymanders. We mobilized against voter suppression. We trained networks of volunteers to spread timely voter information far and wide in critical states — helping fuel incredibly strong midterm turnout.
And we proved that when we all show up, speak up, and refuse to be intimidated, we are unstoppable. **The midterm elections represented a watershed moment in our fight to protect democracy.**
**The will of the people came through in resounding numbers that can’t be ignored: flipping not only control of Congress but also the most state legislative chambers in decades. State after state, voters picked their politicians instead of the other way around. **
We’re still unpacking all the results. It honestly feels like we’re drinking from a firehose of good news—overwhelming in the best possible way.
Here are two under-the-radar victories you should savor right now:
1. The people of Missouri voted to repeal the state’s gerrymander,
2. Maryland voters approved a ballot measure that lets the state weigh in on how maps are drawn amid the national redistricting crisis.

**We’ll have more to say in the days and weeks ahead about the pro-democracy wins that you helped make possible.**
_But we know one thing for certain: the fight isn’t over. More attacks on democracy are brewing, even in just the weeks ahead._
Texas lawmakers might double down on last year’s extreme gerrymander — by trying to redraw their map again before the current governor leaves office.
And some anti-democracy lawmakers have already staked their claim on trying to skew the census, because denying a fair count is one of their best plays to deny fair maps.
**But this movement just showed that when we fight back for democracy, we can win. We can’t stop now.**
[**Your ongoing support**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142987621/658735749/-1680110036?refcode=don_aotl_tier1_email_NowWhat_email_20261106-AOTL-Tier1-NowWhat_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20261106-AOTL-Tier1-NowWhat_&utm_campaign=NowWhat&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAzMmRlNmZjLWUxZDktZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=uL7QtwyavmeRZWQ_wyEx5naAITihynrdCF4KqbGbyns=) can help ensure we’re ready to mobilize voters in the next few weeks, when we see attempts to weaponize lame-duck sessions for further map manipulation. You can help power the fight to defend the census from political interference. And you can help protect the principle of free and fair elections.
**The next victories are formed in moments like this, when we choose not to rest on our laurels — but to continue the fight. And now we know what we’re truly capable of when we come together. **
Thank you for all the ways you’ve protected our democracy,
KT Coleman
Deputy Campaigns Director

## SpaceX Eyes Data Center
SpaceX [said](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJykkb2unDAQRp8GOiP_rQ0FRRq6mzYlmjseFisGI3t2yd6nj8jmDW49miOd8_36mD8gprjff8JGI8PXMu901kTMVOZ6ANKfAAxIO1N55cd-p8rnrKV2Qikh3QzI8UmzhTaMxuHgbUuj8oMZvDSub9dRmht83j4X3yuSvfcQpENLvSY3LMqaNo4XTynplJFO-g5vvUbj_XLDQWlLjZUUIufS8UpQ4lfeYUmv_KTSYd7aNK7MR23Mj0ZPjZ7O8-x-PzNcx0ZPl1KjJ8y4xkqYHzu_Gj299cSaK1dR8hleYiPiuN9F3sVR8pErBfH_TWAWVwrxbiEQtuNxYaFwxESzgSGQxEF4S72wi3UCpCQhewM9LgFkMN3KW2rLGI4zphSr842V9w1i-ufB353gOeq_AQAA__8b452d) at a community meeting that it is behind a proposed 747-acre data center campus in rural Cochise County that could create thousands of construction jobs. Meet judge
#3 on the Oligarchy’s bench: Amos Mazzant.

From his seat on the federal bench in Texas, Mazzant has used his power to
do two things: protect big business and make life harder for working
people.

First, he took overtime pay away from millions of workers.

For decades, inflation quietly shrank the number of salaried workers who
qualified for overtime. In 2016, the Department of Labor worked to fix
that, so more workers would get time-and-a-half for hours over 40 a week.

Mazzant blocked it, claiming the Labor Department had “exceeded its
authority.” About 4.2 million workers lost their shot at overtime pay.

Then, he shielded corporations from scrutiny.

Congress passed the Corporate Transparency Act to fight money laundering,
fraud, and tax evasion by requiring companies to disclose who really owns
them. Judge Mazzant froze it nationwide.

That opened the door for the Trump administration to let American
companies skip reporting their owners entirely. Anonymous shell companies
are back, and with them, a playground for tax dodgers and financial

name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: where is the moral outcry?
body:
And blue-state governors are protecting the abortionists who do it.

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)
Dear Pro-Life Friend,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:
_“I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.**Not now, not ever.** ”_
The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count.

**That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do.** They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.”

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life:

_“I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?”_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**“It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.”**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.
[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb) _Roe v. Wade_ had been called “settled law” for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

[So please make your most generous tax-deductible contribution right now](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)**:**
**> >> $25** puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop.
**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits.
**> >> $100** launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials.
**> >> $250** helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out.
**> >> $500** helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event.
Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind.
Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do.

Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her.

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, _Students for Life_

P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. We’re preparing a legal brief to stand with them, and I need your help to finish this fight. [Please give $500, $250, $100, $50, or $25 right away](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)**.**
[GIVE NOW >>](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)

name: NEGOP
subject: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair...
---
| Thank you to everyone who mailed, texted, or shared slate cards; who found locations and delivered signs; and who door-knocked, phone-called, and wrote personal notes. Thank you as well to our poll watchers and observers. Nebraska's Republican candidates would not have succeeded without you.
Your work paid off in important ways. Nationally, Nebraska is recognized as a state that pushed back the Democrats' blue wave. We are viewed as a bright spot. A special thank-you is owed once again to the Third Congressional District. As I said at the Vice President JD Vance rally, the First and Second Districts are our front lines, but we rely on the Third District as our rear guard--to stop any of the nonsense that gets past the eastern part of the state. The Third District did not disappoint. Voter loyalty to the Party and good Nebraska common sense prevailed.
We re-elected all of our congressional incumbents. Congressman Mike Flood's race was closer than any of us watching were comfortable with, and the rural counties of the First District made the difference. Thank you. Many of our neighboring states, and the country as a whole, fared far worse.
Second District congressional candidate Brinker Harding was unsuccessful. Given the environment, I don't know of anyone who could have won with an "R" beside their name. Brinker and his team ran a strong campaign, but it was not enough. All of our constitutional state officers won re-election, and our new nominee for Secretary of State, Scott Petersen, won handily. The margins were not as strong as we normally see for statewide offices, but again the Third District carried us through. The brightest spot in our state elections was the State Board of Education. We now hold a 5-3 majority. Congratulations to Elizabeth Tegtmeier, Angie Eberspacher, Sherry Jones, and Lou Ann Goding for stepping up to run or re-run and enduring the attacks from the left. A special thank-you goes to SBOE member Kirk Penner for his help in these races. Lou Ann Goding is one of the few Republicans who narrowly won in Douglas County; she will be an excellent addition to the board. Like SBOE member Lisa Schonhoff, she is data-driven and no-nonsense.
Our University of Nebraska Board of Regents races were won by liberal candidates. We had an outstanding candidate in Dr. Jeremy Hosein, but he was outspent, and the urban areas of Lancaster County preferred the "Independent" Democrat consultant Brent Comstock.
We appear to have lost three seats in the Unicameral, though some races remain very close and provisional ballots are still being counted. Overall it could have been much worse. We elected and re-elected some very strong conservatives, and I am grateful to each of them. Taylor Royal and Senator Brad von Gillern narrowly lost races they would have served well in. Rebecca Rens, Chris Anderson, and Tobias Howard put up valiant efforts in what proved to be a nearly impossible year for new candidates in urban areas, no matter how hard they worked.
Douglas and Lancaster County Republicans did not fare well. Both counties lost their races for County Attorney and Sheriff. Our eastern urban districts will now bear the consequences of those decisions--growing homeless encampments, lower arrest rates, lighter sentencing requests, and little to no cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. I hope that I am wrong, but fear that I am not. Once again, thank you. Each of you knows the work you put into this election. I am humbled to serve alongside you.
I promise to wake up every day continuing to safeguard our values and to prepare us for the 2028 election. There is no surrender. Our values - love of God, family, state and nation - are too precious to do any less. God is good. He will see us through this time and be the protection we need over our state and our nation.
God bless Nebraska and God bless America.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: .3% .3% | ~~ | | Peter, Out of more than 213,000 votes counted in Alaska, Mary Peltola’s lead is just 637. That's three-tenths of one percent — the closest Senate race in America, per the New York Times, with roughly a quarter of the expected vote still to come. And think about what those 637 votes are carrying: the fifth and final win of the most historic cycle Indigenous Americans have ever seen, and a stronger Democratic Senate majority with Mary Peltola in it. The first four are already in the win column — Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan. Governor-elect Deb Haaland. Congresswoman Sharice Davids. Congresswoman-elect Claire Valdez. One seat stands between this movement and a perfect five for five. ~ Now, the two things happening at once in Alaska: The count rolls on in batches until as late as November 18, with the ranked-choice tabulation after that. Slow is normal — it's how Alaska makes sure ballots from its most remote communities arrive and count. The courtroom is where Trump lives now. A federal judge threw out the DOJ's lawsuit to block certification — and the DOJ appealed the same day. With Mary's lead at 637 votes and their ballot dispute involving several times that many, this is exactly the knife-edge outcome that lawsuit was built for. They're not walking away from it. name: David Hogg
subject: A truly historic night 🌊
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Across the country. Up and down the ballot.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261106-1&t=1&akid=4235%2E587540%2Ed_BTpa)
Peter, I’m still reveling in our successes from Election Day. And I hope you are too!
Across the country, up and down the ballot, people made it clear that they will not tolerate the unconstitutional actions, tactics, and corruption of the Trump administration. But even more importantly, they made clear the kind of elected officials they want representing them: young, bold, unapologetically progressive leaders who will fight for them, not corporations or the billionaire class.
**Young voters turned out in record breaking numbers and played a major role in creating this historic blue tsunami.**
Our Leaders We Deserve endorsed candidates flipped 12 seats in our Red-to-Blue federal and state races. In state legislatures, our candidates won 27 seats, broke 2 Republican supermajorities, and flipped 7 state legislature chambers blue (INCLUDING THE TEXAS HOUSE!!). And at the federal level, our candidates won 8 seats, playing an integral role in flipping the House and Senate.
Across the country, our elected candidates made history with “firsts,” including Abdul El-Sayed, who became the first Muslim American to be elected to the Senate.
**This was by far our biggest election cycle yet at Leaders We Deserve — but we’re only just getting started.**
We saw strong blue shifts _everywhere_ , including deep red states that so many wrote off. But none of those shifts came easy. We’ve been investing heavily and recruiting young candidates in states like Texas and North Carolina for years, all building towards this moment. And now in 2028, we have _so many_ opportunities to build young, progressive power at the federal and state levels.
For right now, we should take some time to celebrate our hard work. This record-breaking cycle would not have been possible without you, Peter.
Thank you,
David Hogg
P.S. We can’t stop for too long — otherwise we’ll lose our footing in 2028. _And we can’t afford to have that happen_. Now is our chance to set the stage for success in the Presidential cycle. **[If you’re able, can you chip in $5 to make sure we don’t lose momentum as we gear up for the 2028 cycle?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261106_1_recap.Hu7wso&refcode=em20261106-4235&amount=5&t=2&akid=4235%2E587540%2Ed_BTpa)**

Two years later, on January 3, 2019, four of its candidates were sworn

His company endorsed every one of them on the 2018 ballot and handed
them a television platform to campaign on. Help me find out exactly
how that happened.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

Two years from a founding document to four seats in the Congress of
the United States. That is not an accident. THAT IS A PIPELINE, AND
SOMEBODY BUILT IT ON PURPOSE. Help me take it apart in a court of law.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

And the nephew he hired now reaches millions of young men every single
day.

On September 10, I sued Hasan Piker personally for more than $150
MILLION in Palm Beach County, Florida, for telling that audience that
someone was going to come around and take action against Americans for
what they believe. Help me fund that case and the next one.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

GIVE $25, $50 OR $100 — FUND THE CASE AGAINST THE MACHINE →
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

And look at the names on the indictment our Citizens’ Grand Jury
returned in Charleston on September 5. Nine jurors, voting
UNANIMOUSLY, on seven felony counts: Hasan Piker, Zohran Mamdani,
Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, Abdul El-Sayed and Barack Hussein Obama.

Two of those names were put into Congress by the organization Cenk
Uygur helped found. A third is the nephew he hired. That is not a
coincidence. IT IS AN ORG CHART. Help me put it in front of a jury.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

My name is Larry Klayman. I founded Judicial Watch in 1994 and Freedom
Watch after it. I am a former federal prosecutor. I exposed Filegate
and Chinagate under the Clinton administration, I beat the Obama NSA
in federal court and shut down its illegal bulk-surveillance dragnet,
and I AM THE ONLY LAWYER IN AMERICAN HISTORY WHO OBTAINED A COURT
RULING THAT A SITTING PRESIDENT HAD COMMITTED A CRIME.

Forty years of this work has taught me one thing above all others. You
do not stop a movement by suing the loudest person in it. You stop it
by finding out who writes the checks, who books the platform, and who
decided this was the message. THAT IS WHAT DISCOVERY IS FOR.

So The Young Turks are next, and I want to be plain with you about
why. Not because Cenk Uygur has opinions I dislike. He is entitled to
every opinion he has, and so are you, and so am I.

He is next because in my judgment this company has spent a decade
building the distribution network that carries this poison into the
minds of young Americans, and because a man does not get to construct
the machine, hire the operator, and then stand back and say the
machine has nothing to do with him. I intend to prove exactly that in
a court of law.

Let them sue me for saying it. They will not, and their lawyers will
tell them precisely why. A libel case would put Cenk Uygur in a
deposition chair, under oath, answering questions about his funding,
his bookings, his editorial decisions and his hiring. No media company
in America hands a lawyer like me that opening. I AM COUNTING ON IT.

Here is why the courtroom is the only room that works. A broadcaster
controls his own show completely. He can cut a segment, delete an
archive, decline an interview and put out a statement written by a
lawyer. He has never once in his life had to finish a sentence he did
not want to finish.

HE CANNOT DO ANY OF THAT UNDER OATH. In a deposition he answers what
he is asked or he takes the consequences of refusing. Subpoenas reach
corporate records. Discovery reaches the funders, the bookings, the
internal correspondence and the decisions nobody ever intended you to
see. Fund the subpoena that opens those files.
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6409086/UaHR0cHM6Ly9mcmVlZG9td2F0Y2gucmV2di5jby9mdy11eWd1ci1waXBlbGluZS1tYi1vbS8/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNseDFCdHk0aw/qP3V0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1tYiZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPW9tJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZnctdXlndXItcGlwZWxpbmUmdXRtX3Rlcm09MjM4NjJfd3IxXQ/gau3i7w/s7o5c9209aa

We do not write strongly worded letters to Congress. We do not go on

YOUR REAL JUSTICE DEPARTMENT, because the one in Washington has been
inert for years and I stopped waiting on it a long time ago.

None of it is free. Filing fees, court reporters, transcripts,
investigators, forensic accountants to trace corporate money, and the
years of appeals a media company with real revenue will force on us
because delay is cheaper for them than defeat. It costs roughly $400

Before a single word is written.

The Piker case is live right now and the motions to try to kill it are

complaint drafted at the same time. Both of those things run on your
gifts.
