November 6, 2026

In a massacre that would embarrass Genghis Khan, the Democrats obliterated Republicans in the midterm elections. At the time of this writing, the Democrats have picked up seven Senate seats giving them a total of 54. Two races, Alaska and Mississippi, are too close to call, but odds are they will both go Democratic. In the House the Democrats have already won thirty seats and political pundits believe this number could climb to 46. Thus, the Democrats will have about 260 to 175 majority.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a089325-29fb-4fa1-8f44-99ce5ec50cd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Traditional Republican states such as South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa elected Democratic senators. And the liberal wish of turning Texas Blue finally came true, as the incumbent Republican Governor was vanquished and the open Senate seat was won by Democrat James Talerico by 12%. The State House also flipped to the Democrats as did all the constitutional offices.

In my home state of Connecticut, elected Republicans in our Assembly and Senate are rarer than Ivory-Billed Woodpeckers. Eight Senate seats were lost and now the Democrats have a 33-3 majority! The Governor, the Senators, constitutional officers and the Congressmen are all Democrats.

How did this happen?
**The invasion of Iran was a disaster.** With neither the consent of Congress nor the American people, President Trump decided he was going to bring peace to the Middle East by neutering Iran. But he had no plan. Only regime change is going to change Iran's policies, and this is not possible without an armed insurgency by Iranians, American ground troops or the use of nuclear weapons. The result, the clever Iranians looked at American polls, blocked the Strait of Hormuz and caused gas and diesel prices to skyrocket. Hello Democrats.

**People are tired of President Trump 's antics**. The inflationary tariffs were bad enough, but having his family promote cryptocurrency scams while his son-in-law Jared Kushner is extorting foreign leaders to[ invest in his hedge fund](https://substack.com/redirect/5087973e-a891-4d5c-9290-38c5e5a82aed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a bit much. And why insult Canada by saying it should become our 51st state while imposing lumber tariffs that increased housing costs. And sucking up to the barbarian Putin has accomplished nothing. The federal deficit is higher than ever. So much for fiscal conservatism.
**President Trump has lost his juice**. The conventional wisdom was that either Vance or Rubio would be the presidential nominee and if Trump choose one of them, the other would bow out. This has been thrown out the window. It may well be that both Vance and Rubio are too tainted by Trump and Republicans will look at more electable candidates such as Ron DeSantis or Nikki Haley.

**Trump was not the only issue**. [70% of the American people](https://substack.com/redirect/f4d8d130-6a9f-43fc-b345-7448514ce907?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) believe America is on the wrong tract. This number is consistent no matter what party is in the White House. We once had a country in which a man could support a family on one income. Now you can barely do it on two incomes. Young people are refusing to marry because they can't afford to. Neither party has any concrete solutions to high housing, health insurance and car prices. Taxes are too high but cutting them is politically impossible, especially with our massive $40 trillion deficit.

**This Blue Wave makes it easier for Republicans to win the White House in 2028.** Americans love divided government since it prevents the extremes of either party from imposing their will. The Democrats have relatively large majorities in the House and Senate, and many voters do not want to see an unchecked Democratic president, especially if the Democrats nominate a socialist such as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (AOC).

**Israel will have to fight harder for its existence.** Even prominent Jewish politicians such as Bernie Saunders and Jamie Raskin have embraced the Palestinian cause, and Democratic rallies are replete with Palestinian flags. The swing state of Michigan just elected a Democratic Senator, Abdul El-Sayed, who is openly hostile to Israel's existence. Unless President Trump by some miracle can turn the war around with Iran, Israel may soon find itself abandoned by the American political class.
But as bad as this election was for Republicans, it is not without precedent. The Democrats lost 63 seats during the Clinton presidency in 1994 and 54 seats during the Obama presidency in 2010 - more than the Republicans lost this cycle. Yet both Clinton and Obama won reelection easily. And there is no better street fight than Donald Trump, even when he is a lame duck. It would be foolish to count him out.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad38c65-0ab6-4436-bfe5-a4a77d71f149?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

But if this election shows anything, America is an unhappy country in spite of our affluence. People find happiness in faith, family, friends and financial security. The pollical, economic and cultural changes of the past two generations have made this possible for fewer people.

subject: Grant Report: November 6, 2026
body:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-november-6-2026?e=c16f400a56)
https://grantdemocracy.org/

Election Recap: Litigation, Some Glitches, and What Comes Next

By Justin Riemer, President, USGI

Although the results were noteworthy, Tuesday’s election was a relatively quiet affair, free of major meltdowns or the federal intervention some had warned of. Of course, the dust hasn’t completely settled: there are potential recounts in some House races and too-close-to-call Senate races in Mississippi, where there is a brewing (https://electionlawblog.org/2026/nrsc-sends-demand-to-mississippi-election-officials-to-segregate-provisional-ballots-likely-for-potential-legal-action-in-the-colom-hyde-smith-senate-race-not-clear-if-state-can-or-will-comply/) legal battle over affidavit ballots, and Alaska, where ranked-choice voting could lead to a significant delay before we know who won.

Litigation:

The main litigation fireworks occurred leading up to Election Day, with the Department of Justice suing both Alaska and California. The Alaska suit involved “Decoy Dan,” a spoiler candidate with the same name as incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan. Citing the National Voter Registration Act and, later, the Supremacy Clause, DOJ sought to halt Alaska’s certification of the election on voter confusion grounds. The district court dismissed the case finding DOJ lacked standing and DOJ has filed a notice of appeal. A criminal investigation is also reportedly underway.

The California suit sought to sequester, and not count, ballots cast by individuals the federal government identified as likely noncitizens until the state verified their citizenship. DOJ was denied a temporary restraining order in the district court and lost at the Ninth Circuit and the Supreme Court.

Progressive groups also sued to preemptively stop the federal government from pressing election officials, including through warnings of potential prosecution, not to count ballots from voters it had flagged as likely noncitizens. SEIU’s case in the Northern District of California was remarkable, if only for the speed with which the Ninth Circuit stayed the trial court’s temporary restraining order, lifted the stay, and then reinstated it. The court subsequently denied (https://www.jurist.org/news/2026/11/ninth-circuit-leaves-restrictions-on-doj-election-enforcement-on-hold/) plaintiffs’ request for rehearing before the full court. The litigation remains ongoing.

Administrative Issues:

Election Day ran smoothly in most jurisdictions. The most notable problem occurred in Westchester County, New York, where voting machines rejected ballots, forcing voters to deposit them in emergency secure bags. The source of the problem appears to be Westchester’s omission of a local race in Ardsley (pop. 5,000). According to the state Board of Elections (https://elections.ny.gov/system/files/documents/2026/11/westchester-ballot-scanning-press-release-final-11032026.pdf) , the county updated its election programming to reflect the change but deployed it only to machines in Ardsley. Machines elsewhere, still running the original programming, could not recognize the ballots, which had been printed with the corrected information, as the New York Times reports (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/nyregion/midterms-westchester-voting-issues.html) .

Litigation ensued, and shortly after polls closed, a state court judge signed a consent order (https://grantdemocracy.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/301C8B1611FC0D99DC119113E67AB3393C0310E9LEGALCASEBOOK.pdf) requiring the police to transport ballots to a central location for counting on Wednesday under the supervision of representatives from both parties.

Other isolated problems arose before and on Election Day, including ballot printing errors in Contra Costa County, California, (https://richmondside.org/2026/11/03/san-pablo-voters-ballots-missing-races/) voters receiving incorrect ballots in Bismarck, North Dakota (https://www.kfyrtv.com/2026/11/03/possible-ballot-mix-up-bismarcks-district-7-has-candidate-frustrated/) , long lines in Nevada (https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/politics-and-government/nevada/aguilar-says-nevada-voters-deserve-better-after-long-election-day-waits-3909976/?sfmc_id=419583069&utm_source=Newsletter&utm_medium=PoliticsEmailAlert&utm_campaign=Politics%20Alert%20-%20Aguilar%20says%20Nevada%20voters%20deserve%20better%20after%20long%20Election%20Day%20waits&utm_term=Aguilar%20says%20Nevada%20voters%20deserve%20better%20after%20long%20Election%20Day%20waits) , and delays in Broward County, Florida, (https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/community/broward/article317901350.html) tied to a new system that helps ensure
voters get the correct ballots.

Concerns about DOJ’s deployment of election observers also failed to materialize, although Michigan and New Mexico reported complaints (https://abc7news.com/live-updates/midterm-elections-2026-live-updates-election-results-key-races-us/20001292/entry/20013438/) about some observers’ actions. Nor were any ICE agents reported outside polling places.

Initiative Results & Policy Implications:

For conservatives dismayed by Tuesday’s results, a silver lining may be that voting-related initiatives fared (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/ballot-measures#elections-voting) comparatively well. Constitutional amendments enshrining voter ID passed relatively easily in Nevada, North Carolina, and Ohio, although they failed in Arizona, California, and Colorado. Citizen-only voting initiatives were also approved comfortably in Alaska, Arkansas, Kansas, South Dakota, and West Virginia. The citizenship amendments may prove especially important given a recent federal court ruling (https://grantdemocracy.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/0-25CR60249_DocketEntry_10-01-2026_64.pdf) that the federal ban on noncitizen voting is unconstitutional.

Tuesday’s results will undoubtedly impact election policy. The Democrats’ takeover of Congress all but forecloses passage of the SAVE America Act or similar federal legislation for the foreseeable future. At the state level, Democrats won trifectas in Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin and broke Republican trifectas in Georgia, Iowa, New Hampshire, Ohio, and Texas. At a minimum, this will prevent adoption of additional conservative-backed voting policies and may lead to the repeal of existing ones in states like Arizona and Wisconsin. Expect Democrats to push for expanded automatic and Election Day voter registration, broader mail voting, looser ballot harvesting restrictions, and repeal of voter ID and proof-of-citizenship laws. The effects will also reach agency rulemaking and informal policymaking.

Alaska

A New York Times investigation (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/28/us/politics/alaska-dan-sullivan-conspiracy-peltola.html) reported that operatives aligned with Mary Peltola’s campaign, working with Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee aides, spent months recruiting candidates, including Dan J. Sullivan, to draw votes from Senator Dan Sullivan. The Peltola campaign and the DSCC denied involvement.

The Justice Department sent (https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/03/justice-department-letters-peltola-sullivan-alaska-senate-race) more than 20 target or document-preservation letters to people and organizations allegedly involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan to run for the U.S. Senate, according to a person familiar with the investigation.

Several rural in-person absentee voting sites in Western Alaska did not open (https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-10-27/some-rural-alaska-absentee-voting-sites-failed-to-open-ahead-of-midterms) as scheduled, with the Division of Elections listing five as temporarily closed and removing three from its website without explanation.

Election returns showed (https://alaskapublic.org/news/politics/elections/2026-11-04/6-takeaways-from-alaskas-election) voters approving Ballot Measure 3, which limits voting in state and local elections to U.S. citizens. The outcome of Ballot Measure 2—which would repeal the state’s top-four primary and ranked-choice voting system, along with certain campaign disclosure requirements—remains undecided, with an estimated 50,000 to 75,000 ballots still uncounted and final certification scheduled for November 25.

Arizona

Voters rejected (https://arizonadailyindependent.com/2026/11/03/arizonans-reject-ballot-measures-for-voter-id-and-more/) Proposition 144, which would have added voter ID and citizens-only voting requirements to the state constitution.

Arkansas

The Washington County Election Commission voted unanimously (https://www.4029tv.com/article/washington-county-election-monitors/74252821) to decline a Justice Department request to place election monitors inside polling places on Election Day, citing the short notice.

The Pulaski County Election Commission voted 2–1 (https://arktimes.com/arkansas-blog/2026/10/29/pulaski-election-commission-denies-federal-request-to-send-in-poll-monitors) to deny the Justice Department’s request to place four monitors inside its polling places.

Voters approved (https://www.ualrpublicradio.org/local-regional-news/2026-11-04/a-roundup-of-2026-arkansas-election-results) Issue 1, providing in the state constitution that only U.S. citizens may vote.

California

Fresno County reported (https://abc30.com/post/typographical-printing-error-fresno-county-ballots/20003781/) that ballot-marking devices at its vote centers printed “Fowler Unified School District” in place of Fresno Unified on ballots. The county said tabulation still records votes in the correct contest, posted signs at vote centers, and offered print-on-demand ballots.

A system crash while retrieving preliminary results and a batch of mail ballots mislabeled as Election Day votes delayed (https://krcrtv.com/news/local/ballot-mix-up-delayed-shasta-county-election-day-count-as-workers-fixed-mislabeled-batch) Shasta County’s count by several hours on election night.

Federal prosecutors sent letters (https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/doj-presses-california-counties-to-verify-voter-eligibility-ahead-of-midterms/3960151/) to county registrars across the state demanding that they set aside and verify the ballots of registrants the DOJ lists as likely noncitizens and turn over identifying information within 48 hours.

Federal agents subpoenaed (https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/10/ca-election-officials-subpoenas/) three Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder employees to testify before a grand jury on November 4 and served the Orange County Registrar with a grand jury subpoena for unredacted records on 60 voters.

The Justice Department served (https://news.bloomberglaw.com/ip-law/doj-subpoenas-new-california-election-leaders-during-court-fight) grand jury subpoenas on top election administrators in Sonoma and Santa Clara counties, requiring responses by November 17. The subpoenas seek information about the counties’ responses to an October 23 DOJ letter requesting citizenship verification or the setting aside of ballots for “suspected aliens.”

Voters rejected (https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/11/california-election-2026-prop-39/) Proposition 39, which would have required government-issued ID at polling places and partial identification numbers on mail ballots.

California federal prosecutor Bill Essayli announced (https://townhall.com/news/amy-curtis/2026/10/29/bill-essayli-california-voter-fraud-indictments-n2685515) that a federal grand jury indicted three Los Angeles County noncitizens on federal election fraud charges. The defendants include a Mexican national who allegedly registered in 2013 and voted in 2020, a Cambodian national who allegedly registered in 2021 and voted in 2022 and 2024, and a Canadian national who allegedly registered in 2018.

A federal grand jury indicted (https://www.justice.gov/usao-cdca/pr/federal-grand-jury-indicts-10-noncitizens-who-illegally-registered-vote-california) 10 noncitizens living in Los Angeles and Orange counties for allegedly registering to vote in California by falsely claiming U.S. citizenship.

Colorado

The Secretary of State’s office told the Justice Department (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/22/colorado-pushes-back-on-federal-election-monitors/) that the monitors it planned to send to Adams County must apply for approval under state election rules before entering nonpublic areas such as mail ballot processing and signature verification. The DOJ said it chose Adams County because the Voting Rights Act requires bilingual ballots there, and declined (https://coloradosun.com/2026/10/29/colorado-allows-doj-election-observers-but-with-limits/) Secretary Griswold’s conditions, which would have required state-appointed escorts and designated observation areas.

Voters rejected (https://gazette.com/2026/11/03/ballot-id-requirements-colorado-election-results/) Amendment 84, which would have required voters to provide an identification number on their mail ballot envelopes.

Voters rejected (https://www.denvergazette.com/2026/11/05/colorado-ballot-measures-what-is-passing-failing-and-undecided/) Amendment 86, which would have required approval by the independent redistricting commission and the Colorado Supreme Court for mid-decade congressional redistricting.

Connecticut

The Secretary of the State’s office advised (https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/local/wallingford-to-recount-ballots-after-election-day-error/3792605/) Wallingford to conduct a discrepancy recount after poll workers fed about 100 emergency paper ballots, which must be counted by hand, into a tabulator.

Florida

A vendor error sent (https://www.wesh.com/article/volusia-voters-wrong-mail-ballots/74221363) about 350 Volusia County voters in the 6th Congressional District mail ballots carrying another city’s contests. Two had already been returned and counted, and the Supervisor of Elections mailed replacements to the rest.

The Justice Department warned (https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/south-florida-fake-election-monitors-department-of-justice/) election officials that people falsely claiming to be its monitors had appeared at South Florida early voting sites. Miami-Dade and Broward officials said they had received no such reports.

On November 3, severe flooding forced (https://www.wlrn.org/government-politics/2026-11-03/polling-places-shift-in-areas-affected-by-flooding) election officials to relocate () 21 polling sites across 30 precincts in eight Florida counties after roads became impassable, or polling locations were damaged. Governor DeSantis issued an executive order declaring a state of emergency in seven counties, allowing election supervisors to designate alternative polling locations.

A malfunctioning safety feature on Broward County’s new voting system delayed (https://www.opb.org/article/2026/11/03/election-day-unfolds-with-relatively-few-problems-some-voters-disrupted-by-weather-machine-issues/) the start of Election Day voting by about 20 minutes. Supervisor of Elections Joe Scott urged voters who left to return.

Georgia

An Anthropic AI model pulled (https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/gov-kemp-reasserts-confidence-voting-security-after-ai-review) aggregate counts from the Secretary of State’s public election data hub without being prompted, the company said. Secretary of State Raffensperger said only public data was reached, and state officials said no voting equipment or nonpublic registration system was breached.

An isolated districting error placed (https://www.mdjonline.com/elections/cobb-elections-discovers-ballot-error-affecting-east-cobb-precinct/article_0300e398-0755-4a91-b570-3d644cf1f7b9.html) the wrong state House race on ballots for Cobb County’s Sewell Mill 01 precinct. Votes cast there in the District 43 race, which appeared in place of District 37, will not be counted.

Indiana

Early and mail ballots in four Floyd County precincts omitted (https://www.lpm.org/news/2026-11-05/floyd-county-candidate-exploring-legal-options-after-incomplete-ballot-issue) the District 1 county commissioner race until officials caught the error, affecting 572 voters. The Democratic candidate said she was weighing a recount or a special election.

Kansas

Voters approved (https://www.kmuw.org/2026-11-03/kansas-voters-approve-amendment-to-clarify-wording-on-noncitizen-voting) a constitutional amendment clarifying that only U.S. citizens may vote in Kansas elections. The amendment revises the Kansas Constitution, replacing language granting voting rights to “every citizen” with language specifying that “no person” may vote unless they are a U.S. citizen, at least 18 years old, and a resident of the voting area. The amendment will take effect after election results are certified.

A county clerk’s clerical error caused (https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/midterm-election-results-2026-latest-updates/card/one-kansas-polling-site-briefly-ran-out-of-ballots-after-ordering-mix-up-RGhfF9YX4jBcVEEMdJj6) a ballot shortage at the Linwood Community Building in Leavenworth County, where election officials delivered approximately 100 paper ballots instead of the 1,000 needed. Voting was halted for about 90 minutes while officials delivered additional ballots.

Kentucky

A county clerk told the Justice Department (https://www.wdrbwave.com/2026/10/26/doj-seeks-federal-monitors-louisville-election-clerk-cites-state-law-barring-them-inside-polls/) that its election monitors may not enter polling places because state law does not list them among those permitted inside, a position Fayette County and the State Board of Elections share.

Maine

The Public Interest Legal Foundation filed a complaint (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/troubling-discovery-state-voter-rolls-sparks-action-days-before-midterms-should-have-been-fixed) with Secretary of State Shenna Bellows alleging that the state’s rolls contain 3,181 potentially deceased registrants and 693 duplicate registrations, and said it may pursue the Help America Vote Act’s administrative complaint process if the state does not act.

Maryland

On November 4, Governor Moore called (https://marylandmatters.org/2026/11/04/moore-new-maps-question-3/) on the General Assembly to draw new congressional maps when lawmakers convene in January, after voters approved Question 3 by about 60%. The constitutional amendment removes compactness and contiguity requirements and other protections for congressional districts and clarifies the Supreme Court of Maryland’s jurisdiction over redistricting challenges.

Massachusetts

Voters approved (https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/massachusetts-election-results-ballot-questions-2026/4043419/) Question 4, allowing voters to register at the polls on Election Day, and rejected Question 3, which would have created a top-two primary.

Michigan

On November 3, a bomb threat forced (https://www.wxyz.com/news/bomb-threat-called-into-polling-location-in-gibraltar-police-conducting-sweep) the evacuation of Gibraltar Carlson High School in Wayne County, which served as a polling location for Brownstown Township Precincts 8 and 11. Voting moved outside while officers from the Brownstown Township and Gibraltar police departments and the Wayne County Sheriff’s Office swept the building. Police identified a suspect, and a Secretary of State’s Office spokesperson confirmed around 6 p.m. that the threat was unfounded and the building was clear.

Minnesota

Hennepin County prosecutors charged (https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/10/28/james-okeefe-and-cam-higby-charged-with-unlawful-voting-for-youtube-videos) James O’Keefe and Cameron Higby with felony unlawful voting and identity theft, alleging they misrepresented their identities to election officials during the August primary while filming the encounters. O’Keefe’s group said no ballots were cast and the project tested the state’s vouching law.

Missouri

Voters repealed (https://ballotpedia.org/Missouri_Congressional_Map_Referendum_(2026)) the 2025 congressional map by referendum, leaving the 2022 map in place.

Nevada

A vendor printing error put (https://mynews4.com/news/local/printing-error-put-false-on-32000-washoe-county-ballot-return-envelopes) the word “FALSE” on about 32,000 Washoe County mail ballot return envelopes in a field meant to stay blank. The Registrar said the error did not affect ballot validity and was corrected in later batches.

Voters approved (https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/voter-id-requirement-added-nevada-082924092.html) Question 7 for the second time, adding to the state constitution a photo ID requirement for in-person voting and an identification-number requirement for mail ballots.

New Jersey

A programming error labeled (https://newjerseyglobe.com/local/glitch-on-hudson-voting-machines-leaves-spanish-language-ballots-without-democratic-line-b/) both of the first two columns “Line A” on the Spanish-language ballots on Hudson County’s early voting machines, leaving no Column B for Democratic candidates. The vendor attributed it to human error in programming the translated header, and the county replaced the machines.

Republican legislators asked (https://newjerseyglobe.com/campaigns/gop-lawmakers-demand-investigation-into-new-noncitizen-voter-registration-case/) Acting Secretary of State Emehelu to investigate how a 19-year-old lawful permanent resident became an active voter through the Motor Vehicle Commission, and to audit MVC-generated registrations.

New Mexico

A federal grand jury indicted (https://www.abqjournal.com/news/maryland-man-indicted-in-alleged-new-mexico-voter-fraud/3149565) a Maryland man on a charge of submitting a false voter registration application to the Bernalillo County Clerk in 2022.

New York

The State Board of Elections said (https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/rochester/news/2026/10/22/some-voters-receive-late-ballots) it is investigating mail ballot delays tied to Fort Orange Press, the Albany vendor whose envelope shortage held up part of Monroe County’s first mailing.

Ballot scanners across Westchester County rejected (https://www.opb.org/article/2026/11/03/election-day-unfolds-with-relatively-few-problems-some-voters-disrupted-by-weather-machine-issues/) paper ballots on Election Day after a program update made following preelection testing, and poll workers placed ballots in emergency bags. Counting of the set-aside ballots resumed (https://abc7ny.com/post/midterm-results-vote-counting-resumes-westchester-county-election-day-ballot-glitch/20015392/) the next day.

North Carolina

In an interview with the Daily Signal, J. Christian Adams of the Public Interest Legal Foundation argues (https://www.dailysignal.com/2026/10/23/noncitizen-voting-election-2026/) that registration systems should stop any application on which the applicant answers “no” to the citizenship question, and that states can check their rolls against federal citizenship data without waiting for Congress.

Former Virginia State Board of Elections Secretary and Florida Director of Elections Don Palmer argues (https://www.dailysignal.com/2026/11/02/election-integrity-on-ballot/) that the midterms will decide whether Congress finishes the administration’s citizenship-verification agenda.

Bright Line Watch’s October survey (https://brightlinewatch.org/democracy-before-2026-midterms/) of 492 political scientists and 2,750 members of the public found Republicans more confident than Democrats that eligible voters can cast ballots, and less confident that administrators will count them accurately.

body:
| | | | [](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjk18vO7wfT-2FWuWGj5qYFNqYx7X5ohQ4dCOx5p85so2pL-Xzk_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHer4Gkk3hTvyUoeoP-2BXPW5ZICldNIqnvoMNgEPxSy31jz-2B4tE7I0VSL3R7f50jsoJqiM9yDuDz8uEL8ToHXmadxq8KNYzZSzxxQXnkw1KWXnTsRUEWQjT698gLcefzYn8-2BR1zC-2BTLOIIYbbLrVQ9fqtgp9fi3Z8wUY99XPQITXSYrajISShVajfCujd3niaPLSuoSS5tdF1dmlkomh9tUyWLBsp7h5-2Bq51XZ7-2FjLsMeKX4-3D)
---
|
---
Dear Friend, Like you, I'm still shocked, but not surprised, by the election results from earlier this week.

Of the 180-plus state lawmakers in the State Freedom Caucus Network, seven patriots lost their re-election bids on Tuesday. I'm angry they lost through no fault of their own, but because of a national Blue Wave that ran all the way down the ballot in some states.

There was some good news, though, and it highlights the Network's unique structure and mission. We have so many fighters in more than a dozen states that even in a bad election year, we still chalked up real victories.

**Wyoming Freedom Caucus** founding member Secretary of State Chuck Gray won his race to replace Harriet Hageman in Congress.

**Louisiana Freedom Caucus** founding member State Sen. Blake Miguez will advance to the Dec. 12 runoff in the open 6th congressional district. He will be the heavy favorite to win.

Both Chuck and Blake will be ready to fight in D.C. in January.
---
[](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjsvcX-2BTkwxYbebIdBX-2B73guuoHMzJZ-2BadAauFwB5b0vVxMGzNe7GFIyGIyBeJ644R4WTLmmyf-2BoreyyOJ8FcEn8-3DF7Me_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHer4Gkk3hTvyUoeoP-2BXPW5ZICldNIqnvoMNgEPxSy31jz-2B4tE7I0VSL3R7f50jsoJqiM9yDuDz8uEL8ToHXmadxq8KNYzZSzxxQXnkw1KWXnTtybFXED-2BYG6ktpIjcd0tKK1tEfKkl2T6T3QbikwHPY6yYEmMBJDu5kGhCLMEhi3pXTsmrZTy7gvK5-2B-2Fnw-2B8JfkRkr1e4LGiJWAu8EMF9kIWlZ-2F5sVrrWVzINn7lx2JvJc-3D)
---
**Montana Freedom Caucus** members all won on Tuesday. As we have said for months, they should roughly increase their size by 50%, from 20 current members to perhaps 30, because of their successful primary elections. There was no Blue Wave in Big Sky country.

**South Dakota Freedom Caucus** member State Rep. Heather Baxter was elected Secretary of State.

And thanks to our state Freedom Caucuses, both West Virginia and South Dakota passed constitutional amendments on Tuesday that require citizenship to vote.

House Freedom Caucus member Byron Donalds will be Florida's next governor. House Freedom Caucus member Barry Moore will be that state's newest U.S. Senator.

After Tuesday's election, the Missouri legislature held its leadership elections. **Missouri Freedom Caucus** members State Sen. Nick Schroer and State Rep. Darin Chappell were elected Senate Majority Leader and House Majority Leader. Imagine that! It was only a couple of years ago when they were punished by leadership for being too conservative. Now they ARE the leaders in their respective chambers.

Last but not least: because of Darline Graham's failed candidacy, South Carolina will have a Democrat senator for the first time in more than 20 years. But you'd be wrong if you thought the Palmetto State is descending into liberalism. The **South Carolina Freedom Caucus** is as strong as ever, and the state just elected Mark Burkhold as comptroller. Burkhold campaigned on radical transparency about how the state spends tax dollars. Expect SCFC members to work with him and push DOGE-style audits. And SCFC's biggest antagonist, incoming House Majority Leader Micah Caskey, lost his re-election bid.

So broadly speaking, are we upset about how Tuesday turned out? Absolutely. But your state Freedom Caucuses, and the patriots who belong to them, are only getting started. That's something to cheer about.
---
|
---
**HELP US KEEP BUILDING** Tuesday showed what we already know. The establishment and the Blue Wave can take seats, but they can't stop organized Freedom Caucuses that keep recruiting, keep educating voters, and keep showing up. Chuck Gray and Blake Miguez are headed to Congress. Heather Baxter is South Dakota's next Secretary of State. Missouri Freedom Caucus members now hold both majority leadership posts. Citizenship-to-vote amendments passed in West Virginia and South Dakota.That progress happens because supporters like you make it possible.

clean_body: | | | | | Dear Friend, Like you, I'm still shocked, but not surprised, by the election results from earlier this week. Of the 180-plus state lawmakers in the State Freedom Caucus Network, seven patriots lost their re-election bids on Tuesday. I'm angry they lost through no fault of their own, but because of a national Blue Wave that ran all the way down the ballot in some states. There was some good news, though, and it highlights the Network's unique structure and mission. We have so many fighters in more than a dozen states that even in a bad election year, we still chalked up real victories. Wyoming Freedom Caucus founding member Secretary of State Chuck Gray won his race to replace Harriet Hageman in Congress. Louisiana Freedom Caucus founding member State Sen. Blake Miguez will advance to the Dec. 12 runoff in the open 6th congressional district. He will be the heavy favorite to win. Both Chuck and Blake will be ready to fight in D.C. in January. Montana Freedom Caucus members all won on Tuesday. As we have said for months, they should roughly increase their size by 50%, from 20 current members to perhaps 30, because of their successful primary elections. There was no Blue Wave in Big Sky country. South Dakota Freedom Caucus member State Rep. Heather Baxter was elected Secretary of State. And thanks to our state Freedom Caucuses, both West Virginia and South Dakota passed constitutional amendments on Tuesday that require citizenship to vote. House Freedom Caucus member Byron Donalds will be Florida's next governor. House Freedom Caucus member Barry Moore will be that state's newest U.S. Senator. After Tuesday's election, the Missouri legislature held its leadership elections. Missouri Freedom Caucus members State Sen. Nick Schroer and State Rep. Darin Chappell were elected Senate Majority Leader and House Majority Leader. Imagine that! It was only a couple of years ago when they were punished by leadership for being too conservative. Now they ARE the leaders in their respective chambers. Last but not least: because of Darline Graham's failed candidacy, South Carolina will have a Democrat senator for the first time in more than 20 years. But you'd be wrong if you thought the Palmetto State is descending into liberalism. The South Carolina Freedom Caucus is as strong as ever, and the state just elected Mark Burkhold as comptroller. Burkhold campaigned on radical transparency about how the state spends tax dollars. Expect SCFC members to work with him and push DOGE-style audits. And SCFC's biggest antagonist, incoming House Majority Leader Micah Caskey, lost his re-election bid. So broadly speaking, are we upset about how Tuesday turned out? Absolutely. But your state Freedom Caucuses, and the patriots who belong to them, are only getting started. That's something to cheer about. | HELP US KEEP BUILDING Tuesday showed what we already know. The establishment and the Blue Wave can take seats, but they can't stop organized Freedom Caucuses that keep recruiting, keep educating voters, and keep showing up. Chuck Gray and Blake Miguez are headed to Congress. Heather Baxter is South Dakota's next Secretary of State. Missouri Freedom Caucus members now hold both majority leadership posts. Citizenship-to-vote amendments passed in West Virginia and South Dakota.That progress happens because supporters like you make it possible. We'll be back with another update soon. Until then, please be sure to our efforts so that we can support our State Freedom Caucuses!In Liberty, Andy RothPresidentState Freedom Caucus Network | |

_That dining chair that is just so is the one I select, ready for the possibility._
I need to tighten a screw on that one.
_It is never just for Elijah, though it has always been his. Now too many have come after for it to be his alone._
Every chair could use a polish.
_For the one or many who stop in, we will give up ours and then pull up a barstool for ourselves._
The barstools, too, need some attention.
_The table will seat us all. It is built for many and has served us well. Even with its scratches, it remains one of my favorite pieces of furniture in the whole house._
I need to recenter it.
_This work has always been just a tad more important than the food._
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

name: Hull for New Mexico
subject: One last favor, and a big thank you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by [Hull for New Mexico](https://us
body:
I couldn't have asked for a better team.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZOyjFYZjPIj?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810)
| |
# One last favor, and a big thank you
---
| | | | | | Friend,
I want to start with two words: thank you.
Thank you for the doors you knocked, the calls you made, the yard signs you put up, the events you showed up for, and every dollar you gave to this campaign. Whether you gave $5 or volunteered every weekend since spring, you were part of something that mattered.
The result wasn't what we worked for. But I'm proud of the campaign we ran and the ideas we put in front of New Mexicans: safer communities, a stronger economy, schools that deliver for our kids, and a state government that answers to the people it serves. Those ideas don't go away because an election is over. They're still worth fighting for, and I'll keep fighting for them.
I have one last favor to ask.
Our signs are still standing in yards, along roads, and on street corners across New Mexico. If you put one up, or you see one on property where you have permission, please take it down this week and either recycle it or throw it away. Please don't remove signs from private property without the owner's okay, and stay safe near traffic.
Leaving our communities cleaner than we found them is the right way to close out this campaign.
Being your candidate has been one of the great honors of my life. Carrie and I are grateful to every one of you.
With gratitude,
---

name: BREAKTHROUGH HOUR with Sean Feucht
subject: A SHAKING FOR AN AWAKENING
body:
Episode 21 now available!| | | |
---
| | |
---
This week’s Breakthrough Hour is about what happens when the fire burns everything to the ground—and what God does with the ashes. Tuesday was a political earthquake. Texas went blue. Abortion rights were enshrined in three more states. And evangelical turnout hit its lowest point since the Reagan era. We need to have an uncomfortable conversation about how we got here. The church doesn’t need a political strategy right now. We need a word from heaven. That’s why next Friday night, November 13th at 7 p.m., we’re gathering at Camp Elah—our house of prayer on Capitol Hill—to worship, pray, and declare that Jesus is King over Washington DC. I hope you’ll join us. 310 3rd Street NE. The fire is real. The destruction is real. But so is the new growth. This is our moment to return to the Lord, to rebuild, and to wake up.

Tuesday was a political earthquake. Texas went blue. Abortion rights were enshrined in three more states. And evangelical turnout hit its lowest point since the Reagan era. We need to have an uncomfortable conversation about how we got here. The church doesn’t need a political strategy right now. We need a word from heaven. That’s why next Friday night, November 13th at 7 p.m., we’re gathering at Camp Elah—our house of prayer on Capitol Hill—to worship, pray, and declare that Jesus is King over Washington DC. I hope you’ll join us. 310 3rd Street NE. The fire is real. The destruction is real. But so is the new growth. This is our moment to return to the Lord, to rebuild, and to wake up. * * *
**By Wendy M. Yurgo**
We hired a hatchet man. We knew exactly who we were getting.
Donald Trump wasn't hired to make Washington comfortable, protect the feelings of career politicians, or preserve a bloated bureaucracy that has spent decades burning through our money. He was hired to turn the place around.
And I understood the assignment.
Years ago, when I was practicing law exclusively, one of my specialties was business turnarounds. I absolutely loved it. Still do.
Give me a company buried in debt, bleeding money, riddled with dysfunction, and written off by everyone else, and I'm in my element. I love digging into the financials, following the money, finding the waste, and figuring out who made the mess, who benefited from it, and what it would take to clean it up.
And believe me, I usually found a whole lot more than bad business decisions. I found corruption.
I was DOGE-ing long before DOGE was a thing.
Here's what I learned. **You cannot rescue a failing organization without making people uncomfortable.**
You cannot eliminate waste without upsetting the people spending the money. You cannot remove incompetent leadership without offending the people who put them there. And you certainly cannot expose corruption and expect the people profiting from it to thank you.
Turnarounds are ugly, expensive, and exhausting. They require difficult decisions, sleepless nights, damaged relationships, and the willingness to be unpopular. Sometimes you have to tear an organization down to its foundation before you can build something worth saving.
The people who hired you had better understand that, because the minute the turnaround gets painful, everyone suddenly becomes an expert on how you should be doing your job.
Sound familiar?
Trump was first hired in 2016 to confront a political establishment that had spent decades accumulating debt, expanding government, and leaving our children to pay for it. Instead, much of his first presidency was consumed by the Russia-collusion allegations, investigations, congressional warfare, and two impeachments.
The Steele dossier's credibility collapsed under scrutiny. Special Counsel Robert Mueller did not establish a criminal conspiracy between the Trump campaign and the Russian government, although his investigation documented Russian interference in the election. Subsequent investigations exposed serious failures in the FBI's surveillance process.
Washington spent years fighting over Donald Trump.
Then came 2024. Trump won the Electoral College, won the popular vote, and Americans gave him another chance to finish the job.

He didn't waste a minute. The man barely had time to put on his tuxedo before he rolled up his sleeves.
At an age when most Americans would be enjoying retirement, Trump returned to one of the most demanding jobs in the world. He assembled a team I consider exceptionally capable, and they went to work on immigration enforcement, energy, trade, regulatory reform, government efficiency, and federal spending.
Not every initiative has worked. Some have run into the courts. Others have proven more difficult to implement than anticipated. But look at the sheer volume of what this administration has taken on in less than two years.
I don't agree with everything Donald Trump does. Never have. Never will.
**But I didn 't hire him to agree with me. I hired him to do a job.**
* * *
# **We will not give up hope, and neither should you**
Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3f1d4867-ae67-4245-9478-bf2112f07ea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
We must fight for our nation with every thing we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
**PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
When I took over a troubled company, I didn't promise the owners that every decision would make them happy. I promised to find out what was wrong and do what was necessary to fix it. Sometimes that meant eliminating expenses people had grown comfortable with, firing executives who had become untouchable, or confronting owners who were themselves part of the problem.
Nothing destroys a turnaround faster than people demanding results while fighting every decision necessary to produce them.
**America hired a turnaround CEO. Then, halfway through the assignment, we elected a board that fundamentally disagrees with the turnaround.**
Except Washington isn't corporate America.
As a CEO, I can eliminate a department, terminate an executive, cancel an unnecessary expense, and restructure operations within the law. A president cannot.
Our Founders designed it that way, and for good reason. But those same constitutional checks and balances make reforming Washington infinitely more complicated than rescuing a private company.
Congress controls appropriations. Courts review executive actions. Federal agencies operate under mountains of laws and regulations. And the bureaucracy has had decades to perfect the art of protecting itself.
**The debt didn 't accumulate overnight. The bureaucracy didn't become this enormous overnight. And neither will disappear overnight.**
We're talking about trillions of dollars, generations of obligations, and American families paying for decisions made long before Trump returned to Washington. There is plenty of blame to go around, Republicans included.
But Americans hired someone to confront it. They knew it would be difficult, knew it would take time, and knew he would make decisions they wouldn't like.
Then came November 3.
Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. Americans were frustrated over high prices, the economy, the war with Iran, and the direction of the country. Republicans paid the price.
But elections don't just register frustration. They transfer power.
And beginning in January, congressional power will belong to the party that opposes much of the turnaround Trump was elected to carry out.
The new House majority will control its legislative agenda and investigative committees. The Democratic Senate will have the power to block nominees. Both chambers will wield enormous leverage over legislation and federal spending.
Trump will retain his executive authority and veto power. But passing legislation, confirming appointments, and securing funding for his priorities will become considerably more difficult.
As an attorney, I believe in legitimate oversight. I also know exactly what happens when legal process is used primarily to exhaust an opponent.
**The process becomes the punishment.**
The legal fees, document demands, depositions, hearings, and endless hours spent defending yourself instead of doing the work you were hired to do. Sometimes you don't have to win a case to cripple your opponent. You just have to keep him fighting it.
Now imagine two years of that in Washington.
Spending battles consume Congress. Investigations dominate the headlines. Legislation stalls, and the administration spends precious time defending its decisions rather than advancing its agenda.
Then come the complaints. Why hasn't the waste been eliminated? Why is Washington still dysfunctional? Why aren't things getting better?
**You cannot tie a man 's hands behind his back and then complain that he isn't getting the job done.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3f1d4867-ae67-4245-9478-bf2112f07ea2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

I've seen this happen in business. Owners hire someone to rescue a failing company, promise their support, and then panic when the restructuring begins. They protect the people who created the problems, reverse necessary decisions, and undermine management. When the turnaround fails, they blame the person they hired to save them.
**Some people love the idea of being rescued. They just cannot tolerate what rescue actually requires.**
Trump still has two years left in office, and Washington has an enormous amount of unfinished business. The national debt continues to grow. Families still need relief. Businesses still need an economy in which they can survive.
**The clock doesn 't stop because Washington decides to fight. Neither do the bills.**
The politicians will have their hearings, the lawyers will have their cases, and the television networks will have their ratings. The American people will pay for every minute of it.
America hired Donald Trump to do a job. Twice. In 2024, voters gave him four years to finish it. Now, barely halfway through, they've handed his political opponents the power to challenge much of his agenda.
If Washington spends the next two years tearing itself apart while the debt grows, the bureaucracy survives, and meaningful reforms stall, Americans will demand to know who is responsible.
The president will answer for his decisions, Congress for its actions, and voters for the government they elected.
**Want to know who derailed the turnaround? Look in the mirror.**

subject: One AMBER Alert saved this little girl
body:
A predator promised a mother a new life. Then one alarm changed everything.

| | | |
---
| |
---
| | God's Children Are Not For Sale
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
My name is Eduardo Verastegui.

I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and the founder of **Sound of Freedom Foundation. **

Years ago, I met the people who rescue children from trafficking.When I heard what is done to these children, I asked myself one question:

**_What if it were my child?_**

That question changed my life. And it is why I am writing to you today.

I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her "Lola."
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckTGP3CAQhX8N7s5iwGBvQRFptd2liCKlRGMYdtGB2QDe_P3IvmvSppx5M9_M0_v1bt8xprjdv2MmU3uwtdmyEeaVKiaqveGLfH_ElmK3ggv9BvDGtUXX44vshIM33nkEN5CB-SIvC19ADQ8jBS1yXfk8L5MiBRCUcAG0FKu--OUyRHPwALgGzTmI0U-o-CpBCg4LR84mfv4wVnrua4oOt47tI5TqaHQlD8k8en82Jr8xcWPi1sjtlcZW9s2XECqRLzkcFfZYtrHU-zFVgk0l4WnHovvN5K2VvTqyrnhi8vrj5w3UrEAxofeebSYf98zklTLG9NX8XGHy-sDqsX2cpE_JYX5ivG9MXv859iV3qgdsqMY__8SUYtMzm_j9gJ---n9G8TLibwAAAP__f8-brQ)

Lola's mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl.

Then she met a man online.

He promised her the moon and the stars.

He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for.

**It was a lie. **

Soon, Lola and her mother were missing.

One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico.

So she sounded the alarm.

**She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola 's picture and pushed her case into the public eye.**
---
[ Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckTGP3CAQhX8N7s5iwGBvQRFptd2liCKlRGMYdtGB2QDe_P3IvmvSppx5M9_M0_v1bt8xprjdv2MmU3uwtdmyEeaVKiaqveGLfH_ElmK3ggv9BvDGtUXX44vshIM33nkEN5CB-SIvC19ADQ8jBS1yXfk8L5MiBRCUcAG0FKu--OUyRHPwALgGzTmI0U-o-CpBCg4LR84mfv4wVnrua4oOt47tI5TqaHQlD8k8en82Jr8xcWPi1sjtlcZW9s2XECqRLzkcFfZYtrHU-zFVgk0l4WnHovvN5K2VvTqyrnhi8vrj5w3UrEAxofeebSYf98zklTLG9NX8XGHy-sDqsX2cpE_JYX5ivG9MXv859iV3qgdsqMY__8SUYtMzm_j9gJ---n9G8TLibwAAAP__f8-brQ)
---
And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services.

Alone. Frightened.But alive.

Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim.

We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear -- that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked.

**But he did not get to keep her. **

**We stopped him. **

Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckTGP3CAQhX8N7s5iwGBvQRFptd2liCKlRGMYdtGB2QDe_P3IvmvSppx5M9_M0_v1bt8xprjdv2MmU3uwtdmyEeaVKiaqveGLfH_ElmK3ggv9BvDGtUXX44vshIM33nkEN5CB-SIvC19ADQ8jBS1yXfk8L5MiBRCUcAG0FKu--OUyRHPwALgGzTmI0U-o-CpBCg4LR84mfv4wVnrua4oOt47tI5TqaHQlD8k8en82Jr8xcWPi1sjtlcZW9s2XECqRLzkcFfZYtrHU-zFVgk0l4WnHovvN5K2VvTqyrnhi8vrj5w3UrEAxofeebSYf98zklTLG9NX8XGHy-sDqsX2cpE_JYX5ivG9MXv859iV3qgdsqMY__8SUYtMzm_j9gJ---n9G8TLibwAAAP__f8-brQ)
---
Friend, this is not a movie.

About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department.

**Two million. Each one made in the image of God. **

Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it.

**That truth does not let us look away.**

Jesus said, "_Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these._ " (Matthew 19:14 NIV)

That is why **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists -- **to stop the sale of God 's children. **

And Lola's story shows the most important truth of all: **children are found when people pay attention. **

Here is how you can join the fight today:

1\. **Stay alert.** Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises.

2\. **If you see something, say something**. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through **Sound of Freedom Foundation's** partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733.

3.**Make your first gift**. Help **Sound of Freedom Foundation** and our partners keep sounding the alarm.

But when good people speak up, **God 's children come home. **

Tonight, a child is waiting to be found. You can be the one who steps in right now.

**Friday, November 6, 2026 -**_****_
_**Iran:** President Donald Trump threatens to "destroy what is left" of Iran, says decision on new strikes coming soon. Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Strait of Hormuz._
_**Palestine:** Two Palestinians die from wounds sustained in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. 94% of Gaza's population needs shelter assistance, UN says. Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Ansarallah attacks over Saudi Arabia. Turkish parliament approves trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli forces fire on olive-pickers, detain resident amid new ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon._

DOJ civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns. California Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes death sentences of all 548 death-row inmates. Bloomberg: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly considering leaving Trump administration._
_**International:** Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns amid bank collapse and corruption allegations. U.S. imposes new sanctions on Cuba. Russian strikes cause power outages across seven Ukrainian regions; death toll from aid center attack rises to 53. Indonesian police name fourth suspect in alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto. Macau pro-democracy activist sentenced to 12.5 years in prison. Tanzania sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison. Two Egyptian army officers killed in operation along Sudan border._

# Iran
* **Trump threatens to "destroy what is left" of Iran, says decision on new strikes coming soon: **President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would soon decide whether to launch another round of U.S. strikes on Iran, threatening to "destroy what is left of the country."
* Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said that the U.S. must decide whether to "go further" to prevent Iran from rebuilding its military and nuclear capabilities, claiming that the country will already need "25 years" to recover from the destruction the U.S. and Israel inflicted on it. "I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so. You will know very soon," he said.
* Trump also said that after more than eight months of war, the U.S. controls "everything that we've wanted to control" in Iran, and that Tehran cannot take action on its nuclear program "without approval."
* **Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Strait of Hormuz:** Two oil tankers caught fire and were immobilized after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Both vessels had switched off their navigation and identification systems, the IRGC claimed, and were attempting to exit the strait through a prohibited passage, with U.S. military support.
* The IRGC said that the strait would "remain closed" until the U.S. meets Iran's seven conditions for a peace deal, adding that attempts by the U.S. military Central Command to force tankers through mined, unauthorized routes would result in "successive defeats."
* Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported an explosion aboard a tanker transiting the strait, approximately 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman, at 1 a.m. local time Friday. It was unclear whether the incident involved either tanker reported by Iran. UKMTO said the vessel continued its voyage, with all crew members accounted for.

# Palestine
* **Two Palestinians die from wounds sustained in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza:** A female medical student at the Islamic University of Gaza [died](https://substack.com/redirect/60c464d4-3edc-4a7c-8c6a-245ae77554e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Friday from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike on the university about a week ago, WAFA reported. A man died from wounds sustained in an Israeli attack on the Al-Shati refugee camp several days earlier.
* **94% of Gaza 's population needs shelter assistance, UN says: **1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter assistance as winter approaches, with 270 displaced families living in four UN shelters at very high risk of collapse, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/476f836c-af46-42f3-8fa6-65014ef49663?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a new report from the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East, known as UNRWA. Meanwhile, 84% of Gaza's population faces frequent disruptions to clean water supplies, while 89% of households lack basic hygiene items.
* Israeli restrictions have prevented UNRWA from directly bringing aid into Gaza since March 2025, leaving food and shelter supplies for hundreds of thousands of Palestinians stranded outside the territory.
* Read Drop Site News contributor Abdel Qadder Sabbah's [latest report](https://substack.com/redirect/f2baafb0-055e-4fe6-89da-d764c55d199b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Gaza: Displaced Palestinians are living in tents, without proper shelter, as winter approaches.
* **Israel destroys 100,000 olive trees this year in the occupied West Bank; Gaza faces "ecocide": **Israeli forces and settlers [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/ad04b3e9-43cd-4226-906e-8818fb56ad95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 760 environmental attacks across the West Bank in the first nine months of 2026, destroying approximately 100,000 olive trees and causing an estimated $67 million in losses, according to the Palestinian Environmental Quality Authority. The attacks targeted farmland, water sources, irrigation networks, and natural reserves, while Israeli forces and settlers also dumped hazardous waste and demolished infrastructure.
* In Gaza, the authority said Israeli attacks have left up to 68 million tons of rubble, including four million tons of hazardous waste, and destroyed 82% of agricultural land, 97% of fruit and olive trees, and 84% of water and sanitation infrastructure. The authority described the destruction as "ecocide."
* **Israeli forces arrest 17 during olive harvest as settlers attack Palestinians across West Bank:**
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/b7a70625-e690-4e60-8d72-6a527b1d2d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 17 people, including 12 international solidarity activists, two foreign journalists, and three Palestinians, after settlers attacked farmers and volunteers harvesting olives in Kafr Ni'ma on Friday, according to WAFA.
* **Nablus:** Settlers [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/1045029b-0777-4bf5-bfc6-82872ff93f60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olives from a farm in Al-Masoudiya, cut electricity poles supplying a home housing three families in Burin, and set fire to residential tents in Duma.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/25ed39e2-33ab-430e-ac06-762f46e04b94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man in Yatta after he and his son confronted settlers who had released livestock onto Palestinian farmland. In Hebron city, Israeli forces raided homes in Jabal Jawhar and Jabal al-Rahma, converting one into a military post, and fired tear gas at residents and traders attending a weekly livestock market.
* **Occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli authorities [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/1d8902a4-b442-4ef6-8b16-80461e6fc8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinian families to demolish their own homes in Jabal Mukabber, displacing 18 people. The two homes, each measuring approximately 50 square meters, were built in 2020.
* **Netanyahu calls Trump 's decision to end U.S. military aid a shift toward "partnership": **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office portrayed President Donald Trump's decision to end U.S. military aid to Israel at the end of this year as a transition from aid to partnership, claiming the move demonstrates the "strength and sophistication" of U.S.-Israel relations. In a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/727a0d5a-3a51-42c9-b0dc-d43ad292f445?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, Netanyahu's office said that Israel had used decades of American military assistance "both to defend itself and to confront enemies who threaten America and the West," describing the funding as a longstanding bipartisan commitment.
* Netanyahu's spokesperson Doron Spielman told Fox News that the Israeli leader had been working with Trump to replace aid with "partnership and mutual investment."

# Yemen
* **Yemen 's Saudi-backed government claims 440 Ansarallah fighters killed or wounded; strikes on Taiz market cause over 30 casualties: **Yemen's Saudi-backed forces claimed they "neutralized" 440 Ansarallah fighters and destroyed or disabled 132 military vehicles and heavy weapons in nearly 1,300 attacks since launching Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 5.
* Meanwhile, Saudi-coalition airstrikes hit a market three times in al-Wazi'iyah, Taiz governorate, on Friday morning, Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV reported. The attacks killed or wounded more than 30 people, with rescue teams still searching for missing victims.
* **Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Ansarallah attacks over Saudi Arabia:** The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia, as well as a drone over the Mecca region, the coalition said on Friday.
* **Turkish parliament approves trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan:** Turkey's parliament [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/ce1d29c8-618f-41f6-b91f-237087cc31d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 279-119 on Thursday to ratify the "Mecca Agreement on Joint Defense" with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, clearing the way for the trilateral security pact, signed in August, to take effect. The agreement aims to strengthen collective security and expand military cooperation among the three countries. During Turkey's parliamentary debate, ruling Justice and Development Party lawmaker Ziya Altunyaldiz said that the pact was not directed against any third country and was intended to prevent further conflicts, not produce them.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli forces fire on olive-pickers, detain resident amid new ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon:**
* **Marjeyoun:** Israeli forces [advanced](https://substack.com/redirect/137d56e2-b8c2-46c2-8c64-0594fe67625d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Kfar Kila toward the outskirts of Deir Mimas, firing near residents harvesting olives and forcing them to flee. The troops blocked entry and exit from the village and detained a resident, taking him to an unknown location.
* **Bint Jbeil:** Israeli forces carried out a massive explosion on the outskirts of Beit Yahoun, toward Konin.
* **Nabatieh:** Israeli forces [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/0cdef807-4c9f-4266-ae92-09149d1bfa36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the outskirts of Mifdoun.

# U.S. News
* **Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed backs Chris Van Hollen over Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader:** In an interview with CNN on Thursday, **Abdul El-Sayed** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3337a59c-8512-48f5-ba55-7ee77c66bd50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he supports Maryland Sen. **Chris Van Hollen** for Senate Majority Leader. El-Sayed said he would look at other options if Van Hollen did not run for the position, adding that he will support a leader who intends to pass legislation. Newly elected Democratic senators in Kansas, Illinois, and Maine--**Adam Hamilton** , **Juliana Stratton** , and **Troy Jackson** --have said they will not back Sen. **Chuck** **Schumer** for the post.
* **Sen. Chuck Grassley denies rumor of resignation during the lame-duck session:** Sen. **Chuck Grassley** [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/96abf6e0-29d7-4abf-ad20-153e3984a902?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) rumors that he would resign before the new Congress is sworn. If Grassley remains in office, he would prevent the incoming Democratic Gov. **Rob Sand** from appointing a successor. Grassley's chief of staff said on Thursday that the 93-year-old Iowa Republican "remains committed to delivering for the people of Iowa, who overwhelmingly elected him to a six-year term in 2022." Grassley has not said whether he will seek a ninth term in 2028.
* **Trump says votes cast for Alaska 's "Fake Dan Sullivan" should go to Sen. Dan Sullivan: **President Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/7566a343-e90e-4092-bd95-ca499defa2d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that the votes cast for **Daniel J. Sullivan Jr**. "should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan." As of Friday morning, 75% of the votes were counted, and Democratic candidate **Mary Peltola** maintains a close lead over Sen. **Dan Sullivan**. The DOJ has sought to intervene in the election, citing voter confusion over the addition of Daniel J. Sullivan to the ballot.
* **In the Mississippi Senate race, Scott Colom widens lead by 1,800+ votes:** Democratic candidate **Scott Colom** [widened](https://substack.com/redirect/cad36d22-a3b1-48cf-ad5b-0d37f3e5d722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his lead over Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith** in Mississippi's Senate race to more than 1,800 votes on Thursday, according to Decision Desk HQ. Earlier in the week, Colom was in a virtual dead heat with Hyde-Smith, at one point leading the incumbent by just 28 votes. Mississippi is awaiting 3,600 outstanding mail ballots.
* **Aggressive DOJ civil rights director Harmeet Dhillon resigns: Harmeet Dhillon** resigned as head of the DOJ civil rights division, Attorney General **Todd Blanche** announced on Thursday. In her official capacity, Dhillon aggressively attacked left-wing groups, universities, and state election apparatuses. She ran the DOJ's largest ever election-monitoring operation, which did not produce a single announced finding of voter fraud. She [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/90391a1d-0969-4535-b01b-21bdb2814bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) intends to return to the law firm she founded, Dhillon Law Group.
* **Calif. Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all 548 death-row inmates, rejecting "state-sanctioned killing": **California Gov. **Gavin Newsom**[reduced](https://substack.com/redirect/31cb1350-faea-47ff-adb9-c3dee9f8bd85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the death sentences of every prisoner in the state to life without parole on Thursday. "State-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values," he said. With the sweep of his pen, Newsom cancelled about 25% of the nation's current death sentences. The incoming Gov.-elect **Xavier Becerra** has pledged to maintain a moratorium on executions that Newsom signed earlier in his term.
* **Bloomberg: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly considering exit from Trump administration:** Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** is weighing a possible departure from the Trump administration, Bloomberg [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/d83039cf-2b52-4912-ad5e-3ec76446f3d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The White House reportedly asked him to remain in the role. Rubio dismissed the Bloomberg report, telling the New York Times that it has "always been my plan" to stay until Trump's second term ends.

📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com
# Other International News
* **Paraguayan president Santiago Pe ña resigns, following collapse of Ueno bank and alleged corruption:** On Thursday, President of Paraguay Santiago Peña [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/50895272-5ec3-4724-b848-631cd891bcc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his resignation from the presidency. He said, in a recorded address, that he was stepping down with "the stability of our country, social peace, and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind." His resignation comes amid the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, which has left nearly half of Paraguayans unable to access their accounts. Minutes after resigning, he was impeached in a unanimous vote in the lower house of parliament. Lawmakers accused Peña of corruption, which he denies. Until March 2025, he was a shareholder of Ueno's parent company, Grupo Vazquez. The collapse of Ueno has already led to the resignation of the head of the Central Bank; led to the detention of eight Ueno bank executives; and sent Paraguay's sovereign-bond price tumbling. Ueno administered almost $850 million in public funds.
* **U.S. imposes new sanctions on Cuba:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c73e3743-b4af-4d59-a945-560f15464998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new sanctions on Cuban industries on Thursday, targeting its "crude oil shipping network," state-owned entities, and "China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces." Rubio accused Cuban military officials and "regime insiders" of profiting from "opaque offshore networks" and reiterated an unsubstantiated allegation that the island serves as "a staging ground for a global coalition of hostile anti-American actors." The Trump administration has repeatedly imposed sanctions on the island's industries and its political leaders, and it has maintained its suffocating blockade of fuel to the country.
* **Russia launches attacks on Ukraine 's energy infrastructure; death toll from earlier attack on Ukrainian aid center rises to 50+: **Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure [caused](https://substack.com/redirect/c923167c-a9fe-4630-b8cf-d28d12866bf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new power outages in seven regions, Reuters reported. Strikes late Thursday and early Friday hit Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Chernihiv.
* Separately on Friday, the death toll from a Monday attack on an aid center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia [rose](https://substack.com/redirect/638ca360-38af-4d24-b557-ca5cad249f42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to 53, according to Ukraine's emergency service. Local police said earlier this week that as many as 39 people could still be trapped under the rubble.
* **Indonesian police accuse a fourth official in alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto:** In an investigation into the wiretapping of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, police [named](https://substack.com/redirect/038e3c73-5128-4885-bb89-d857f979b10e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a fourth suspect on Friday, who they referred to by his initials, SU. Local media identified the suspect as Slamet Uliandi, who led the Criminal Investigation Agency's information and technology unit from 2021 to 2026. Earlier this week, police arrested three senior officers in connection with the wiretapping case, including Prabowo's chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo.
* **Macau pro-democracy activist sentenced to 12 years in prison:** A court in Macau, a special administrative region of China, [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/54f90931-1b57-4045-92ef-d7ec7e7cf789?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the pro-democracy activist and former lawmaker Au Kam-san to 12-and-a-half years in prison on Friday. After a national-security trial that was held behind closed doors, Au, 69, was found guilty of "subverting state power by spreading false information" during Macau's leadership elections in 2024. The court said that he worked with "hostile organizations" abroad and leaked confidential information to overseas groups. Human Rights Watch condemned the sentence, and urged the European Union and Portugal, which formerly controlled Macau, to push for Au's release.
* **Tanzania sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison:** On Friday, a three-judge panel in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/5640ad25-5e4a-424e-820e-4d858ea78c8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Tundu Lissu, leader of the political opposition, convicting him of incitement for statements he made before the 2025 elections. The panel dropped a treason charge that carried a possible punishment of death. Lissu, the leader of the Chadema Party, called the trial "political persecution," and accused the judges of coordinating with the government. "I was not charged with incitement but you judges are convicting me with it just to impress the person who gives you the titles," he told the court. "I believe these were directives." He was arrested before the elections of October 2025, which the ruling President Samia Suluhu Hassan went on to win with 98% of the vote. His near-total victory prompted mass protests, which the government subdued by killing thousands of people, according to the political opposition and human-rights groups. British and EU lawmakers said that the case against Lissu was politically motivated and demanded his release.
* **Egyptian soldiers killed in operation on Sudan border:** Two Egyptian army officers were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/7edfff49-e4e5-467f-b2b8-1bfa07521302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during a military crackdown on illegal gold mining along the border with Sudan, Reuters reported. One of the dead was a high-ranking officer. The Egyptian military began its campaign against illegal gold mining in June.

The IRGC said that the strait would "remain closed" until the U.S. meets Iran's seven conditions for a peace deal, adding that attempts by the U.S. military Central Command to force tankers through mined, unauthorized routes would result in "successive defeats." | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/32ab882af307/join-me-at-130-pm-on-saturday-in-redwood-city?e=c0babbc643)
---
| |
---
| | **You’re Invited: Bring the Kids! The Ice Age Comes Alive in Redwood City Saturday ** Join me this Saturday, November 7, for the plaque dedication and grand opening of the new HERO Natural History Gallery at the San Mateo County History Museum in Redwood City!

Bring your children and grandchildren to explore the Peninsula as it existed millions of years ago, discover the Ice Age animals that once roamed our region, see a reconstruction of a 15-million-year-old marine mammal and get up close to real mammoth and mastodon teeth! I'm especially proud to have championed a $500,000 Measure K grant to help make this exciting new gallery possible. I'll be joining museum officials and community members for the official unveiling at **1:30 p.m.** The free **History in Motion **celebration will also feature the opening of the spectacular Taube Family Carriage House and Automobile Gallery and Lora Mundi, the beautifully restored 1863 Lathrop-Connor-Mansfield House. **EVENT DETAILS** **When:** Saturday, November 7, 2026
**Time:** 1:30 p.m. – HERO Natural History Gallery unveiling
**Where:** San Mateo County History Museum
2200 Broadway, Second Floor Redwood City. I hope you'll bring the family and join us for this wonderful celebration! For more information, visit [https://historysmc.org](https://us.list-manage.com/16HY9qUKcgg?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02). Supervisor David J. Canepa
San Mateo County Board of Supervisors * * *

Press contact: Bill Silverfarb (415) 314-1737

body:
Thank you to our election workers. Virginia’s turnaround starts now.
| DELEGATE KAREN HAMILTON
---
Virginia House of Delegates, District 62
| Friends,
---
This election season asked a lot of all of us. I want to thank the many election and poll workers, and the volunteers who diligently worked throughout the year to fight for Virginia. Your long hours and steady commitment made a real difference.
It is an honor to serve the people of Virginia’s 62nd District, and this office belongs to you. Bills for next session are due at the end of this month. #### _**[Voters just handed Democrats a historic mandate, and the last thing we need is a party too afraid to use it. Endless Urgency is here to cut through the noise, expose corruption, and hold those in power accountable. Your support helps us keep these important conversations going and reach more people.
