_Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know._
* * *
I spent most of yesterday bouncing from one media hit to the next, and I swear I heard the same question in almost every one. After Tuesday's historic night for Democrats, anchors and pundits kept leaning in with the same furrowed brow: _Aren 't you worried Democrats are going to overreach?_
I had to laugh. Because I don't remember a single person in the media asking Donald Trump and the Republican Party whether they were worried about overreaching after 2024. Not one.
In fact, I remember the opposite. I remember the press buying into a big lie: that Donald Trump won the 2024 election with a mandate. He didn't. It was an incredibly close election. If roughly 100,000 votes go differently across a handful of states, Kamala Harris is president right now. That's not a mandate. That's a coin flip that landed on its edge.
Now look at this week. Democrats just had their best midterm since 1974. We flipped as many as nine Senate seats. We flipped Texas. Texas!
_That_ is a mandate. And we earned it.
We earned it by nominating incredible candidates who rose above a bad party brand. They focused on the issues the American people told us mattered, they listened, and they were responsive. And voters were not subtle about what they wanted. Fix the economy, because everything costs too much and the job market sucks. End this war. Get rid of these tariffs. And go after the corruption that has rotted our government from the inside out.
So let's be clear about what overreach would actually look like. If Democrats walk in on day one, act like we're popular, and then say, "We're impeaching Donald Trump," that would be an extraordinary waste of time. Nobody voted for a political sideshow.
But that's not the choice in front of us, and the media knows it. What the American people want is for Democrats to call corruption and greed in Washington what they are: an affordability issue. Every dollar skimmed off the top by the people running this government is a dollar coming out of your pocket.
Take Elon Musk. The richest man in the world spent a fortune to buy his way into the government, then helped himself to the American taxpayer while gutting programs working families rely on. And he's not alone. There's Trump and his family's crypto schemes, Jared Kushner's investment fund, and the bribes people like Tom Homan and Alina Habba are taking. It's a whole administration treating the government like a cash register.
Expose it. Investigate it. Follow it with real legal action and prosecute these people to the fullest extent of the law. Then pass serious ethics and campaign finance reform. Start in the first week with a ban on insider trading in Congress and the White House. Make it bipartisan. Any Republican who claims to care about corruption can prove it with their vote, and Democrats should be just as eager to throw out the corrupt assholes in our own party. Then dare Donald Trump to veto it.
That's not overreach. That's the job. That's literally what the American people elected us to do. I'm tired of Democrats being held to a standard Republicans have never had to meet. That doesn't mean abandoning our principles or breaking the rules to get things done. It means playing the game, playing it hard, and actually using our power to make people's lives better.
And if you think I'm spinning, go back and look at what voters said after 2024. In focus groups and in polling, the message was the same over and over: Democrats mean well, but they can't get anything done. They're not fighting for _me_. They're fighting for somebody else.
####
* * *
#### _**[Winning elections means nothing if the people we elect refuse to deliver. Endless Urgency is here to call out corruption, challenge the political establishment, and demand accountability from those in power, regardless of party. This work matters, and keeping it independent matters even more. Help us keep these conversations free and accessible to everyone for just $8/month:](https://substack.com/redirect/7b87080e-9e99-488a-8e99-665920c8e8f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/7b87080e-9e99-488a-8e99-665920c8e8f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
I didn't see one word about overreach in any of the voter feedback I read. People weren't mad that we did too much. They were pissed that we didn't do enough. Pissed that we didn't transform the country. Pissed that we were focused on the wrong things. Pissed we didn't deliver on what we campaigned on.
So the time to deliver is now. This is a generational opportunity, and we cannot waste it being afraid of our own shadow.
Yes, Republicans will hide behind the filibuster. Yes, Donald Trump will veto a lot of bills. Fine. Make them own every vote. Make Trump own every veto. Then send this new crop of young, sharp, media-savvy Democrats across the country to tell people exactly who is standing between them and a better life. Ask voters for more Democratic senators, more Democrats in the House, and a Democratic president in 2028.
And shut out the noise. The Republicans and their MAGA media machine are going to scream about "lawfare." _It 's so unfair! They're coming after America's favorite president!_ Ignore them. Nobody cares. People want criminals investigated, exposed, and prosecuted, whether they're in the Epstein class, the Trump family, or the billionaire class.
And when the media decides we're "going too far," when they start parroting Republican talking points the way they did all day yesterday, tune them out. Stand on business. Stand on our values. That's what most Democrats did in this midterm, and it worked.
Deliver immediate, tangible improvements to the material conditions of people's lives. Take this country back from the corrupt cabal of genuinely evil people who have been abusing it and profiting off of it for far too long.
Voters already told us what they want. They didn't hand us this majority so we could be careful with it. They handed it to us so we'd finally use it.
Deliver. That's the whole strategy.
With urgency,
--Mike

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

After many disappointments from the establishment in the 2024 election
cycle, the people demanded fighters.

So with your help, we at Justice Democrats answered their call.

recruited by Justice Democrats

We bet big by endorsing 15 progressive candidates running in Democratic
primaries for Congress all over the country. Some fought crowded battles
for open seats, while others took on corporate-backed Do-Nothing
Democratic incumbents whose time in power was finally up.

With grassroots support from people like you and our coalition, 2026 was
Justice Democrats’ most successful cycle EVER. Come January, at least 8
new Justice Democrats will head to Congress to join our 9 incumbents,
bringing the bloc to a total of 17 leaders. The race in CA-07 is still too
close to call, but we hope to add Mai Vang to the list and increase those
numbers by one!

These folks aren’t going to Congress for the sake of it: we and their
communities are sending them there to create real, lasting change within
the Democratic Party and our country as a whole. And not a single one of
them took a penny from corporate PACs — your donations fueled them to
victory.

Some of these incoming congressmembers may not have won or run at all had
it not been for everyday people like you nominating and supporting them
through our organization. Take it from them:

“I was recruited by Justice Democrats, an organization that works off of
community nominations, and they reached out to me and let me know that I
had been nominated. When I realized that my community trusted me with this
role, I knew that it was something that I needed to seriously consider.”
— Darializa Avila Chevalier (NY-13)

“When JD came in, they put me on the map. All of a sudden, people started
paying attention and saying this is a candidate who can win, and I won.”
— Dr. Adam Hamawy (NJ-12)

“We were able to win because of Justice Democrats. I didn’t win alone. I’m
gonna be going in with a whole group of people I’m really honored to be
fighting alongside for the better world I know we all believe in.”
— Melat Kiros (CO-01)

Now, our work is far from over.

Voters are done with watered-down half-measures and mealy-mouthed
proposals for incremental change from the powers that be in the Democratic
Party. Instead, they want their representatives to fight like hell for the
bold policies we deserve, like Medicare for All and an end to Israel’s
US-funded genocide.

Know that our bloc is ready to turn the pressure up on Party leadership
and give it their all to hold this fascist administration and its
corporate funders accountable while delivering long-overdue solutions to
the problems working-class people face every day.

name: Ken Martin
subject: I want to talk to you about trust today, Derek
body:
Democrats won because we earned back the trust of real people all over the country who are ready to see real change in their lives. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)
---
Derek, it’s Ken Martin. I’m reaching out with a few thoughts and reflections as we end this historic week. **On Tuesday, all across the country, the American people put their trust in Democrats up and down the ballot, in what shaped up to be one of the most successful midterm elections in Democratic Party _history_.** It’s my mission as the chair of the Democratic National Committee to make sure that Democrats never take that trust for granted. I know I share that goal with the thousands of newly elected Democratic representatives across the country who are ready to create real change for the people in their states, districts, and communities. **Because Derek, none of the wins we saw on Tuesday were by chance. Democrats won because they have spent the past two years working overtime to earn back people’s trust.** In 2024, we faced a disillusioned public who felt like their government didn’t understand or stand for them. Democrats lost ground with communities we had relied on for decades, many of whom either voted Republican or stayed home. Since then, the DNC and Democrats nationwide have worked hard to repair those relationships by connecting with people on the ground — at their doors, on the phones, and in their communities. We made it a priority to _listen_ first, and to ask about what you wanted to see from your representatives. We didn’t wait until the few months before Election Day, we started our outreach the minute Trump took office. **And it worked.** In 2025, we saw major victories in states like Virginia, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. _And importantly,**we didn’t stop showing up after Election Day.**_ Democrats in Virginia and New Jersey _got to work_ and passed meaningful statewide legislation to invest in affordable housing, deliver property tax relief, advance gun safety legislation, and secure funding to help people transition to cleaner energy sources. **And while Democrats in government got to work, Democratic candidates kept working around the clock to organize and talk to voters about what matters.** I am so proud of my team here at the DNC. On top of supporting over 10,000 Democratic campaigns this year, we also launched organizing initiatives, like _Local Listeners_ and _When We Count_ , to reach disillusioned Democrats who sat out last cycle and register _thousands_ of new Democratic voters. **Derek, it was because of innovative programs like these, and the hard work of campaigns and volunteers across the country, that Democrats were able to compete and win at _every level of government this Tuesday._** So I want us to take a moment and remember why this happened:_**People.** People who now have a sense that maybe, just maybe, some better days are ahead._ Democrats won because we earned back the trust of people all over the country who believe in us to deliver real change in their lives. **You — our grassroots team — made this possible. This victory belongs to all of you._But the work doesn’t end now._** Right now, newly-elected Democrats across the country are preparing to be sworn into office and get to work for their communities. And I want you to know that my team and I are listening to what folks are saying across the country — **we know that winning the White House in 2028 is dependent on Democrats delivering real change that Americans can _feel_ over the next two years.** We take seriously the level of trust that you’ve given us this year, and it’s time to continue building the depth of that trust with the way we govern. **That said, I also want to be clear about what my team is focused on, and that’s continuing to build on our winning infrastructure and investment strategies so that we can elect our next Democratic President and hold onto Congress.[If you’re ready and willing to support that effort, I hope you’ll consider chipping in a few bucks today. We’d be so grateful to have you on our team again.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261106_10248_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO) **[SUPPORT OUR WORK](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98376?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.YufugX&c1=7.SxDHGm&c2=em_20261106_10248_fr.47BODs&t=7&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)** **If you can’t donate today, we understand, and we will continue working day in and day out to keep developing trust with grassroots Democrats like you, Derek.** Thank you again, for everything. We couldn’t have done it without you. Ken Ken Martin
Chair
Democratic National Committee | [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&amount=7&refcode=em_20261106_10248_fr&t=8&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)
---

_If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

This past year, Louisiana was ground zero for MAGA's attack on Black voting rights.

Within hours of the decision, our Governor called a state of emergency to stop an ongoing election.

**Thank You for Your Support PA-11**
Thank you...
To the voters of Lancaster and York Counties, our Democratic leadership, our state and congressional candidates, my campaign team and my family.
To our volunteers and everyone who contributed: you gave your time, your talents, and your heart. You knocked on doors, listened to neighbors, and helped turn a campaign into a community. **Our campaign shifted the PA-11 district 10.5 points toward Democrats as compared with the 2024 presidential election. We moved the needle - that 's no small feat and you should be proud of that!** Last night’s election result does not erase that progress, your work, or the connections we’ve built.
Here in Pennsylvania, the words “life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness” became part of our nation’s founding promise. Making that promise real in everyday life is the work of generations. It cannot begin or end with one election.
An election decides who holds office. It does not define our journey or the future of our democracy. The needs that you shared with me remain: a healthier economy, stronger schools, health care, immigration reform, support for farms and working people, and the freedom to make decisions about our bodies and whom we love. **These are reasons to keep working – not to walk away.**
This campaign is one chapter in a much longer effort to make government work for the people. That effort continues. The work ahead still matters: restoring trust and accountability, protecting the programs our communities depend on, and choosing compassion over cruelty.
Mending our country begins with listening to one another, especially when we disagree. Ask a neighbor what matters to them. Listen to understand – not just to answer. We can stand firmly for our values and still respect one another’s dignity. **Our differences do not change the fact that we are still neighbors.**
I implore you to keep showing up for your communities.
Volunteer, attend a community meeting, check on a neighbor, and make room for voices too often ignored. **We do not need to hold office to make a difference**. I will keep listening and showing up, and I hope you will join me.
Take a breath and take care of each other. Then, when you are ready, **stay involved**. Keep organizing, voting, **and holding elected leaders accountable**. Democracy is something we practice every day – not something that ends on election night.
Thank you for your courage, generosity, and belief that government should work for the people. **One loss does not end our movement. We will keep moving forward together**.
Thank you, Lancaster and York Counties. **Our work continues.**
\- Nancy Mannion

The slaughter of the Athenians at the Assinarus River by Syracuse in 413 B.C., as recorded by the historian Thucydides in his _History of the Peloponnesian War,_ is one of the best passages of human writing _._ The peerless Thucydides __ records the gruesome end of the Athenian era of empire with a visceral gore rivaled only by the macabre cannibalism of the Old Testament. The passage remains the most vivid depiction of the utter human despair and desperation brought about by war.
The great historian tells us the fleeing Athenians -- having foolishly overextended their military campaign into Sicily -- found themselves suddenly surrounded, driven back by a superior force, and exhausted into disorder by starvation and chaos. The anguished soldiers retreated helter-skelter and stumbled into the river. Forgetting the dire threat of the pursuing Syracusans, the hoplites hurled themselves into the river in a frenzy to quench their desperate thirst.
As the master historian conveys it:
> _When they reached the river, they plunged in with no order left. Each man wanted to cross first, while the enemy pressed them and made the crossing harder. Forced to move in a mass, they fell against one another and trampled one another down. Some were killed at once among the spears and equipment; others, tangled in it, were swept downstream. The Syracusans took positions on the far bank --which was steep--and shot down at the Athenians from above. Most of the Athenians drank eagerly, jostling one another in the hollow of the riverbed. The Peloponnesians came down after them and slaughtered chiefly those in the river. **The water was soon fouled, but even so they drank it, muddied and bloodied; many fought over it.**_
That is, so desperate was the plight of the routed Athenian army -- once an empire the envy of the Mediterranean world -- that its humiliated soldiers spent their dying moments slurping the blood of fallen comrades without thought of the murder raining down upon their heads.
Now... at the risk of sounding overly dramatic, the reason this passage comes to mind is because of the result of the elections. You need not have read much Thucydides to understand which political party is lying in puddles of blood and mire, electorally speaking.

On the national front, it seems plain to me that President Donald Trump's decision to launch a war of choice against Iran on behalf of Israel while the vast majority of Americans were primarily concerned with affording food and housing was the proximate cause of the landslide. If Trump had focused on doing the things that he said he was going to do during his campaign, as opposed to doing things that he campaigned against, the Republicans might have lost some races, but the damage would not have been so severe. Broadly speaking, these election results are what happens when millions of conservatives and independents decide that perhaps voting isn't really worth it.

Maine, in some ways, bucked the national trend. Now, this map could be the result of the tens of millions of dollars that flowed into the state on behalf of Susan Collins, but I'm choosing for the sake of my own self-esteem to believe that Maine's an outlier here because it's the only state with The Maine Wire conducting aggressive investigative reporting. That being said... the Maine GOP has been, once again, humiliated into despair.
As I write this, tens of thousands of lifelong Mainers -- Old Mainers, you might call them, irrespective of their age -- are eyeing the exits. Florida? New Hampshire? Tennessee? Is there somewhere you can run to where the schools won't be run for the benefit of corrupt teachers unions and transgender radicals? Is there another state that won't steal your money to enrich the friends and family of politicians, while simultaneously protecting organized crime and racketeering operations? Are there places where the cities aren't overrun with fentanyl-brained zombies, scaggy-armed with taxpayer-subsidized syringes, leaking their HIV-positive blood all over the children's playground?
Those who've placed Donald Trump at the center of their existence and allowed their hatred of him to animate their every impulse can be happy for a moment. But their lives aren't really going to change, except for perhaps they'll need something new to replenish their hatred in a few years. I'm sure J.D. Vance and Marco Rubio are up for the task. But for those who haven't been hanging out on overpasses wagging foreign flags, the question over every dinner table is whether Maine has crossed the socialist event horizon. That is, has Maine veered so close to the sucking black-hole maw of centrally planned corruption that there will be no reversing the economic, demographic, and cultural decline.
The answer to that question will depend, in large part, on the beleaguered conservative movement, if you can call it a movement. Those of the conservative disposition find themselves, once again, confused and leaderless, relegated to super minority status, destined to be ruled by DSA Democrats from the failed cities of Portland, Lewiston, and Bangor. We conservatives are like the Athenians, drowning in blood and mire, except we never even had a fond empire to remember, apart from the good ole days when Maine actually had an economy that wasn't wholly dependent on government spending and political patronage.
Whether the conservative movement can coalesce into a viable insurgency will become apparent over the next few weeks. Today, Republican senators and Republican House members will select leaders from their diminished ranks. Similarly, the chairman of the Maine Republican Party will appoint members of a nominating committee on Nov. 15, the beginning of the process that will determine whether current Maine GOP Chairman Jim Deyermond gets another two-year term. That party election will come in January, around the time the 133rd State Legislature is convening.

As the conservatives of Maine begin to navigate the next two years, it's worth looking back at the unlearned lessons of the past. To return to Thucydides:
> _It will be enough for me, however, if these words of mine are judged useful by those who want to understand clearly the events which happened in the past and which (human nature being what it is) will, at some time or other and in much the same ways, be repeated in the future._
In other words, Thucydides wrote and studied history primarily because human nature's immutability means that past events offer a preview into future events. What happened before is a guide to what will happen in the future. So with that as a starting point, we must begin by asking: What has happened within the Maine Republican Party that has produced such a miserable record of failure? How did Maine Republicans get wiped out by a party that has, over the last eight years, made life worse for Mainers by every conceivable metric?
The origin of our current predicament could be found in any of the post-LePage years. But I place it in the Covid-19 period, when the Republican Party ceded all manner of authority -- executive, moral, legal -- to Gov. Janet Mills. With all prudence cast aside, and federal Biden Bucks raining on Maine, Mills was able to buy off every pet constituency. That includes the no-bid contracts she used to secretly construct a political machine that would greatly aid in her re-election in 2022, as I've detailed at length with our reporting on Gateway Community Services.
As some of you may recall, in 2022, the consultants and campaign managers and analysts (all of whom make far more money than anyone at the Maine Wire) were predicting a "Red Wave." Commentator Phil Harriman predicted a full sweep for the red team, with 81 seats in the House, while then-BDN columnist and Maine Policy Institute CEO Matt Gagnon offered a slightly more measured view that there was a chance to flip the Senate. The nominal leaders of the Maine Republican Party were scheming and jockeying for who might become the Speaker of the House or the President of the Senate before the ballots had even been cast. I'm sure I was just as bullish -- or naive -- about the red wave, but I had the wisdom (or cowardice) not to write down any predictions.
Wrapped in the mirage that "she kept us safe," Mills defeated ex-Gov-now-Congressman Paul LePage -- both because LePage never directly assailed her totalitarian and unscientific pandemic policies and because he failed to articulate a sound abortion stance. Mills's second term, combined with an NGO complex constructed entirely on taxpayer money, made a formidable coalition. From 2020 to 2024, and perhaps still today, the gay race communists successfully harassed all good men and women out of politics with threats to ruin their lives or businesses for espousing crazy ideas like, maybe high school girls should not be forced to compete athletically against males who say they girls. So just as the Democratic machine was solidifying its formal political power, leftist cultural aggression sent conservatives into retreat.

Of course, 2022 was the first of several dismal performances for professional Republicans. The red wave was actually a red humiliation, with GOP candidates shellacked back into minority status here in Maine. Having just taken over TheMaineWire.com, I offered some candid observations about what I'd seen in the lead-up to the unexpected defenestration of the would-be Republican kings who were still measuring leadership office drapes by the time the polls started dousing them in reality. You can go back to the post-mortem I wrote in 2022 following that disastrous election. In that controversial piece of writing, I correctly predicted what Maine was about to experience over the next four years.
> [Gov. Janet] Mills could reverse course on her campaign promises, hike the income tax to 10 percent, encircle Swan's Island with offshore windmills, legalize fourth trimester abortion, and put a Planned Parenthood in every county, and I'm not sure Republicans in Augusta would be able to win majorities two years from now.
In fact, Gov. Mills and the Democratic majorities did raise our taxes, they did protect costly green energy scams, and they did impose the most extreme late-term infanticide law in Western Civilization. They imposed harsh gun control, expanded gender ideology into virtually every public space, and created an express superhighway for noncitizens to get welfare vis-a-vis the "Office of New Americans." Welfare fraud exploded almost exponentially while Asian transnational organized crime ran riot through rural Maine. Taxes soared and spending soared even more, leaving the Democrat coalition of the 133rd Legislature with a more than $1 billion deficit, which they will invariably tackle by hiking taxes even more on the handful of productive working people who've yet to escape this state.
My Jeremiah-like warnings fell on deaf ears. Here's the important point from four years ago that went ignored:
> The dwindling few Republicans who will inhabit the State House this next legislative session need a clean slate. Otherwise, they might as well spare taxpayers the per diem and stay at home. Anyone remotely connected to the old leadership must step back and allow a new generation of conservatives to lead the party. This includes staffers in the House and Senate GOP offices...
>
> I know the talent pool for Republican operatives is shallow in Maine, but we're at rock bottom here... As for new leadership, placing young, media savvy, strategically minded conservatives in charge is the only possible path to becoming relevant again...
None of this was particularly insightful or brilliant. After a professional football team goes multiple seasons without a single win, they typically change up the coach, the quarterback, and the strategy. But Republican leaders -- whoever those are or were -- did nothing of the sort. No new staff was hired. No new leaders were elevated. No new ideas or tactics were deployed. The same tired hands wrote the same tired scripts to blather out on the same AM radio signals to the same tired audience. Throughout the next legislative sessions, Republicans plowed through with the same perma-minority mindset that believes, falsely, that the extreme leftists who wear the Democrat name tags are interested in good-faith negotiations over policies that will improve the lives of Mainers. (Pro tip: They aren't.)
These leftist extremists who operate under the banner of the Maine Democratic Party are only interested in power, control, and money, with maybe a few naive youngsters still stupid enough to believe that "social justice" was ever a real thing. They will lie, cheat, and steal to get more power, control, and money, and you cannot negotiate in good faith with Democratic politicians and radicalized DSA staffers who will lie, cheat, and steal to advance their narrow, selfish interests. Yet, like Charlie Brown with the football, Republicans plodded ahead in the last three legislative sessions again and again for a kick, only to cry about sore asses on the House floor with speeches no one listens to and no one cares about. Meanwhile, Lucy snickers with her friends, counting stacks of cash, and chortling about stupid and gullible the conservatives.
That's not the only prescient wisdom I dispensed four years ago. Here's another bit:
> If a Republican donor wanted to make a substantial difference in future state elections, he should consider making a large donation only on the condition that it be used to construct an elite early voting and mail-in voting apparatus. Voting in modern elections now takes place over several weeks. Conservatives may not like it, it may open the door for fraud and bureaucratic shenanigans, but it's a reality. These are the rules and this is the playing field. If Republicans want to win, they must show up early, not just on game day.
Whether a GOP mega donor stepped up to the plate to fund such an effort, I don't know. Judging by the chronic indebtedness of the Maine Republican Party, I'm guessing no. Also: the results are right there in the early voting numbers. From 2022 to 2026, Republicans were clobbered in the early voting contest, even though they did make some slight progress in closing the gap. In 2022, Democrats had 64,622 more early voters than the Republicans did, a lead that dropped to 41,488 in 2026. However, Republicans managed to have 60,174 absentee ballot requests four years ago but just 31,618 this year. Very obviously, no concerted effort has been made to level the playing field in early voting. Trump bears most blame for this. His imbecilic pooh-poohing of early voting was a generational mistake. But he's not the only Republican with a platform. Who knows where the GOP might be sitting if they'd embraced some early voting initiatives, as conservative groups in other states have done so successfully. Indeed, if Republicans had embraced early voting with any kind of success, Democrats like Shenna Bellows might be out there condemning early voting as undemocratic!
Four years after my unheeded call for a better early voting program, I would also recommend that Maine conservatives embrace large-language models as a tool to help them fight from a minority and poorly financed position. Used properly, new and emerging technology could be the equivalent of giving the Mujahideen shoulder-fired rockets to take on the vastly superior Soviet forces. Of course, this would require them to listen to my earlier advice about hiring some staff who weren't already collecting Social Security when the Soviet Union was mucking around in Afghanistan. In case I haven't made myself clear, the GOP caucuses in the State House need to utterly gut the current staffer ranks and consultant ranks and come up with some brand new talent if they want anything to change. If they continue to pay the same staff and the same consultants, they will continue to get the same results.

The other area where the Maine Republican Party has seriously disadvantaged itself and must reform if it wishes to alter the trajectory of the state is structural and financial. Briefly, the Maine GOP's approach to raising and spending money is scattered and non-strategic. Compounding the problem, Republicans in Maine have a reputation among the donor class for being a group of greedy over-promisers who will both steal your money _and_ lose. Word spreads fast among GOP donors. One untrustworthy consultant or politician can create a negative feedback loop that leads to even good or worthy causes being ignored because of the perception that conservatives in Maine are not to be trusted. Earning back that trust will require a radical reformation of how the party operates.
Before explaining the money game at play in state politics, it's useful to understand a few things about how state legislative races are funded. Whether you like it or not, political campaigns require communicating ideas, and communicating ideas typically requires money. For both political parties, there are three principal political committees that endure regardless of individual personalities. These are used to raise money for the party state committees and legislative caucuses. On each side, there's the state committee, the state senate caucus committee, and the state house committee. Yes, there are dozens of other interest group funds and leadership PACs, but those are of less importance to this discussion than the big three central committees that set tone and strategy for party operations.
The most obvious fact that emerges from a cursory review of campaign finance documents is that the Maine Democratic Party and the Maine Republican Party are operated and governed according to completely different rules, philosophies, and strategies. The election results are the supreme judge of which party has the more effective mode of operation. Demonstrably, the Maine Democrats are running a more successful fundraising operation than the Republicans (which typically happens when a party can actually deliver legislation for pharmaceutical lobbies and other corporate interests), but the left-wing party is also much better at managing and deploying that cash to earn votes.
On the Democratic side, the House and Senate committees engage in regular fundraising. They wine and dine lobbyists, hold special events, and do the routine business of raising campaign cash. The expenditures are typically limited to the cost of fundraising: mail, payroll, office equipment, food and rent. But the key part is that eventually, a big chunk of the money raised by that committee is transferred to the central Democratic State Committee. The same goes for the Democratic Senate Committee. Regardless of who is running either political committee, the expenses are lean and all of the money flows to the central committee.
From 2018 through the available 2026 filings, the Democratic Senate and House committees reported payments to the state party of $10.51 million and $5.22 million, respectively, compared with $1.46 million and $216,640 from their Republican counterparts. The Democrats' current charter puts finances under a Finance Subcommittee and the annual budget before the Democratic State Committee. It also establishes a coordinated campaign committee for voter identification, absentee ballots, turnout, and voter files.
Once the money hits the central committee, the decisions about how to allocate that money are not made by a single chairman or executive director. Instead, the Democratic Party is governed by a committee so that many sets of hands and eyes have oversight over how campaign cash is being distributed. That's important for a few reasons. For one, it ensures that a shared and overarching strategic vision is overseeing the allocation of resources. That makes it less likely that a vulnerable incumbent will not get support or a candidate with a comfortable lead will get resources that could be spent elsewhere. Equally importantly, committee decision making over the allocation of resources ensures that campaign contributions are not steered for the benefit of narrow financial interests.
The spending mix is different, too. The campaign finance reports show Democrats reported $4.46 million for mailers and printed literature against Republicans' $1.47 million, and $4.65 million for payroll and staff against $1.41 million. Republicans reported $9.29 million for television and cable against Democrats' $1.93 million. That is a stark difference in what the committees bought. Of course, there's some overlap between the state campaign finance filings and the federal campaign finance filings, so these numbers aren't exactly perfect. But the records suffice to show significant differences in how the two parties raise, manage, and deploy resources.
The clearest way the Maine GOP could reform its various fundraising organs is by establishing governance via committee so that narrow interests can't dominate campaign spending in ways that are guided by something other than winning. Because let's face it: politics is a nasty game. It's even nastier behind the curtain with the consultants living that feast-or-famine lifestyle, hustling from election to election. Then you add to that the skim. For those who don't know, politics is filled with people who make money by skimming. They skim the fundraising. They skim the junk mail that clutters your mailbox and goes right in the garbage. They skim the television ads and the radio ads and the social media ads. A politician hires a fundraising consultant who helps him raise $500,000 for his campaign? Well, the fundraising consultant gets a slice of that treasure chest, even if all he did was provide a Rolodex and some talking points. Now, say that politician wants to spend $250,000 on television ads. Somewhere in the middle a political consultant is getting a skim -- could be 15%, 20%, or even more. Who's keeping track of that skim? Usually the one doing the skimming. But that's how political campaigns raise campaign cash and transform it into communications that reach voters.
There's nothing inherently wrong with the skim -- everyone has to eat -- but it does create perverse incentives to deploy resources in ways that prioritize something other than winning. For example, if you're getting the TV skim, you're probably going to recommend lots of TV. Ditto if you're getting the mail skim. If it turns out that paying young activists to door knock is the more effective strategy, but you're not getting a skim on the door-knocking... well, the door-knocking might get pushed to the back burner. Whoever emerges as the next crop of Republican leaders needs to take a careful look at who had been skimming and whether that skimming has been oriented toward the good of the party or toward narrower interests. Even if winning has been the top priority, a party that purports to back meritocracy ought to find a way to swiftly replace professionals with demonstrated losing records.
The last thing I'll say, at the risk of sounding too harsh on Maine's Republicans, considering that they're still drowning in their own blood and mire while spears and arrows rain down on their heads, is that they are vastly outmatched not only by a better funded and better run Democratic Party, but also by a humongous leftist dark-money operation that works hand-in-glove with official Democrats to advance the same goals, often in more vicious ways. I'm talking, of course, about the constellation of 501(c)3 and 501(c)4 and other NGOs funded by George Soros, Hansjorg Wyss, Pierre Omidyar, and many other leftist billionaires.
Unlike the Maine Republicans, the Maine Democrats have both the Bangor and Portland newspapers effectively serving as their communications and propaganda organs. And they have dozens and dozens of NGOs that get both dark-money funding _and_ taxpayer dollars. The playing field is tilted and the game is unfair. Conservatives can either whine about it, get better at politics, or move to New Hampshire.

Nov 6 | | | | | | | | | | | The slaughter of the Athenians at the Assinarus River by Syracuse in 413 B.C., as recorded by the historian Thucydides in his History of the Peloponnesian War, is one of the best passages of human writing . The peerless Thucydides records the gruesome end of the Athenian era of empire with a visceral gore rivaled only by the macabre cannibalism of the Old Testament. The passage remains the most vivid depiction of the utter human despair and desperation brought about by war. The great historian tells us the fleeing Athenians -- having foolishly overextended their military campaign into Sicily -- found themselves suddenly surrounded, driven back by a superior force, and exhausted into disorder by starvation and chaos. The anguished soldiers retreated helter-skelter and stumbled into the river. Forgetting the dire threat of the pursuing Syracusans, the hoplites hurled themselves into the river in a frenzy to quench their desperate thirst. As the master historian conveys it: When they reached the river, they plunged in with no order left. Each man wanted to cross first, while the enemy pressed them and made the crossing harder. Forced to move in a mass, they fell against one another and trampled one another down. Some were killed at once among the spears and equipment; others, tangled in it, were swept downstream. The Syracusans took positions on the far bank --which was steep--and shot down at the Athenians from above. Most of the Athenians drank eagerly, jostling one another in the hollow of the riverbed. The Peloponnesians came down after them and slaughtered chiefly those in the river. The water was soon fouled, but even so they drank it, muddied and bloodied; many fought over it. That is, so desperate was the plight of the routed Athenian army -- once an empire the envy of the Mediterranean world -- that its humiliated soldiers spent their dying moments slurping the blood of fallen comrades without thought of the murder raining down upon their heads. Now... at the risk of sounding overly dramatic, the reason this passage comes to mind is because of the result of the elections. You need not have read much Thucydides to understand which political party is lying in puddles of blood and mire, electorally speaking. Sign up for The Robinson Report. It's free! On the national front, it seems plain to me that President Donald Trump's decision to launch a war of choice against Iran on behalf of Israel while the vast majority of Americans were primarily concerned with affording food and housing was the proximate cause of the landslide. If Trump had focused on doing the things that he said he was going to do during his campaign, as opposed to doing things that he campaigned against, the Republicans might have lost some races, but the damage would not have been so severe. Broadly speaking, these election results are what happens when millions of conservatives and independents decide that perhaps voting isn't really worth it. | | ---|---|--- Maine, in some ways, bucked the national trend. Now, this map could be the result of the tens of millions of dollars that flowed into the state on behalf of Susan Collins, but I'm choosing for the sake of my own self-esteem to believe that Maine's an outlier here because it's the only state with The Maine Wire conducting aggressive investigative reporting. That being said... the Maine GOP has been, once again, humiliated into despair. As I write this, tens of thousands of lifelong Mainers -- Old Mainers, you might call them, irrespective of their age -- are eyeing the exits. Florida? New Hampshire? Tennessee? Is there somewhere you can run to where the schools won't be run for the benefit of corrupt teachers unions and transgender radicals? Is there another state that won't steal your money to enrich the friends and family of politicians, while simultaneously protecting organized crime and racketeering operations? Are there places where the cities aren't overrun with fentanyl-brained zombies, scaggy-armed with taxpayer-subsidized syringes, leaking their HIV-positive blood all over the children's playground? Those who've placed Donald Trump at the center of their existence and allowed their hatred of him to animate their every impulse can be happy for a moment. But their lives aren't really going to change, except for perhaps they'll need something new to replenish their hatred in a few years. I'm sure J.D. Vance and Marco Rubio are up for the task. But for those who haven't been hanging out on overpasses wagging foreign flags, the question over every dinner table is whether Maine has crossed the socialist event horizon. That is, has Maine veered so close to the sucking black-hole maw of centrally planned corruption that there will be no reversing the economic, demographic, and cultural decline. The answer to that question will depend, in large part, on the beleaguered conservative movement, if you can call it a movement. Those of the conservative disposition find themselves, once again, confused and leaderless, relegated to super minority status, destined to be ruled by DSA Democrats from the failed cities of Portland, Lewiston, and Bangor. We conservatives are like the Athenians, drowning in blood and mire, except we never even had a fond empire to remember, apart from the good ole days when Maine actually had an economy that wasn't wholly dependent on government spending and political patronage. Whether the conservative movement can coalesce into a viable insurgency will become apparent over the next few weeks. Today, Republican senators and Republican House members will select leaders from their diminished ranks. Similarly, the chairman of the Maine Republican Party will appoint members of a nominating committee on Nov. 15, the beginning of the process that will determine whether current Maine GOP Chairman Jim Deyermond gets another two-year term. That party election will come in January, around the time the 133rd State Legislature is convening. As the conservatives of Maine begin to navigate the next two years, it's worth looking back at the unlearned lessons of the past. To return to Thucydides: It will be enough for me, however, if these words of mine are judged useful by those who want to understand clearly the events which happened in the past and which (human nature being what it is) will, at some time or other and in much the same ways, be repeated in the future. In other words, Thucydides wrote and studied history primarily because human nature's immutability means that past events offer a preview into future events. What happened before is a guide to what will happen in the future. So with that as a starting point, we must begin by asking: What has happened within the Maine Republican Party that has produced such a miserable record of failure? How did Maine Republicans get wiped out by a party that has, over the last eight years, made life worse for Mainers by every conceivable metric? The origin of our current predicament could be found in any of the post-LePage years. But I place it in the Covid-19 period, when the Republican Party ceded all manner of authority -- executive, moral, legal -- to Gov. Janet Mills. With all prudence cast aside, and federal Biden Bucks raining on Maine, Mills was able to buy off every pet constituency. That includes the no-bid contracts she used to secretly construct a political machine that would greatly aid in her re-election in 2022, as I've detailed at length with our reporting on Gateway Community Services. As some of you may recall, in 2022, the consultants and campaign managers and analysts (all of whom make far more money than anyone at the Maine Wire) were predicting a "Red Wave." Commentator Phil Harriman predicted a full sweep for the red team, with 81 seats in the House, while then-BDN columnist and Maine Policy Institute CEO Matt Gagnon offered a slightly more measured view that there was a chance to flip the Senate. The nominal leaders of the Maine Republican Party were scheming and jockeying for who might become the Speaker of the House or the President of the Senate before the ballots had even been cast. I'm sure I was just as bullish -- or naive -- about the red wave, but I had the wisdom (or cowardice) not to write down any predictions. Wrapped in the mirage that "she kept us safe," Mills defeated ex-Gov-now-Congressman Paul LePage -- both because LePage never directly assailed her totalitarian and unscientific pandemic policies and because he failed to articulate a sound abortion stance. Mills's second term, combined with an NGO complex constructed entirely on taxpayer money, made a formidable coalition. From 2020 to 2024, and perhaps still today, the gay race communists successfully harassed all good men and women out of politics with threats to ruin their lives or businesses for espousing crazy ideas like, maybe high school girls should not be forced to compete athletically against males who say they girls. So just as the Democratic machine was solidifying its formal political power, leftist cultural aggression sent conservatives into retreat. Of course, 2022 was the first of several dismal performances for professional Republicans. The red wave was actually a red humiliation, with GOP candidates shellacked back into minority status here in Maine. Having just taken over TheMaineWire.com, I offered some candid observations about what I'd seen in the lead-up to the unexpected defenestration of the would-be Republican kings who were still measuring leadership office drapes by the time the polls started dousing them in reality. You can go back to the post-mortem I wrote in 2022 following that disastrous election. In that controversial piece of writing, I correctly predicted what Maine was about to experience over the next four years. [Gov. Janet] Mills could reverse course on her campaign promises, hike the income tax to 10 percent, encircle Swan's Island with offshore windmills, legalize fourth trimester abortion, and put a Planned Parenthood in every county, and I'm not sure Republicans in Augusta would be able to win majorities two years from now. In fact, Gov. Mills and the Democratic majorities did raise our taxes, they did protect costly green energy scams, and they did impose the most extreme late-term infanticide law in Western Civilization. They imposed harsh gun control, expanded gender ideology into virtually every public space, and created an express superhighway for noncitizens to get welfare vis-a-vis the "Office of New Americans." Welfare fraud exploded almost exponentially while Asian transnational organized crime ran riot through rural Maine. Taxes soared and spending soared even more, leaving the Democrat coalition of the 133rd Legislature with a more than $1 billion deficit, which they will invariably tackle by hiking taxes even more on the handful of productive working people who've yet to escape this state. My Jeremiah-like warnings fell on deaf ears. Here's the important point from four years ago that went ignored: The dwindling few Republicans who will inhabit the State House this next legislative session need a clean slate. Otherwise, they might as well spare taxpayers the per diem and stay at home. Anyone remotely connected to the old leadership must step back and allow a new generation of conservatives to lead the party. This includes staffers in the House and Senate GOP offices... I know the talent pool for Republican operatives is shallow in Maine, but we're at rock bottom here... As for new leadership, placing young, media savvy, strategically minded conservatives in charge is the only possible path to becoming relevant again... None of this was particularly insightful or brilliant. After a professional football team goes multiple seasons without a single win, they typically change up the coach, the quarterback, and the strategy. But Republican leaders -- whoever those are or were -- did nothing of the sort. No new staff was hired. No new leaders were elevated. No new ideas or tactics were deployed. The same tired hands wrote the same tired scripts to blather out on the same AM radio signals to the same tired audience. Throughout the next legislative sessions, Republicans plowed through with the same perma-minority mindset that believes, falsely, that the extreme leftists who wear the Democrat name tags are interested in good-faith negotiations over policies that will improve the lives of Mainers. (Pro tip: They aren't.) These leftist extremists who operate under the banner of the Maine Democratic Party are only interested in power, control, and money, with maybe a few naive youngsters still stupid enough to believe that "social justice" was ever a real thing. They will lie, cheat, and steal to get more power, control, and money, and you cannot negotiate in good faith with Democratic politicians and radicalized DSA staffers who will lie, cheat, and steal to advance their narrow, selfish interests. Yet, like Charlie Brown with the football, Republicans plodded ahead in the last three legislative sessions again and again for a kick, only to cry about sore asses on the House floor with speeches no one listens to and no one cares about. Meanwhile, Lucy snickers with her friends, counting stacks of cash, and chortling about stupid and gullible the conservatives. That's not the only prescient wisdom I dispensed four years ago. Here's another bit: If a Republican donor wanted to make a substantial difference in future state elections, he should consider making a large donation only on the condition that it be used to construct an elite early voting and mail-in voting apparatus. Voting in modern elections now takes place over several weeks. Conservatives may not like it, it may open the door for fraud and bureaucratic shenanigans, but it's a reality. These are the rules and this is the playing field. If Republicans want to win, they must show up early, not just on game day. Whether a GOP mega donor stepped up to the plate to fund such an effort, I don't know. Judging by the chronic indebtedness of the Maine Republican Party, I'm guessing no. Also: the results are right there in the early voting numbers. From 2022 to 2026, Republicans were clobbered in the early voting contest, even though they did make some slight progress in closing the gap. In 2022, Democrats had 64,622 more early voters than the Republicans did, a lead that dropped to 41,488 in 2026. However, Republicans managed to have 60,174 absentee ballot requests four years ago but just 31,618 this year. Very obviously, no concerted effort has been made to level the playing field in early voting. Trump bears most blame for this. His imbecilic pooh-poohing of early voting was a generational mistake. But he's not the only Republican with a platform. Who knows where the GOP might be sitting if they'd embraced some early voting initiatives, as conservative groups in other states have done so successfully. Indeed, if Republicans had embraced early voting with any kind of success, Democrats like Shenna Bellows might be out there condemning early voting as undemocratic! Four years after my unheeded call for a better early voting program, I would also recommend that Maine conservatives embrace large-language models as a tool to help them fight from a minority and poorly financed position. Used properly, new and emerging technology could be the equivalent of giving the Mujahideen shoulder-fired rockets to take on the vastly superior Soviet forces. Of course, this would require them to listen to my earlier advice about hiring some staff who weren't already collecting Social Security when the Soviet Union was mucking around in Afghanistan. In case I haven't made myself clear, the GOP caucuses in the State House need to utterly gut the current staffer ranks and consultant ranks and come up with some brand new talent if they want anything to change. If they continue to pay the same staff and the same consultants, they will continue to get the same results. This Substack is reader-supported. Equally importantly, committee decision making over the allocation of resources ensures that campaign contributions are not steered for the benefit of narrow financial interests. The spending mix is different, too. The campaign finance reports show Democrats reported $4.46 million for mailers and printed literature against Republicans' $1.47 million, and $4.65 million for payroll and staff against $1.41 million. Republicans reported $9.29 million for television and cable against Democrats' $1.93 million. That is a stark difference in what the committees bought. Of course, there's some overlap between the state campaign finance filings and the federal campaign finance filings, so these numbers aren't exactly perfect. But the records suffice to show significant differences in how the two parties raise, manage, and deploy resources. The clearest way the Maine GOP could reform its various fundraising organs is by establishing governance via committee so that narrow interests can't dominate campaign spending in ways that are guided by something other than winning. Because let's face it: politics is a nasty game. It's even nastier behind the curtain with the consultants living that feast-or-famine lifestyle, hustling from election to election. Then you add to that the skim. For those who don't know, politics is filled with people who make money by skimming. They skim the fundraising. They skim the junk mail that clutters your mailbox and goes right in the garbage. They skim the television ads and the radio ads and the social media ads. A politician hires a fundraising consultant who helps him raise $500,000 for his campaign? Well, the fundraising consultant gets a slice of that treasure chest, even if all he did was provide a Rolodex and some talking points. Now, say that politician wants to spend $250,000 on television ads. Somewhere in the middle a political consultant is getting a skim -- could be 15%, 20%, or even more. Who's keeping track of that skim? Usually the one doing the skimming. But that's how political campaigns raise campaign cash and transform it into communications that reach voters. There's nothing inherently wrong with the skim -- everyone has to eat -- but it does create perverse incentives to deploy resources in ways that prioritize something other than winning. For example, if you're getting the TV skim, you're probably going to recommend lots of TV. Ditto if you're getting the mail skim. If it turns out that paying young activists to door knock is the more effective strategy, but you're not getting a skim on the door-knocking... well, the door-knocking might get pushed to the back burner. Whoever emerges as the next crop of Republican leaders needs to take a careful look at who had been skimming and whether that skimming has been oriented toward the good of the party or toward narrower interests. Even if winning has been the top priority, a party that purports to back meritocracy ought to find a way to swiftly replace professionals with demonstrated losing records. The last thing I'll say, at the risk of sounding too harsh on Maine's Republicans, considering that they're still drowning in their own blood and mire while spears and arrows rain down on their heads, is that they are vastly outmatched not only by a better funded and better run Democratic Party, but also by a humongous leftist dark-money operation that works hand-in-glove with official Democrats to advance the same goals, often in more vicious ways. I'm talking, of course, about the constellation of 501(c)3 and 501(c)4 and other NGOs funded by George Soros, Hansjorg Wyss, Pierre Omidyar, and many other leftist billionaires. Unlike the Maine Republicans, the Maine Democrats have both the Bangor and Portland newspapers effectively serving as their communications and propaganda organs. And they have dozens and dozens of NGOs that get both dark-money funding and taxpayer dollars. The playing field is tilted and the game is unfair. Conservatives can either whine about it, get better at politics, or move to New Hampshire. | | | | * ---|---|--- | Nov 4 | You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Our movement accomplished something unimaginable on Tuesday night. **Well, not to me.**
My team and I entered this fight knowing we were on the cusp of making history, so we held nothing back. We scoured the nation for fearless climate leaders, and as of this morning, **we’ve elected 216 this year.**
In my decades of activism, I have always believed in one simple truth: everyday people have the power to create change when we come together. **Now, together, we have fundamentally shifted what power looks like in this country.**
Thank you for making this possible.
I want you to see what our climate champions ran on:
_Holding Big Tech Accountable._
_Stopping AI data center expansion._
_Passing polluter pay legislation._
_Lowering utility bills for everyday people._
**This message is loud and clear. And our candidates overcame enormous odds to deliver it.**
Corporate polluters and outside groups bankrolled by Donald Trump’s super PAC and Elon Musk poured hundreds of millions to try to buy this election.
They had bottomless bank accounts, but we had something much stronger: a people-powered movement that cared too much to sit this one out.
This election was a test of whose interests our government serves.
By showing up, knocking on doors, and chipping in what you could, you sent an unmistakable reminder that climate is in fact a winning message. These issues are on the forefront of our minds, and they need to be a priority for our elected officials.
Thank you, thank you, thank you for trusting us. I do not take your support for granted. Onward!
xx Jane

My team and I entered this fight knowing we were on the cusp of making history, so we held nothing back. We scoured the nation for fearless climate leaders, and as of this morning, we’ve elected 216 this year. In my decades of activism, I have always believed in one simple truth: everyday people have the power to create change when we come together. Now, together, we have fundamentally shifted what power looks like in this country. Thank you for making this possible. I want you to see what our climate champions ran on: Holding Big Tech Accountable. Stopping AI data center expansion. Passing polluter pay legislation. Lowering utility bills for everyday people. This message is loud and clear. And our candidates overcame enormous odds to deliver it. Corporate polluters and outside groups bankrolled by Donald Trump’s super PAC and Elon Musk poured hundreds of millions to try to buy this election. They had bottomless bank accounts, but we had something much stronger: a people-powered movement that cared too much to sit this one out. This election was a test of whose interests our government serves. By showing up, knocking on doors, and chipping in what you could, you sent an unmistakable reminder that climate is in fact a winning message. These issues are on the forefront of our minds, and they need to be a priority for our elected officials. Thank you, thank you, thank you for trusting us. I do not take your support for granted. Onward! xx Jane Before you go... I couldn’t be prouder of this grassroots movement. But Big Oil isn’t going to roll over. Our newly elected leaders need us behind them on Day One to hold the line. | ---|--- | | | | ---|---|---|---|---

### Over the Shoulder, Over the Horizon
Elections have consequences, but also, elections sometimes are the consequences. The Republicans are seeing the consequence of allowing Trump to govern the way he has for the past two years. We'll see if the Democrats have learned what happens when the leadership keeps out new voices. How do either of them explain the rise in Americans calling themselves Independent? The Major Parties have a lot to learn, but maybe we do too. We've been building this Party for nearly 5 years. Are we on the right track? How have things changed in that time? What have we learned? What should be our goals for the next 5 years? How do we accomplish them? Many of you have emailed us over the past 5 years with ideas or comments about what you'd like to see. While we all are understanding the blue wave that hit our State this week, before we start planning for 2027, let's consider the big picture. Please share your thoughts on these questions or what ever you're thinking. You can reply to this email or share on our SLACK channel. If you haven't joined already, use the link below. **You are a Forwardist. Help us understand what that means to you.**

### Volunteer with PA Forward Party
2027 is a year for building local engagement and local campaigns. We plan to hold more events and get our message out to a wider audience. We want to define our goals clearly to that audience. We want to find new ways to support the candidates who affiliate with us and recruit more great candidates in the future. If you want to help, this is the time to get involved.

## 2026 Candidates!
We want to to thank all of our 2026 Forward endorsed candidates. Election night was very exciting watching all the returns come in and there were a lot of close races. These races didn't ultimately go the way we hoped but we're proud of the relationships we made and everyone's hard work over the past year. Thanks to those of you who knocked on doors, gathered signatures, made calls, sent texts, or spread the word to help PA Forwardists running for office. This year, we endorsed 2 Republicans, 2 Democrats, and 2 Independents. We're proud to be an organization that can stratal the partisan divide. While our focus will continue to be local and state elections, we had the opportunity this year to work with 2 congressional candidates including the current most bi-partisan member of congress. The 4 State House candidates we endorsed were spread across the state and ran great campaigns. The effort and commitment that goes into one of these campaigns make us endlessly grateful that these candidates would throw their hat in the ring. We look Forward to working with all of these candidates again in the future.

We'll see if the Democrats have learned what happens when the leadership keeps out new voices. How do either of them explain the rise in Americans calling themselves Independent? The Major Parties have a lot to learn, but maybe we do too. We've been building this Party for nearly 5 years. Are we on the right track? How have things changed in that time? What have we learned? What should be our goals for the next 5 years? How do we accomplish them? Many of you have emailed us over the past 5 years with ideas or comments about what you'd like to see. While we all are understanding the blue wave that hit our State this week, before we start planning for 2027, let's consider the big picture. Please share your thoughts on these questions or what ever you're thinking. You can reply to this email or share on our SLACK channel. If you haven't joined already, use the link below. You are a Forwardist. Help us understand what that means to you. Volunteer with PA Forward Party 2027 is a year for building local engagement and local campaigns. We plan to hold more events and get our message out to a wider audience. We want to define our goals clearly to that audience. We want to find new ways to support the candidates who affiliate with us and recruit more great candidates in the future. If you want to help, this is the time to get involved. | "Sign up as a PA Forward Party volunteer!" 2026 Candidates! We want to to thank all of our 2026 Forward endorsed candidates. Election night was very exciting watching all the returns come in and there were a lot of close races. These races didn't ultimately go the way we hoped but we're proud of the relationships we made and everyone's hard work over the past year. Thanks to those of you who knocked on doors, gathered signatures, made calls, sent texts, or spread the word to help PA Forwardists running for office. This year, we endorsed 2 Republicans, 2 Democrats, and 2 Independents. We're proud to be an organization that can stratal the partisan divide. While our focus will continue to be local and state elections, we had the opportunity this year to work with 2 congressional candidates including the current most bi-partisan member of congress. The 4 State House candidates we endorsed were spread across the state and ran great campaigns. The effort and commitment that goes into one of these campaigns make us endlessly grateful that these candidates would throw their hat in the ring. We look Forward to working with all of these candidates again in the future. name: Jeff Tiegs, Rescue In Blue
subject: Meet the man rescuing hundreds of children
body:
He poses as a buyer – and then he brings them home.

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e11347311/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvYzJCSDVVZGNEdA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNsQjcwSTA5NA/qP2hpZHM9bmN5Z0JTUjdidTZyTTBsc10/gau4MoQ/s8s20da8307

[Rescue in Blue Logo]
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Friend,

The traffickers think he’s one of their customers.

_He isn’t. _

He goes by Tracker. In his line of work, he can’t use his real
name.

For years, Tracker has worked deep undercover inside the sex
trafficking networks run by Mexican cartels. He poses as a buyer and
beFriends the traffickers. He waits for the moment they trust him.

In his words, “ONCE THEY TRUST YOU, THEY START OFFERING YOU
GIRLS.”

Friend, that’s when Tracker’s real mission begins.

Inside those brothels, strip clubs, and massage parlors are girls who
were taken at 12, 14, or 16 years old.

Many were stolen from their families while trying to cross the border.
Their parents were told the police had stopped the car and immigration
had taken their daughter.

THEY NEVER HEARD FROM HER AGAIN.

These girls are forced to serve as many as 30 or 40 men in a single
night. They’re promised freedom once they “pay off” $50,000 or
$100,000.

But that goal line always moves.

AND TRACKER SAYS THIS ISN’T ONLY HAPPENING SOUTH OF THE BORDER.
IT’S HAPPENING IN TEXAS... SAN FRANCISCO... NEW YORK... LAS VEGAS...
AND ELSEWHERE ACROSS AMERICA.

Tracker has to reach these girls without harming them and without
raising suspicion.

One method he can share: he gives a victim a cell phone. To the
traffickers, it’s just a gift from a customer.

In reality, it’s often what cracks the case wide open, giving
authorities what they need to take down the entire ring.

BY HIS COUNT, TRACKER HAS HELPED FREE MORE THAN 200 SURVIVORS.

And Friend, that’s why I’m writing to you today, even though you
may not know me yet. I’m Jeff Tiegs.

I spent more than three decades in U.S. Army Special Operations as an
Army Ranger, a Special Forces Green Beret, and a Delta Force
commander, leading intelligence-driven operations around the world.

As a Green Beret, I lived by the words “Free the Oppressed.” At
Delta Force: “Oppressors Beware.”

TODAY, I LEAD RESCUE IN BLUE, WHERE I PUT THOSE WORDS TO WORK FOR
CHILDREN STILL WAITING TO BE FOUND. HERE’S WHAT WE DO:

Undercover work like Tracker’s only becomes a rescue when trained
officers are ready to act on it.

But most local police departments have never been trained to recognize
trafficking, even when it’s happening in their own communities.

AT RESCUE IN BLUE, WE CHANGE THAT.

We equip law enforcement officers and partners like Tracker with the
specialized training... technology... and operational support they
need to identify victims... arrest predators... and build cases that
bring traffickers to justice.

Our three-day Training Camp and Operation Rescue puts experienced
military and intelligence professionals alongside local law
enforcement to prepare them for one mission:

FINDING CHILDREN WHO DESPERATELY NEED SOMEONE TO COME FOR THEM.

So far, people who share your concern have helped us:

Train more than 9,200 OFFICERS...

Support the arrest of 398 PREDATORS...

And recover 183 TRAFFICKING VICTIMS who now have the chance to rebuild
their lives.

THIS IS THE KIND OF OPERATION YOUR SUPPORT MAKES POSSIBLE.

But Tracker can’t do this alone. And right now, girls are being held
in places he hasn’t found yet, still waiting for someone to come.

THAT’S WHY WE NEED YOU, FRIEND.

WILL YOU MAKE YOUR FIRST GIFT TODAY TO HELP PARTNERS LIKE TRACKER
RESCUE MORE CHILDREN?
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Your gift of $50, $75, $100, OR WHATEVER YOU CAN GIVE today helps
provide specialized training, advanced investigative tools, and
operational support so more children can be found and more traffickers
can be stopped.

HELP TRACKER RESCUE MORE CHILDREN
[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.

Friend, you don’t have to go undercover to help set a child free.

TODAY, YOU CAN STAND BEHIND THE PEOPLE WHO DO WITH YOUR SUPPORT FOR
RESCUE IN BLUE AND PARTNERS LIKE TRACKER.

Thank you for standing with our men and women in blue, and with the
children who need them most.

Sincerely,

name: Yasmin at Swing Left
subject: The conversation we need to have after Tuesday night
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Let’s translate the joy we’re feeling into lasting wins.
#
Hi there,
It’s been a few days, and I’m still feeling the [Election Night Joy](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3272?t=1&akid=3411%2E1562180%2EBkk_Bl). The American people delivered a thunderous repudiation of Donald Trump and the Republican Party that has reverberated into districts and states we haven’t won in a generation.
And now that the dust has begun to settle from the incredible night we had on Tuesday, I’d like to spend some time digging into the conversation we need to have next.
Thanks to the thousands of hard-working people across this country, we find ourselves in the new reality we were all fighting for. The Swing Left community showed up. Democratic candidates jumped into the arena to run for office, campaign staff worked tirelessly, supporters invested their time, energy, and money into this midterm election, and voters made their voices heard at the ballot box. Together, we helped bring about the beginning of the end of the Trump era. And we have a tremendous opportunity in front of us.
**What we do next will determine whether this election is yet another temporary swing in the balance of power or the beginning of a sustained era of Democratic governance that delivers consistently and materially for the American people.**
Democrats won the 2026 midterms through a combination of strong candidate matchups, disciplined messaging, and good organizing together with a powerful wave of anti-Trump voter sentiment.

We cannot take these victories or the people who voted for Democrats this year for granted. Without Trump on the ballot, and with voters tending to vote against the party in power, there is no guarantee that the people who voted for Democrats in 2026 will do so again in 2028.
**You’ve seen this cycle-to-cycle whiplash before.** After big Democratic wins in 2018 and 2020, Democrats lost the House in 2022, and Republicans won back full control of Washington by 2024.
We’ve been in a cycle of change elections, where control flip-flops between parties, for nearly two decades. If we want the next election, and the elections that follow, to be different, Democrats can’t take anyone for granted. We have to work hard, starting as soon as the new Congress begins, to build voters' trust throughout the next two years.
**We heard this from voters in Ground Truth conversations throughout the election cycle.**
One of these was Michael, in his 70s, who lives in Wisconsin’s 3rd District (which flipped blue Tuesday!) and retired from the Army after 30 years. When a volunteer in this community called in July, he was a 5 out of 10 on voting for Democrats, angry that they hadn’t stopped MAGA. He and his wife were so discouraged that they skipped the Fourth of July. The volunteer listened, then circled back. At the end of the call, Michael said he was a 10 out of 10 in his likelihood to vote for Democrats in the midterms, with a warning: **they need to deliver.**
This is where we—the grassroots—continue to come in. We cannot help build durable Democratic majorities that will last through the next election and beyond simply by getting better at mobilizing the coalition we already have to turn out to vote. We need to expand it and strengthen it. **To sustain the wins of 2026 in the critical elections ahead, Democrats must reach voters that have been traditionally overlooked or written off and persuade people who don’t yet agree with us, including Republicans who voted for Trump, independents, and people who feel left behind.**
Over the last year, Ground Truth gave us an opportunity to put this approach into practice. We learned a lot about what happens when we take the time to have real conversations with voters, and how grassroots volunteers can help build the relationships that campaigns alone often can’t. The power of all of us working collectively and enthusiastically towards one goal is something money can’t buy, and Democrats can’t afford to let that advantage go to waste between elections.
Now we’re taking those lessons into the next phase of Swing Left’s work to win in 2028. **That’s what we want to talk with you about on our next community-wide call, on November 19th.**
On Swing Left’s virtual post-election call, we’ll gather to celebrate what this community helped accomplish in 2026, share what we learned from Ground Truth, and give you a first look at Swing Left’s strategy for 2027 and 2028. It’s a chance to have an honest conversation about what we need to keep doing to ensure the results we saw on Tuesday aren't a momentary bright spot for Democrats.
**[Join us for Swing Left’s Inside Update call on November 19th.](http://act.swingleft.org/go/3273?t=2&akid=3411%2E1562180%2EBkk_Bl)**
**[RSVP Now »](http://act.swingleft.org/go/3273?t=3&akid=3411%2E1562180%2EBkk_Bl)**
Thank you again for everything you put into this year. You gave your time, resources, and energy to try something new with us, and we’re proud of what we built together.
With gratitude,
Yasmin Radjy
Executive Director, Swing Left
P.S. For a preview of what we’ll cover on the call, take a look at the refreshed [**Swing Left strategy page**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3274?t=4&akid=3411%2E1562180%2EBkk_Bl).

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261106-1&t=5&refcode2=3411_1562180_Bkk_Bl&akid=3411%2E1562180%2EBkk_Bl)
