body:
I want to share a few things... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5860379?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/PDn1L7X0jy9?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

Hello, my friend.

As you surely know by now, we came up short in my campaign for re-election as Nevada Controller. And I don’t need to spend a lot of time here dissecting why the outcome occurred. As we all could see by early evening on Tuesday, it was simply an awful year for Republicans up and down the ballot, from coast to coast. Despite our best efforts, that proved too much to overcome.

I called my opponent, Michael MacDougall, to congratulate him on Wednesday morning, and pledged to do whatever I can to ensure his smooth transition into office so that he is set up to be successful.

Obviously, I’m very disappointed by the result. And I know you are, too. We fought so hard throughout this race, and it’s a tough feeling when you don’t prevail in the end.

But I want to leave you with just a few things.

First, I’m enormously proud of the work my team and I have done in the Controller’s Office the past few years. I ran for Controller to promote government transparency, and we were able to accomplish something very significant on that front — putting the state checkbook online ([checkbook.nv.gov](https://us.list-manage.com/feekfXF2axg?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)) so taxpayers can see where their money is going. That’s a big, tangible accomplishment, one that should provide lasting value to our state and its citizens.

I want to thank my incredible Controller’s Office team. It’s been such a joy not only getting to work with them, but to get to know them as individuals. They’re an awesome bunch, and I will miss them all tremendously.

I especially want to acknowledge and thank my Chief Deputy Controller, James Smack, for serving our office so capably and energetically during my term. James was indispensable to the success we had, and did a phenomenal job running much of the day-to-day operations of our office. He’s a dedicated and talented public servant, and a very good man. I’m honored to have been able to work with him.

I also want to thank my campaign team, Robert Uithoven and Ray Serrano, two of the smartest and hardest-working people you’ll ever meet in politics. These guys were doing the crucial work behind the scenes throughout the campaign, and they helped to put us in as good a position to win as possible in what turned out to be a very tough year. They offered wise counsel throughout this race, and I couldn’t be more grateful for their leadership and support. I consider them both good friends as well.

It has been the honor of a lifetime to serve as your Controller. And I still believe that this state I love so much has a bright future ahead of it. That’s because what makes our state so wonderful is not its politicians — it’s our people. When all is said and done, it’s not the political victories or the policy wins that stick with me from the past 20 years I’ve spent in Nevada politics. It’s the personal relationships I’ve made and the amazing people I’ve met who have touched my life in ways I’ll never forget.

Which brings me to you. I cannot thank you enough for standing with me in this campaign. Your support — both financial and moral — means more to me than I can possibly express. I appreciate you so much, and I will always be grateful to you for being part of this team. Thank you, my friend.

I want to thank my parents, Tom and Carol, and my brother Eric, for all of your love and encouragement throughout not only my career, but my entire life. I love you all so much.

And I want to thank my wife, Valerie, and our son, Isaac, who have stood with me through all the ups and downs of this campaign. Those who aren’t on the inside of politics can’t appreciate how much our family sacrifices right along with us. Valerie: You are the love of my life, and I can’t tell you how much your love and support mean to me.

So many people have reached out to me these past few days to ask me how I’m doing. I’m very thankful for that. There are a lot of things I’m feeling, but I want you to know that above all, what I feel is gratitude. It’s a privilege to be able to serve the people of the State of Nevada. And I’m so grateful to God for that opportunity among so much else that He has blessed me with.

I wish all of you well. And I hope we’ll keep in touch. I love you from the bottom of my heart.

For Nevada’s future, now and always ...

Andy

I cannot thank you enough for standing with me in this campaign. Your support — both financial and moral — means more to me than I can possibly express. I appreciate you so much, and I will always be grateful to you for being part of this team. Thank you, my friend. I want to thank my parents, Tom and Carol, and my brother Eric, for all of your love and encouragement throughout not only my career, but my entire life. I love you all so much. And I want to thank my wife, Valerie, and our son, Isaac, who have stood with me through all the ups and downs of this campaign. Those who aren’t on the inside of politics can’t appreciate how much our family sacrifices right along with us. Valerie: You are the love of my life, and I can’t tell you how much your love and support mean to me. So many people have reached out to me these past few days to ask me how I’m doing. I’m very thankful for that. There are a lot of things I’m feeling, but I want you to know that above all, what I feel is gratitude. It’s a privilege to be able to serve the people of the State of Nevada. And I’m so grateful to God for that opportunity among so much else that He has blessed me with. I wish all of you well. And I hope we’ll keep in touch. I love you from the bottom of my heart. For Nevada’s future, now and always ... | | | | Fellow Patriot, **[I was just charged with TWO FELONIES for my undercover journalism in Minnesota.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=aba9aaa024ff4b009462986fbd3f62b5&_e=YW0cfJvnO__bIue7Yy8yMzSsM7Q0WFWqYs7oMhO-VpuLL62k38zWX21CXJ3a79X7YNYgkZJHcvi-dno6881y_-g6wBTBcvKWQuH_YM76b4Af8bkJxTpgJOuD-85PXwkTKJkq_lk03DC2TsZ01-0USPPHlearDGVAapYyE0-K36Pn-A6-sqsbjXfvYgDSjohTY55LGyiUyjPNjoUmfGGWRqDsx9WmqjEwfQFhURLqOb7L47wB4j-9NR8ON5_m1AABoaFzmDOwibG-oiWn7SKi4ou0id8TjGNnISMPS5rglo6qrjEBFA11KKDknvgM4J5Kg6FyLpImOZDjP_Ne69qgpLBKbJI9yRtjCx4KCLKGGnmFegdQrG5hmCu2BXJz4MOspeWEaPANQOFwzgG4P1zJy42QRsgGZ91ReSFtWDuUMSvf3yRA238wEK_G0ctoujv4RWSzPdOP2RQDnmqwMj8NWB3kRV26THr46gGOnVvKwaB1KMFAbx_DueCXRmIchgq0LEb_0Zp6jChsWjVhXT4o8v1cqvIgky2T_Gg709J4Zcs5tPU7TUImEsdXlIg8FinxbhHu5sezr7UUuFHAKiSISJe0uqoygMpMi4LRQXShdTP_H3IRkj0cWrbKCq5DPAuGEVOGGOL5-u2UphgeDwAwmnXS_ioI3EQxrh6HqvI2JV-yV8NUWtA7pj925UE8n1w1JiA6dNuTaDxROL0fV9TbQJ4X3_adCLclb1PMMw1JuyJ5yfBF7pU76wd0pu9KoG99mcHAJmmC9uGIrIS0un2DBTSdM7Rz4RnBfgd8rVE81M730QLxn5qWffd1wrZfZ0dkzqN5yjFHvazt2GMWp2pKMusSnCwIcMRMnlJUs1Wyg6jJl5hnkWnVP99X11lWhxZO)** **Back in August, we published a********bombshell investigative report on voter vouching laws****.****We never cast a ballot. We never signed a voter oath.****Yet now, fellow journalist Cam Higby and I are facing felony charges and possible JAIL TIME.** Even the county prosecutor acknowledged that we never intended to vote.**These charges are nothing more than an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism and intimidate anyone who dares to expose wrongdoing.** But I refuse to back down. subject: Thank You.
body:

From the bottom of my heart, thank you.
While Tuesday night wasn't the outcome we had hoped for, I couldn't be more grateful for the people who stood alongside us throughout this campaign.
To every volunteer who knocked on doors, made phone calls, put up a yard sign, walked in a parade, attended events, or gave up their evenings and weekends to help us, thank you. We couldn't have done this without you.
To everyone who donated, encouraged us, shared our message, and put their trust in me at the ballot box, I'm so grateful for your support.
Over the past year, I've had the opportunity to meet so many wonderful people across Minnesota's Second Congressional District. I've heard your concerns, learned your stories, and made friendships that I'll carry with me long after this election.
A campaign may come to an end, but my commitment to our community doesn't. I'm proud of the campaign we ran, the people who made it possible, and everything we accomplished together.
Thank you for believing in me and for being part of this journey.
Eric,

A satellite view of Qeshm Island in Hormozgan Province, Iran, within the Strait of Hormuz region on January 17, 2026. Photo by Gallo Images/Orbital Horizon/Copernicus Sentinel Data 2026.
TEHRAN, Iran--On the morning of October 31, Mehrzad Panjeh and his brother Mehran were fishing in the Strait of Hormuz off of Qeshm Island when a drone struck the water near their boat. The blast set the boat on fire and threw Mehran into the sea. Mehrzad, whose knee was broken in the attack, could only watch from the burning deck as his brother struggled in the water.
Their relatives Mohammad Panjeh and his son Mahmoud were also hit as they fished in a nearby boat. Their boat broke apart, leaving the two clinging to the floating wreckage for hours.
The four had come to check on baited hooks left in the water between the town of Souza and the village of Mesen on the Qeshm's southern coast, a method known locally as ghollab-e entezari, or "waiting hooks."
"We were doing our usual work, just what we were doing as fishermen for years," Mehrzad Panjeh told Drop Site News. "We never thought it would come to that." The four fishermen were wounded, but miraculously survived.
The attack,[ at around 11:30 a.m. about 18 nautical miles off Mesen](https://substack.com/redirect/0e89e1d8-15a5-41ab-bac8-b4d8d27fe878?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), was one of at least three strikes in Iran's southern waters over four days.
Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan's deputy governor for political affairs and an informed official in Hormozgan province, who spoke on condition of anonymity as he was not authorized to speak to the media, told Drop Site that U.S. forces carried out the October 31 attack. Nafisi also blamed the U.S. for another strike on Qeshm two days later, on November 2, and an earlier attack that killed a ship captain in the Persian Gulf on October 30, the day before the fishermen were hit.
Unnamed American officials cited in the Wall Street Journal said the U.S. conducted the November 2 strikes, claiming them as the latest in a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks. The U.S. deliberately kept quiet about the attack to avoid signaling a return to major combat operations, one official said.
The U.S. strikes came during a particularly tense period ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, amid widespread speculation the U.S. and Israel would re-escalate the war and embark on another heavy bombardment campaign on Iran. Attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways hit a record high in October, with over two dozen recorded incidents. Meanwhile, diplomatic efforts, with regional mediators, led by Qatar, to reach an agreement have struggled to break a deadlock. Vice President JD Vance said on November 2, the eve of the midterms, that he and Trump were optimistic about reaching an agreement, while Iran insisted the next move was Washington's.
While the sweeping success of the Democratic Party in the vote on Tuesday was viewed as a rebuke of Trump and the Iran war, Tehran has remained cautious. Vance blamed the Iran war in no uncertain terms for the Republican losses at the polls. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance said on Thursday. Yet Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Wednesday dismissed the Democrats' electoral gains and warned against giving any concessions, saying in a written message that "Those who harbor the slightest hope that partisan and factional shifts could result in a different approach or who imagine that by giving concessions to the U.S., they can make it abandon its hostility towards Iran, are seriously mistaken."
The series of attacks on Qeshm in the runup to the midterms that were blamed on the U.S. passed seemingly without retaliation from Iran. But for those at the target end of the bombs, the attacks will not be soon forgotten.
## **No Safe Waters**
As the main provider for a household of six, Mehrzad Panjeh could not afford to stay ashore. His catch brings in between 30 million and 40 million tomans ($110 to $150) a month, leaving little room to give up his livelihood.
"We were moving along the coast in an area we considered completely safe. We always went there," he said. "We didn't hear anything, but suddenly something struck the water close to us. It was moving so fast that I couldn't tell what it was at the time."
Only later, after watching the news, did he know it had been a drone. He thinks fragments hit their boat, and its engine caught fire. He fractured his knee and suffered burns to his legs, while fragments of the damaged vessel pierced both legs.
"When my brother fell into the water, I didn't know if he was alive or dead," Mehrzad said. "A few seconds later I heard him calling out. I looked around and saw him four or five meters away. I couldn't move and he was struggling in the water. I was screaming and crying. I wanted to help him, but my knee was broken and I couldn't walk."
Passing fishermen pulled Mehran from the water. Three boats reached Mehrzad about half an hour later, while his boat was still giving off thick smoke. Meanwhile, Mohammad and Mahmoud had climbed onto floating pieces of their boat. They drifted into deeper water with no one nearby to call for help.
"We couldn't contact our family or anyone who could find us," Mahmoud said. "My phone fell into the water and my father's had no signal. It was terrifying."
It was several hours before rescue boats and fishermen nearby found the father and son clinging to the wreckage at around 4 p.m.
Ahmad Noursoroudi, head of Qeshm's Red Crescent, told Drop Site that Mohammad, Mahmoud, and Mehran had minor injuries. Mehrzad was more seriously wounded in both legs and is now recovering at home, with one leg in a cast and the other bandaged.
Again, that night, at around 9:45, Mousa Eyvazi was walking along South Coast Street along the waterfront on Qeshm with his wife and their 12-year-old daughter, Hana, when he heard aircraft overhead. He could make out at least two planes moving through the dark before several explosions nearby came in quick succession.
"It was like an earthquake. Everything shook," Eyvazi told Drop Site. "My daughter screamed. My wife was frightened too. I picked up my daughter and led them to a corner by a wall. At first, I thought they had hit somewhere inside the residential area. People walking along the waterfront were screaming, covering their heads and running away."
Only hours later did Eyvazi learn that the explosions had come from a military site near the residential areas.
The Red Crescent and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Qeshm told Drop Site that no residential areas had been hit and no civilians killed. Both, however, declined to provide further details, citing security concerns, including the site's exact location, the extent of the damage, and whether it had sustained more than one impact.
Despite the October 31 attacks, on November 2, President Donald Trump[ said](https://substack.com/redirect/240e97c3-ebca-4d52-93ca-f28323e6d7bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that "we haven't been doing any fighting for months."
Unnamed U.S. officials acknowledged the November 2 strikes on Qeshm, telling the the Wall Street Journal it was a defensive measure and claiming it was carried out after Iranian forces on the island fired a surface-to-air missile at an American aircraft over the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump gave a different emphasis the following day, on November 3,[ describing](https://substack.com/redirect/0f4c9df8-6f95-420c-a473-1280d9677636?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the target as a newly built anti-aircraft facility that American forces had watched during its construction.
The official in Hormozgan province told Drop Site the air defense site had not yet become operational. "The Americans struck an air defense position that was under construction and nonoperational," the official said. "It had no sensitive equipment and had not adeployed missiles." His account could not be independently verified.
On October 30, the day before the attack on the Panjehs' boats, Captain Nasser Ebrahimi-Nejadan, a 50-year-old military officer from the southwestern city of Abadan, was[ killed](https://substack.com/redirect/34a6d139-da43-4b99-a1df-1070c2d964c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by shrapnel when his vessel was attacked in the Persian Gulf, according to Iranian media.
Ebrahimi-Nejadan served in the military, according to two friends and colleagues, Farhad and Abdolreza, who are also military personnel and asked to be identified by their first names only. Neither was on board, but Abdolreza was among the last people to speak with the captain before his death.
Abdolreza said that in his final conversations with Ebrahimi-Nejadan a few hours before he was killed, he reported normal conditions aboard, but with reconnaissance drones overhead and tensions rising. Ebrahimi-Nejadan had also told his crew to stay alert and follow safety procedures.
On Thursday, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that he was leaving his options open about resuming an all-out war. "I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so. You will know very soon," he said.
As the war remains unresolved, residents of Qeshm fear they will once again be caught in the middle.
Since the November 2 strike, many families on Qeshm are preparing for more attacks, Eyvazi said. Fishermen, meanwhile, say they now think twice before every trip out to sea. Mehrzad's son now has to help with the fishing to cover the household's expenses.
"I want him to come home safely," Mehrzad said. "After what happened to me, it's harder knowing he's out at sea."
Friends who visited him this week told him they had stayed ashore on Tuesday and Wednesday and planned to go back out on Saturday.
"But there's still the fear of another attack," he said.

**NOVEMBER 6, 2026**
Unofficial results show Amendment 3 passed with nearly 62% of the vote. But what exactly did Floridians approve?
The amendment increases the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. It also reduces the annual assessment-growth cap on non-homestead properties from 10% to 5%.
But there is another part that deserves attention: how counties and municipalities may use property-tax revenue.
The amendment identifies seven categories:
1. Public safety
2. Education
3. Infrastructure
4. Natural-resource and flood-control projects
5. Local bonds for purposes allowed under these categories, and debt service on existing obligations
6. Retirement benefits for local government employees
7. Operations and administration of county officers and municipalities, along with other expenditures approved by county officers or county or municipal governing bodies, unless prohibited by general law

That seventh category is particularly important. It leaves room for local decisions. The amendment establishes boundaries, but it does not dictate every spending choice.
And these rules apply to county and municipal property-tax revenue, not every dollar in a local budget.
Homeowners voted for relief. Now local leaders must determine how to manage the change. That means examining priorities, scrutinizing how resources are allocated, and finding efficiencies that make existing funds go further without diminishing essential services.
We should not assume that cuts are inevitable. We should expect transparent decisions and responsible stewardship.
What would you like your county commissioners to explain about how your property-tax dollars are spent?

# [October jobs jump 165K, putting December hike back in play](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/512774e2-e86e-409b-8efd-8245bc879842?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[more than double consensus expectations,](https://substack.com/redirect/512774e2-e86e-409b-8efd-8245bc879842?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% and put a December rate hike back on the table.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Private payrolls surge** : Private employment rose 159,000, with professional and business services adding 70,000 jobs, well above the prior-year monthly average.
* **Revisions lift prior months** : August and September were revised higher by a combined 84,000, reinforcing the strength of the labor market heading into the print.
* **Unemployment dips** : The jobless rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%, against expectations it would hold steady, while average hourly earnings rose 0.4% month-over-month.
* **Yields climb on data** : Two-year Treasury yields rose as much as 7 basis points as traders priced roughly 70% odds of a quarter-point hike at the December meeting.

# [Nasdaq plunges into correction on AI data-center fears](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Nasdaq Composite **[slid more than 5%](https://substack.com/redirect/a5ae2f1c-f3d2-4cef-9ac7-a1aa7ae632f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Thursday[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ccf6a2cf-dbaf-4023-89f0-2147a842f8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[into correction territory,](https://substack.com/redirect/ccf6a2cf-dbaf-4023-89f0-2147a842f8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ccf6a2cf-dbaf-4023-89f0-2147a842f8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)more than 10%[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/05c37651-acda-4302-9738-692428d005ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[below its October high,](https://substack.com/redirect/05c37651-acda-4302-9738-692428d005ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as a Democratic midterm sweep ignited fears that new data-center rules could slow the AI buildout.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Democratic sweep drives selloff** : Investors dumped AI and chip shares after Democrats took both chambers, with Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa having campaigned on an immediate moratorium on data-center approvals.
* **Chip index bloodbath** : The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 12%, its worst day since March 2020, while Nvidia dropped more than 9% as hyperscalers and related names also sank.
* **Trillions erased overnight** : Roughly $2.5 trillion vanished from U.S. equities in the session, reversing Wednesday's post-election bounce and sending the S&P 500 down more than 4%.
* **Friday bounce attempt** : Nasdaq futures pointed higher early Friday as dip-buyers stepped in, though the move recovered only a fraction of Thursday's losses.

# [Democrats demand national data-center moratorium after midterms](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bernie Sanders and other Democrats **[called for a national data-center moratorium](https://substack.com/redirect/fbd9d4be-2773-412a-ba57-0209767cd9cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/fbd9d4be-2773-412a-ba57-0209767cd9cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)after their midterm sweep, citing voter referendums and state-level campaigns that targeted AI infrastructure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Sanders call** : Sanders wrote "National data center moratorium now," arguing **[Americans do not want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment](https://substack.com/redirect/06b3f918-8725-4a1e-9ff2-038027d979f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** or gutting jobs.
* **State-level pledges** : Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on a moratorium on new approvals, while other incoming Democratic governors in key buildout states signaled similar pauses.
* **Voter signal** : A CNBC poll found 56% of voters said AI and data centers were crucial or major factors, and 65% of those voters backed Democratic candidates.
* **Capacity at risk** : Democratic-won states account for a substantial share of planned U.S. data-center capacity, raising questions about the pace of the AI buildout.

* * *
# [Analysts split on buying the AI dip after Thursday's rout](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Dan Ives called the tech selloff[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ed8dfe4b-d467-40f7-b004-238e9aafbebc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[a golden buying opportunity for marquee names,](https://substack.com/redirect/ed8dfe4b-d467-40f7-b004-238e9aafbebc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/ed8dfe4b-d467-40f7-b004-238e9aafbebc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)while other strategists[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/52f6f842-a3e5-478c-9006-42ba5b393ba5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[warned against catching falling knives](https://substack.com/redirect/52f6f842-a3e5-478c-9006-42ba5b393ba5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as the Nasdaq entered correction territory.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Ives view** : Ives said the pullback in Apple, Microsoft and Nvidia is overdone and comparable to the Covid and tariff selloffs, framing it as a chance to add to core holdings.
* **Caveats remain** : Barron's live coverage noted calls to buy the dip but flagged ongoing questions about data-center timelines and whether the AI trade can recover quickly.
* **Against the dip** : David Bahnsen and others argued investors should not chase the decline, pointing to the risk that oversold conditions can stay oversold.
* **Modest Friday bounce** : Early Friday gains recovered only a fraction of Thursday's losses, leaving the broader trend still under pressure.

[Subscribe](https://substack.com/redirect/996fe125-f9d0-46f2-ba4a-63a53b35fae1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# [Retail traders dump most stocks in a day since Covid](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Retail investors **[sold a net $338 million of single stocks on Thursday,](https://substack.com/redirect/82c5c9df-06ed-44d2-943e-76bdc45f4a9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the largest one-day outflow since March 2020, according to Vanda Research.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Largest since 2020** : The outflow marked the biggest single-day retail selling of individual names since the early pandemic crash.
* **Concentration in tech** : The selling hit AI and chip-related names hardest as the broader market reversed Wednesday's gains.
* **Contrast with prior day** : Retail activity had been more constructive earlier in the week before the midterm results and AI fears accelerated the decline.
* **Broader tape** : The move coincided with heavy institutional and mechanical selling, amplifying the overall session loss.

* * *

The decline[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2238e6d8-5435-452e-9f16-08aaadbd92f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[expanded beyond AI names to every S&P 500 sector](https://substack.com/redirect/2238e6d8-5435-452e-9f16-08aaadbd92f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Thursday, contributing to a roughly $1.7 trillion drop in the index as **[safe-haven assets outperformed.](https://substack.com/redirect/1991a246-9854-4f84-8dc0-a3c8a7bc34e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4d8c4f9c-156a-4887-8a7e-699865ffd85f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Broad participation** : All 11 S&P sectors finished lower, with financials, industrials and consumer names joining the tech-led selling.
* **Safe havens hold** : Two defensive assets gained ground amid the carnage, providing relative shelter as equity volatility spiked.
* **Low-vol outperformance** : The Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF fell only about 1%, outperforming the broader market by a wide margin.
* **Financials hit** : Banks and brokerages including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Robinhood and Webull declined sharply as the selloff caught the group.

name: Jeff Hurd
subject: The campaign is over. The job isn't.
body:
Friends,

I'm grateful that the people of Colorado's Third District put their trust in me to continue representing them in Congress.

And I'm especially grateful to all of you.

You knocked doors, made calls, hosted events, contributed, talked to your friends and neighbors, and drove a lot of miles across a very big district. You gave this campaign your time and energy because you believed in what we were trying to do.

I know what that took. From the bottom of my heart: Thank you.

I also want to thank Dwayne Romero for a hard-fought race, for his service to our country, and for putting himself forward to serve. Running for office isn't easy, and I respect him for doing it.

Now the election is behind us.

Whether you voted for me or not, I'll keep working hard, listening, and delivering results for every part of this district.

I won't get everything right. You won't agree with every decision I make. But I'll keep doing my best to represent Western and Southern Colorado seriously and effectively.

There's still a lot to do.

Families are dealing with high costs. We need to protect Colorado water, strengthen our rural communities, support our farmers and ranchers, and make sure people can get good health care closer to home.

And right now, communities in Southwest Colorado and the San Luis Valley are recovering from devastating flooding. Helping them is one of my immediate priorities.

The campaign is over. My job isn't.

I'm grateful for the chance to keep doing it, and grateful to all of you who helped make that possible.

Thank you,
Congressman Jeff Hurd
Member of Congress
Colorado's Third Congressional District

On Wednesday morning, I woke my partner up early saying, "You'll never believe this!" The results were beyond my wildest dreams. This is huge. It's huge for our public lands, for checks and balances, for families getting squeezed by rising costs, and for anyone who is tired of watching corruption go unchecked.
Thank you to every candidate who put their name on a ballot, every volunteer who knocked doors and made calls, every voter who showed up, every content creator who used their platform to inform people, and everyone who drove a neighbor to the polls or had a hard conversation with a family member. You did this. Celebrate it. You earned it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6741938d-1caf-4e1e-b6e4-a180ea545c63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Running the NYC Marathon Nov. 1, thank you to everyone who donated to support my fundraiser. Photo: Ryan Lynch @the_reporter_q2
I ran for U.S. Senate in Utah in 2024 and spent this fall doing everything I could to educate, motivate, and turn out voters. So I expected this week to feel like exhaling. Instead I still feel hyper vigilant, braced for impact and tired in a way sleep doesn't fix.
If you feel that way too, you're not alone. I had to do some research to figure out why.

Your nervous system doesn't care about election results. It cares about whether the threat is gone. For two years, a lot of us have lived with a president who tests every limit on his power while the people who were supposed to protect us stood by and watched, or helped. Voters just elected a new Congress that can put a lock on one door. But the same person is still in the house. Your brain can read a headline and say "we won." Your body knows the difference between a check and an ending.
Psychologists call this hyperarousal. The alarm in your brain stays on high alert because the "all clear" signal never comes. It shows up as irritability, trouble sleeping, snapping at people you love, and feeling worn out by days that look calm on paper.
This hits hardest for people who have already learned what it looks like when the rules bend for someone powerful, especially survivors of abuse or trauma. During Trump's first campaign, when the Access Hollywood tape came out, calls to the national sexual assault hotline jumped by one third that weekend. Survivors said his words brought back memories of their own assaults. That is pattern recognition. Psychologist Jennifer Freyd has a name for the pattern: DARVO. Deny, attack, and reverse victim and offender. When a powerful person denies what they did, attacks and punishes the people who speak up, and calls themselves the real victim, a lot of people hear a voice they already know.
This is also why so many of us worked so hard for change. We don't need a think piece to understand what we're up against. We can feel it in our guts. We have seen people like this up close: the ones who lie without blinking, punish anyone who tells the truth, and take what they want because they can. We know we have to fight, because we know exactly who they are. The rest of us live by rules. We wanted the rules to apply to them too.
Some of us have also learned the hard way what happens when an institution we trusted protects the powerful instead of us.
And it isn't just Americans. A psychologist who works with Iranians says people carry chronic fear long after they leave an authoritarian society. In Latin America, a legacy of fear still haunted the region years after democracies returned in the 1980s. As that psychologist puts it, sometimes what looks like hypervigilance is actually wisdom.
My rescue dog Lila taught me the same thing. She has been safe with us for years. She sleeps in the bed. She climbs peaks with me. And she will still never let you touch her with your foot. Somebody kicked her once, and her body remembers.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8e95f305-a5fb-48e9-90f3-165dd4c52aae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So if you're celebrating and your body still won't settle, you're not broken. You're paying attention. You're wise. The danger rating dropped from high to considerable. That's a huge deal, and we did that together. It is not a reason to stop reading the slope.
Tell me in the comments: one word for how you felt Wednesday morning. Share this with someone who's celebrating and still can't relax. And consider becoming a paid or free subscriber, because staying watchful is the work now.

We know we have to fight, because we know exactly who they are. The rest of us live by rules. We wanted the rules to apply to them too. Some of us have also learned the hard way what happens when an institution we trusted protects the powerful instead of us. And it isn't just Americans. A psychologist who works with Iranians says people carry chronic fear long after they leave an authoritarian society. In Latin America, a legacy of fear still haunted the region years after democracies returned in the 1980s. As that psychologist puts it, sometimes what looks like hypervigilance is actually wisdom. My rescue dog Lila taught me the same thing. She has been safe with us for years. She sleeps in the bed. She climbs peaks with me. And she will still never let you touch her with your foot. Somebody kicked her once, and her body remembers. | | ---|---|--- So if you're celebrating and your body still won't settle, you're not broken. You're paying attention. You're wise. The danger rating dropped from high to considerable. That's a huge deal, and we did that together. It is not a reason to stop reading the slope. Tell me in the comments: one word for how you felt Wednesday morning. Share this with someone who's celebrating and still can't relax. And consider becoming a paid or free subscriber, because staying watchful is the work now. Thanks for reading Caroline Gleich ⛰️! This post is public so feel free to share it. name: Aimee Prudhomme
subject: Not red. Not purple. Blue.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Powered by People, [poweredxpeople
body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
Hi,
What is this feeling? Is it...hope?
We’ve spent the last few days waking up to a blue Texas. Not red. Not purple. **Bright, beautiful blue.**
I’ve read that sentence a dozen times and it still doesn’t feel real. But it is real — and it didn’t happen by accident. It happened because of thousands of conversations, thousands of volunteers, and thousands of people like you who decided this was the year we’d stop hoping Texas would change and go out and change it.
So before we look ahead, I want to take you back through the year we just had.
It started where it always starts — in the field.
[****](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=3&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
Our bread and butter has always been meeting young, first-time voters where they are, getting them registered, and staying in touch until they cast their ballot. This year we did that at a scale we’ve never done before:
* **2,125 volunteers** trained, active, and in the field across Texas
* **1,948 voter mobilization events** on **89 campuses** statewide
* **71,666 voters registered or verified** , growing our network from about 42,000 in January to **more than 113,000 today**

Every one of those voters has a real person they can text when they have a question about voting. That has always been the point. It’s what makes us different from every other outfit in the state.
[****](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=4&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
And in the spirit of leaving nothing on the table, we tried new things.
I’ve always thought of Powered by People as a startup. We have to be lean, fast, and willing to experiment. This year, we put that to the test.
* We helped Taylor Rehmet win Senate District 9 by 17 points. We piloted a vote-by-mail program that called and texted 30,000 voters in Taylor’s district and stayed in touch with older voters through every step of a process designed to trip them up.
* We personally reached out to 240,000 Texans eligible to vote by mail and worked with thousands of them, at a time when Trump was attacking mail-in voting.
* We worked alongside partners to mail voter registration forms to 150,000 Texans who recently moved. Then we personally reached every single one of them to make sure their registration moved with them, so they didn’t lose their voice in November.

We also launched our first-ever Powered by People internship program, hiring more than 30 interns across the state. We did it because we believe young activists are what’s driving our state, and this country, forward. And one of the most beautiful things I saw all year was Gen Z and Baby Boomer volunteers standing side by side at the same event, registering and reaching voters together. Multiple generations coming together to serve. That’s what a movement built to last looks like.
We showed up in spaces we’d never been in before.
[****](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=5&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
We were everywhere. Wherever people were — especially young people and marginalized communities — we were there:
* We partnered with James Talarico’s campaign at rallies across the state, helping attendees register, update, and verify their registration on the spot.
* We brought Senator Bernie Sanders to El Paso and Houston, activating young progressives in Texas eager for change.
* We teamed up with Texas icons like Alyssa Edwards and Kacey Musgraves, registering and reaching voters at their shows.
* We organized in churches, Islamic centers, and mosques to counter Trump-era Islamophobia, protect Black voters from suppression, and guide newly registered voters — first-timers and even former Republicans — all the way to the ballot box.
* We partnered with and amplified the voices of Latino communities impacted by ICE, including the sons of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who was killed in the street by ICE agents in my backyard in Houston.

And it all came together in the final weeks.
We contacted every single one of the 110,000+ voters in our network, one-on-one. Volunteers texted their voter buddies. They called the county on behalf of voters whose registrations couldn’t be found. They helped a voter’s mom, friend, or grandparent vote for the very first time. We shared the Limited Ballot option with college students across the state who, without us, simply wouldn’t have voted.
[****](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=6&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
And in the last few days, we called every voter in our network that had not voted yet, culminating in an Election Day phone bank where we called 59,000 voters to give them the final guidance they needed to cast their ballot.
So, did it work? You know I am a data nerd, so here is what the numbers tell me.
We’re still waiting on final Election Day tallies, but our Early Voting data tells a clear story: **Powered by People voters turned out at 60% — beating the state average by 20 points.**
But the real story is __who__ showed up. Most of our network is between 18 and 29 years old, and that group turned out at **58.4%** , smashing the statewide youth average of 24.9%. **That’s 2.3x higher than their peers across Texas.**
This is the work that works.
So what’s next?
Powered by People doesn’t have an off switch. We aren’t beholden to a candidate, and we don’t have the normal peaks and valleys of a campaign coming to a close. Here’s the plan:
* **November:** We rest and recover, with a few voter registration events sprinkled in, because someone’s gotta do it!
* **December:** We strategize and refine what worked and what didn’t.
* **January:** We hit the ground running again, continuing to build the voter army that will hold our newly elected leaders accountable for real change and elect a Democrat to the White House in 2028.

We did it. And we keep going.
[**If you’re as proud of this year as I am, will you pitch in $3 today to help us keep this work going into 2027 and beyond?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=7&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
Thank you for every dollar, every shift, and every conversation. Texas is blue because of you.
[****](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261106.vWdjWV&refcode=ema20261106-241169&t=8&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
See you out there,
Aimee

[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pbp-em-2023-footer?refcode=em20261106-241169-footer&t=9&refcode2=241169_444211_bhifCL&akid=241169%2E444211%2EbhifCL)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

name: Team Derek Tran
subject: Thank You, CA-45!
body:
Thank you for your support throughout my reelection campaign! I am humbled that our community has placed their trust in me again to represent them

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-reelection-thank-you-newsletter?e=fa48019594)
---
| | | | |
---
| | Dear Supporter,
Thank you for your support throughout my reelection campaign! I am humbled that our community has placed their trust in me again to represent them.
This win belongs to all of us: to those who knocked on a door, made a call, and believed in what we could accomplish together, and to the families who believed that the promise of the American Dream should be a reality for all.
Fifty-one years ago, my parents fled Vietnam as democracy crumbled. They immigrated to the U.S. and found themselves here, in Southern California. Today, their son represents the largest Vietnamese diaspora in Congress. That is the legacy I carry with me. And now, our community gave me the honor of carrying it forward.
I do not take this responsibility lightly. Congress must be focused on lowering costs, protecting affordable healthcare, and rooting out corruption from this Administration. There’s more to do, and now, we’re going to build on what we’ve done. Let’s get back to work.
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%. It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._
_Use of Derek Tran's military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the Dept. of Defense or U.S. Army._

clean_body: Peter, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." - Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! This victory belongs to all of us,

us, but our fight isn’t. Working families are still getting squeezed while
the ultra-wealthy rake in record profits.

on corporate greed, holding the powerful accountable, and fighting for the
bold, transformative change our communities need. And that’s not going to
stop now.

keep targeting the Squad with relentless attacks because they refuse to
back down in the face of injustice. But no attack has ever been able to
break a movement powered by people. When we stand together, we’re stronger
than anything they throw at us.

name: Color Of Change
subject: URGENT: Mississippi’s Senate race isn’t over. Help Color of Change count every vote.
body:
The race could come down to a handful of ballots — and Color of Change is in an all out sprint to make sure every vote is counted.
#
Mississippi’s Senate race is NOT over. It could come down to a handful of ballots.
**Color of Change helped build massive voter turnout this cycle with our Black Voter Protection Program—and now we need you in the final, all-out sprint to make sure every vote is counted.**
[**Can you rush a donation right now to help us raise $15,000?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=everyvotecountedms26_ln.6aM6KH&refcode=em20261106-1728&t=1&akid=1728%2E2118727%2EkzTg7C)
Right now, Democrat Scott Colom holds an extremely narrow lead over Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. There are an estimated 8,000 to 12,000 affidavit ballots still waiting to be counted. Each one has been set aside over a technical problem — but voters only have a few days to fix their ballots and be counted.
We URGENTLY need to reach Black voters across the state to let them know. So**Color of Change is actively contacting voters in Mississippi, urging them to check their ballots before the deadline, and running digital ads** that reach voters who may not know their ballots are at risk.
**We budgeted $10,000 for text messages and $5,000 for urgent digital ads to reach these voters** — and now we’re racing to raise those funds.
**[Can you rush a donation right now to help us raise $15,000 so that Color of Change can reach Black voters across Mississippi and make sure every vote is counted?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=everyvotecountedms26_ln.6aM6KH&refcode=em20261106-1728&t=2&akid=1728%2E2118727%2EkzTg7C)**
**[DONATE $20 ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21584?c0=everyvotecountedms26_ln.la6Ans&refcode=em20261106-1728&t=3&akid=1728%2E2118727%2EkzTg7C)**
Before Election Day, **Color of Change’s Black Voter Protection Program reached 251,790 infrequent voters across Mississippi by text and phone. We sent 77,424 pieces of direct mail.** And we helped turn out Black voters in unprecedented numbers.
But over 200,000 Mississippi voters were marked “inactive” ahead of the election, and many had to cast an affidavit ballot on Election Day. Others showed up at the wrong precinct because more than 100 polling places were changed or closed since 2024. Their ballots were set aside.
Much of this can be fixed through a process called curing. But the clock is ticking. Voters have until November 10 to fix their ballots. That means **there are only days left, and thousands of voters may not even know their vote is at risk.**
[**The deadline is Tuesday. There’s no time to waste. Will you chip in right now to help us reach Black voters in Mississippi before it’s too late?**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=everyvotecountedms26_ln.6aM6KH&refcode=em20261106-1728&t=4&akid=1728%2E2118727%2EkzTg7C)
**[DONATE $20 ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21584?c0=everyvotecountedms26_ln.la6Ans&refcode=em20261106-1728&t=5&akid=1728%2E2118727%2EkzTg7C)**
In the midterms, Color of Change reached more than 3 million Black voters and contacted nearly 400,000 unregistered voters. Black voters showed up in record numbers, even as the Trump administration spent two years attacking our rights and redrawing maps to dilute our power.
We voted anyway. Now we have to make sure every vote counts.
Until Justice Is Real,
Color Of Change

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**

Jason Crow is a veteran from a working class family, focused on lowering
costs, protecting democracy, and strengthening our national security. If

Hi friend, it's Congressman Jason Crow. By now, I'm sure you've
seen the good news: not only did we win Tuesday night, we secured a
majority in both chambers by a historic margin.

Here in Colorado, we elected incredible servant leaders at every level of
government. I could not be more excited to work alongside this all-star
team to make life easier for working families.

We've built our movement through hard work, grit, and grassroots energy.
Like with every campaign we've run, we've done it by refusing corporate
PAC money and taking on special interests.

To everyone who stepped up and supported our movement, thank you. This
victory is yours. Whether you chipped in, phonebanked, or knocked doors,
this grassroots win was made possible through your showing up. I cannot
thank you enough.

This begins a new direction for Colorado and our country. We're not going
back. We are building something new.

We're going to deliver a government that actually works for working
people, not just the elite. We're going to lower costs, protect
healthcare, end the Iran war, and stop corruption in Washington. You
deserve nothing less.

I am so grateful and so proud of this team. We have so much work left to
do, and I am ready to hit the ground running. It's an honor to serve you,
Colorado.

—Jason

ready to have you. The bigger our coalition, the better. Click here to
help turn this victory into change, together.

| | Friend,

We won. And before anything else, thank you, thank you, thank you!

On Tuesday, Wisconsin elected me your next Secretary of State, and I owe it to you.

For the first time in our state’s history, Wisconsin has elected a person of Latino descent to statewide office. I do not carry that lightly. I think of my mother, of the south side neighborhoods that raised me, and of every young Latina who will now grow up knowing this door is open.

But this campaign was never only about a first. It was about a promise that we would protect the right to vote and fight for the families who are too often left out. You believed in that promise. You knocked the doors, made the calls, chipped in what you could, and told your neighbors why this race mattered. That is how we won.
---
|
---
| And Wisconsin did not stop there. Wisconsin Democrats won a trifecta, the governor’s office and both houses of the Legislature. I will be proud to work alongside Governor-elect David Crowley, Lieutenant Governor-elect Sarah Godlewski, Attorney General Josh Kaul, Treasurer-elect Yee Leng Xiong, and our new Democratic majorities in Madison.

Now the real work begins, and I intend to honor your trust every single day. Thank you for standing with me. Thank you for believing. This victory is yours.
---
| With all my gratitude,

JoCasta Zamarripa
Secretary of State-elect of Wisconsin

name: Citizens Alliance New Hampshire
subject: Tough night on Tuesday...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Citizens Alliance of New Hampshire, Dan Gray, Treasurer, 45 Lafayette Rd
body:
Democrats now hold majorities in both chambers of the legislature, and the coming session will bring some major challenges...

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/KwE4C6WAQvR?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| | | | | | Peter,

Election night brought some difficult results for New Hampshire Republicans and the liberty-minded candidates we worked so hard to elect.

Of the 155 candidates we proudly endorsed this cycle, **51 of our Pledge Signers won their races** and will serve in the New Hampshire House of Representatives.

We congratulate each of them on their victories and thank everyone who stepped forward to defend the principles that make New Hampshire great!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/9jspJmuZ0xz?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
| [SUPPORT CITIZENS ALLIANCE OF NEW HAMPSHIRE’S LIBERTY CHAMPIONS TODAY >>>](https://us.list-manage.com/11EdvfiUi0Y?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70)
---
| | At the same time, we lost 104 races, including several hard-fought contests involving Republicans who have served New Hampshire well.

Democrats now hold majorities in both chambers of the legislature, and the coming session will bring some major challenges.

That is a painful result, and we will not pretend otherwise.

_**The good news?**_ Governor Kelly Ayotte remains in the Executive Office, and Republicans retain enough votes in the Senate to sustain her vetoes when necessary.

That means the worst is not inevitable. It means **our 51 Pledge Signers have an extremely important role to play.** They can advocate for lower taxes, stronger parental rights, responsible spending, transparent government, and legislation that keeps New Hampshire among the freest and most affordable states in the nation.

With these 51 champions, we still have voices in Concord who will fight for liberty-minded legislation that puts New Hampshire first. Our work to expand the roster of liberty advocates has only begun.

We are working to identify elected lawmakers to sign [The Pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/4FHX0c18Dml?e=8c8e704ee6&c2id=4e2c30752203ec2a90a0c0afb040bd70) and recruit them to join the fight.
---
|
---
| | The foundation we built this cycle remains strong.

**Together, we knocked on over 400,000 doors, sent over 250,000 text messages, and ran targeted digital advertising campaigns to support our Pledge Signers.**

Every ounce of that energy was spent empowering candidates who will stand for New Hampshire’s future.**

NEXT STEPS:

** We know what is at stake. We know the names of the Republicans who will serve, the votes they can influence, and the battles that lie ahead.

The road back to Republican control is long, but this election gave us an opportunity to build permanent infrastructure for future election cycles. We will use every door knocked, every message sent, every supporter earned, and every candidate relationship developed to build on this year's efforts.

We will keep fighting.

And we will keep New Hampshire the **Live Free or Die** state.

You have my word.

For New Hampshire,
---

**Reacting to a Sea Change 2026 Midterm Election** The Forward Party celebrated Election Day by watching election results as a team in Baltimore, MD on Tuesday. The next morning, Forward Party CEO Lindsey Williams Drath, Founding Co-Chair Christine Todd Whitman, and Executive Chair Kerry Healey sat down to share their reaction to the results. [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=c1vIqT8LaeJ1yAWpG61iLnR20Ou_nEKNMaOmzGS62KgjegtVcv4hCE2x5UuQCgooFUabIdUPsgWNtqkBhiPwhA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_129a&n=1) [Watch the full episode](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfaaohhN9l7zMwGsQDsAjfG1ihYlH27x1nxQRfaKtcztVjzoH1zL-xM0N49m0u_8X-I_XVAjoyzoqDLxD_RntjZ5&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_129a&n=2).**** **Other Thoughts on the 2026 Midterms** The results are mostly in, and while we at the Forward Party didn’t win many of our races, we’ve also have never been more certain that the Independent movement is making huge progress. Voters in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa sent a clear message about the direction of the country and the current administration, electing opposing-party leaders in places that seemed unwinnable for them just a few years ago. Voters weren’t voting for a party so much as they were voting in opposition to the dysfunction they’ve grown so tired of. That’s the voter Forward exists to serve. **Something is happening in the Mountain West** In Montana, South Dakota, Idaho, and Nebraska, Republicans won, but an independent, not a Democrat, finished second. Nearly every one of our federal candidates cleared 30% of the vote, which is no small feat running outside of the two-party system. And compared with the last Democrat to run in each state, independents did markedly better this cycle. **Senate Candidates Brian Bengs and Todd Achilles Outperform Previous Outings** In South Dakota, Brian Bengs earned 39.5% as an independent, up from 26.1% when he ran as a Democrat in 2022, and in his home county of Fall River, he went from 18% to 32%. In Idaho, Todd Achilles earned 33.6%, up from 28.7% for the 2022 Democratic nominee. The trend is unmistakable. In some of the reddest states in the country, independents are now a real alternative. **So What Comes Next?** We’ve had our eyes on 2028 since day one, and today we have more candidates, more data, more state infrastructure and more proof than ever that independents can compete. The question is no longer whether independent voters matter, but whether our political system will catch up to them. We hope you’ll continue on this journey with us and we thank you for being a supporter of our work and the ever growing Independent political movement.

Sullivan. As you read this, just 637 votes separates the top vote-getter
in Alaska’s Senate race.

Fellow Patriot,

We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy.

The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded.

**At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong.**

We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation.

I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down.

I know you won't either!

I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation.

clean_body: Fellow Patriot, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

We could not have won without you

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/e45687cf8a9c/the-next-56-days-matter-70874?e=561a28864e)

| |

Friends,I am honored to have earned your support this election season, and I want to start by saying thank you. Our win would not have happened without you.
Every one of you played a part in this. Some of you signed my nomination papers back at the very beginning. Others put up yard signs, chipped in a donation, or talked to a neighbor. And so many of you showed up to vote. However you helped, it mattered, and I do not take any of it for granted.
I also know this was a hard week. A lot of good people we stood alongside came up short, and that is tough to see.
But I don’t see this as an ending. I see it as a starting point. The things we care about didn’t change on Tuesday, and neither did the people who care about them. The next two years are going to take real work: showing up for our communities, listening to the folks we did not reach this time, and building something stronger for the next election. That work starts now, not a year from now.
I’m going back to Washington ready to champion the priorities you sent me there to fight for, and I’m going to need you with me along the way. Stay in touch, keep talking to your neighbors, and keep showing up. We will be reaching out soon about how we can keep this momentum going together.
Thank you for everything you did this year. I’m grateful to have you with me, and I will keep working hard for you.
Scott Fitzgerald

name: Shawnna Bolick
subject: The Election Is Over
